issue.title: fix(responses): keep the namespace == name shape for deferred top-level tools
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

`<make-me-human-readable>`
Agents built with the OpenAI Agents SDK can now use deferred tools with Claude's tool search through the Responses endpoint. Before, the agent crashed right after Claude found the tool, because the reply did not mark that tool the way the SDK expects.
`</make-me-human-readable>`

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Agents SDK runs crash after Claude's tool search finds a deferred tool
- The bridge omits the `namespace == name` mark the SDK needs
- A client workaround sends `name__name` to the provider instead

How it solves it:

- Deferred top-level tools come back with `namespace` equal to `name`
- Streaming and non-streaming replies both carry it
- Replayed calls with that mark keep the bare tool name
- Other namespaces are still joined, as before

## User Flow

Before: an Agents SDK app on Claude crashes after its first tool search

1. The app sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses with 6 function tools marked `defer_loading: true` and `{"type": "tool_search"}`, model `claude-opus-5` (Bedrock Invoke)
2. The reply holds a `tool_search_call`, then a `function_call` named `get_reporting_categories` with no `namespace`
3. The SDK stops: `ModelBehaviorError: Tool get_reporting_categories not found in agent ia`

After: the same app finishes the turn

1. The app sends the same POST
2. The `function_call` now carries `"namespace": "get_reporting_categories"`
3. The SDK runs the tool and sends its output back; the call reaches Bedrock named `get_reporting_categories`, and Claude answers

## Relevant issues

Part of #50104 (item 1).

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup: Agents SDK 0.24.0, `OpenAIResponsesModel` pointed at the proxy's `/v1/responses`, 6 deferred function tools plus `ToolSearchTool()`, no client-side namespace handling, two user turns. Proxy config as in #50104, with a callback that records each request body sent to Bedrock.

### Before (fd4cef22)

1. Run the agent. It stops after the first model call: `ModelBehaviorError: Tool get_reporting_categories not found in agent ia`. Same on v1.108.0 and v1.109.0rc1. This step ran against a local Bedrock stub

### After (tested on a build of this PR plus the other two PRs for #50104)

1. Run the same agent, live: 4 Bedrock calls, both user turns answered
2. Every `tool_use` in the recorded Bedrock request bodies is named `get_reporting_categories`

Focused checks on this PR's tip:

- New tests: `test_transform_chat_completion_response_deferred_top_level_tool_call_has_namespace_equal_to_name`, `test_function_call_echo_with_namespace_equal_to_name_keeps_bare_name`, `test_function_call_echo_from_namespace_with_member_of_same_name_keeps_qualified_name`, `test_deferred_top_level_name_shared_with_self_named_namespace_member_stays_qualified`. Each fails with the source change reverted.
- The existing `test_claude_count_request_drops_a_malformed_tool_flag_under_drop_params_like_inference` guards the lookup: it reads `defer_loading is True` and does not raise, because token counting under `drop_params` only reads the input.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/responses/ tests/unit/llms/bedrock/messages/`: 2151 passed. The only failures are `test_reasoning_effort_grid_wire_shapes[*-vertex-ai]` (needs the Google Cloud SDK) and `test_every_openai_sdk_response_error_code_has_explicit_status_mapping`; both fail the same way on `main`.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- A deferred top-level `search` beside a namespace `search` holding `search` stays ambiguous
  - The top-level call comes back without a namespace, as on `main`
  - The SDK cannot route `namespace == name` for a namespace member either
- The tool search replay PR for #50104 edits the same file; whichever merges second may need a rebase
- The live After ran on a build with this PR and its two sibling PRs; a live run on this tip alone will follow in a comment

## Final Attestation

- [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes tool name/namespace mapping on the Responses bridge, which affects multi-turn Agents SDK + deferred tool flows; scope is limited to defer_loading top-level tools with explicit collision handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Responses ↔ chat-completion bridging for **deferred top-level tools** (`defer_loading: true`) used with the OpenAI Agents SDK and native tool search.
> 
> **Outbound (Responses → provider):** Adds `deferred_top_level_names()` and threads it through input conversion. When a replayed `function_call` has `namespace == name` for one of those tools, the chat `tool_call` keeps the **bare** name instead of `name__name`.
> 
> **Inbound (provider → Responses):** Extends `namespace_tool_name_map()` so those same tools are restored with **`namespace` equal to `name`**, which the Agents SDK needs to resolve the tool after search.
> 
> Ambiguous cases (e.g. a namespace and a deferred top-level tool both named `search` with a member `search`) still use qualified names; new unit tests cover the happy path and edge cases.
>

issue.title: feat(changelog): add ?digest= and ?models= feed views and a subscribe builder on the changelog page
issue.body:
## Summary

The #shipped Slack channel subscribes to `/changelog.xml` through Slack's RSS app, and today's registry audit commit produced 13 separate items, each titled by one model and each ending in a truncated list of raw `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/...` ids. `/changelog.xml?digest=commit` now folds everything one litellm catalog commit changed into a single item, and `?digest=1h` (`30m`, `4h`, `1d`) folds everything that landed in one clock-aligned window, so the channel gets one post per commit or per hour that reads like a release note.

For commit c319616 the digest item is

```
8 models added, 8 updated on 4 providers
• DeepSeek Flash Latest added on Fireworks AI
• GLM Fast Latest added on Fireworks AI
• ...
• Claude Mythos 5.1 on Azure AI Foundry: Web search price added: $0.01 / query, Web search enabled
• +7 more
```

The title counts the models added and updated (a new provider's bullet counts all of its models) and names their providers (or says `N providers` past three). The body has one bullet per model, regional aliases with the same name collapsed to one with their note written once, the notes of a model's price and capability items joined onto its one bullet, and it stops before Slack's 500-character cut (`DIGEST_BODY_LIMIT` 480) with a `+N more` line. A commit with one model yields that model's bullet as the title.

Per commit, the guid is `digest:<sha>` and the link stays the GitHub commit. Per window, the guid is `digest:1h:<window start ISO>`, the `pubDate` is the window's end, and the link is the commit when the window holds one and the changelog page (with the feed's utm tags) when it holds several. A window counts as closed once the changelog's `generatedAt` is past its end, not the wall clock, so a reader that posts an item the first time it sees its guid never posts an hour the next 10-minute build would still add a commit to. With the 5-minute CDN cache on the function, a window shows up 10 to 25 minutes after it closes.

### Following only the models a proxy runs

`?models=azure/gpt-5,claude-opus-4-5` narrows the feed to those models, next to `?kind=` and `?providers=`. Each value is compared by `modelKey`, the slug of its last path segment, and a listing matches on the key of its catalog id, the slug of the whole id, or the slug of its display name, so `azure/gpt-5`, `openai/gpt-5`, `gpt-5` and `GPT-5` all follow the catalog's `gpt-5`, and a proxy's `model:` strings work as they are. A multi-model addition is cut down to the matching listings and its headline recounted, and a new provider narrowed this way becomes a `model` item (`Alpha added on Newco`) rather than claiming the provider arrived with two models.

The `/changelog` page gets a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel (a `<details>` above the filters) that combines all four dimensions: the cadence (`DIGEST_OPTIONS`: every change, per commit, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d), change-type checkboxes, a provider picker with chips, and a textarea for the proxy's models. `parseModelList` takes the JSON of `/model/info` (`litellm_params.model`, falling back to `model_name`) or `/v1/models` (`id`), a `config.yaml` (its `model:` lines), or ids separated by commas, spaces or newlines, and the panel says how many of them changed in the last 30 days. `feedUrl(filter)` renders the URL with `/`, `:` and `@` kept readable, and the panel offers Copy URL and Copy Slack command (`/feed subscribe <url>`). Opening `/changelog?models=...&digest=1h` (any feed parameter) opens the panel prefilled, so a proxy's admin UI can link straight to a feed for its model list.

```ts
// src/changelogPresentation.ts
interface FeedFilter { kinds; providers; models; digest }
feedFilter(params)            // reads ?kind= ?providers= ?models= ?digest=
feedUrl(filter)               // https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?kind=price&models=azure/gpt-5,o3&digest=1h
parseModelList(text)          // ["azure/gpt-5", "vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929"]
filterChangelogItems(items, filter)  // kind, provider, then models (entries narrowed)

// api/changelog.ts
const entries = filter.digest
  ? digestFeedEntries(items, filter.digest, Date.parse(data.generatedAt))
  : items.map(feedEntry);
```

Filters apply before the digest, so `?digest=1h&kind=price&models=gpt-5` folds only GPT-5 price changes. An unknown `digest=` value falls back to the per-change feed. The default feed is unchanged, so existing readers keep their items and guids.

`changelogRss` now takes `FeedEntry[]` (id, link, timestamp, category, title, body) instead of `ChangelogItem[]`, with `feedEntry()` producing today's per-change item. `FeedFilter.digest` is the validated `digest=` token (`""`, `"commit"` or a span). `ChangelogItem` carries `providerName` so the digest can name providers without recomputing them. Two capability flags that fell through to the generic label are named now, so `Supports web search enabled` reads `Web search enabled`, and `supports_tool_choice` reads `Tool choice`.

Tracking: `middleware.ts` adds `digest`, and `models` next to `kind` and `providers`, to the Feed Fetched event when the query asks for them. The panel sends `Changelog Feed Builder Opened`, `Changelog Feed Builder Changed` (digest) and `Changelog Feed Copied` (what, digest, kind, providers, model count), never the pasted text.

To switch the channel over, unsubscribe the current feed and run `/feed subscribe https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?digest=1h` (or `digest=commit`), or build the URL on `/changelog`. Switching the default feed's shape instead would give every existing subscriber a flood of re-posted items, since the guids change.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Default `/changelog.xml` behavior is unchanged; new query params and UI are additive, with broad test coverage on feed shaping and filtering.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends `/changelog.xml` with **`?digest=`** (`commit`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d`) so Slack/RSS readers get one summarized item per catalog commit or clock window (bullets per model, Slack-length cap, open windows held until the build closes them), and **`?models=`** to narrow updates to specific catalog or proxy model ids (matched on last path segment).
> 
> The changelog page adds a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel: digest cadence, change types, providers, pasted proxy JSON/YAML/model lists via `parseModelList`, generated `feedUrl`, and copy-to-Slack support; query params prefill the panel. `changelogPresentation` gains `FeedEntry`, `digestFeedEntries`, model filtering, and `changelogRss` now renders entries instead of raw items; `api/changelog` and middleware apply the new filters and track `digest`/`models`. README documents the feed options; tests cover digest, model filter, and the UI builder.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 468a3428ec22b995e2bdd8dc9b329a785a7e0463. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

issue.title: fix(proxy): keep the upgrade notice off the request path and count area-labelled release notes
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

handle edge cases for version upgrade UI banner

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Upgrade notice says "0 new features, 0 fixes, and 0 other updates"
- Patch notes written as `- **Area:** Fixed ...` were never counted
- First dashboard request waited up to 5 seconds on an airgapped proxy

How it solves it:

- Counts `- **Area:** Added/Fixed/...` bullets next to the old `* fix(x):` ones
- Endpoint responds 502 once the fetch has failed (changelog or GitHub unreachable, or an unusable answer), and the bell shows nothing
- A release whose notes have nothing countable is announced with its version and link, without the counts
- Endpoint answers from the cache and fetches after the response is sent

Intentional product change: the first `GET /get/latest_release_info` after a proxy start, or after the one hour cache expires, now returns `null` and the next call returns the release. The dashboard keeps an answer for an hour, so the notice shows up on the next page load instead of the first one.

## User Flow

Before: an admin on an older proxy opens the bell and reads a count that is wrong, and on an airgapped proxy the request hangs first

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the page sends GET https://litellm-domain/get/latest_release_info
2. On a proxy whose firewall drops outbound packets, that request stays open for 5 seconds before returning `null`
3. With egress, it returns v1.108.4 with 162 new features, 511 fixes and 178 other updates, missing every change in v1.108.2 to v1.108.4
4. For a release whose notes are all in the new format, the bell reads "0 new features, 0 fixes, and 0 other updates"

After: the request returns right away, the counts include the new format, and a release with no countable notes is announced without counts

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the page sends GET https://litellm-domain/get/latest_release_info
2. On the airgapped proxy it returns `null` in about 50 ms, the proxy logs one warning 5 seconds later, and later calls respond 502 for the 5 minutes the failure is cached. The bell shows no upgrade notice and no error
3. With egress, the first call returns `null`, and the next returns v1.108.4 with 162 new features, 532 fixes and 180 other updates
4. For a release with no countable notes, the bell reads "v1.110.0 is available. Your current version is v1.109.0" with no counts

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, run once at each commit, with no database and no Redis because this endpoint only uses a per-process in-memory cache. `--detailed_debug` is off because one case measures latency.

```bash
# cfg.yaml
model_list: []

export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-<random hex>
env -u DATABASE_URL python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config cfg.yaml --port 4001   # 4002 for the After leg

call() { curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -w ' status=%{http_code} seconds=%{time_total}\n' localhost:$1/get/latest_release_info; }
```

For the airgapped case, `10.255.255.1 docs.litellm.ai` was added to `/etc/hosts` before the proxy started, so connections to the changelog hang until the 5 second timeout. The line was removed and both proxies restarted for the counts case, which read the real changelog feed and the real GitHub releases.

### Before (1d5e0c4be5)

#### Changelog unreachable

1. `call 4001` three times
```
null status=200 seconds=5.230930
null status=200 seconds=0.006274
null status=200 seconds=0.005349
```

#### Counts for v1.108.4

1. `call 4001`, wait 4 seconds, `call 4001`
```
{"version":"1.108.4","new_features":162,"bug_fixes":511,"other_updates":178,"release_url":"https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/v1.108.4/v1-108-4"} status=200 seconds=0.539235
{"version":"1.108.4","new_features":162,"bug_fixes":511,"other_updates":178,"release_url":"https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/v1.108.4/v1-108-4"} status=200 seconds=0.010241
```

### After (851fe34425, changelog unreachable rerun at 7f0c5d10ef)

#### Changelog unreachable

1. `call 4002` twice, wait 6 seconds, `call 4002` twice
```
null status=200 seconds=0.056112
null status=200 seconds=0.010260
{"detail":"Latest release info unavailable: ConnectTimeout: Connection timeout to host https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/rss.xml"} status=502 seconds=0.006491
{"detail":"Latest release info unavailable: ConnectTimeout: Connection timeout to host https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/rss.xml"} status=502 seconds=0.006288
```
2. The proxy log has one warning, 5 seconds after the first call
```
LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: latest_release_endpoints.py:237 - LiteLLM: latest release info unavailable: ConnectTimeout: Connection timeout to host https://docs.litellm.ai/release_notes/rss.xml
```

#### Counts for v1.108.4

1. `call 4002`, wait 4 seconds, `call 4002`
```
null status=200 seconds=0.109739
```

issue.title: feat(changelog): add ?digest= and ?models= feed views and a subscribe builder on the changelog page
issue.body:
## Summary

The #shipped Slack channel subscribes to `/changelog.xml` through Slack's RSS app, and today's registry audit commit produced 13 separate items, each titled by one model and each ending in a truncated list of raw `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/...` ids. `/changelog.xml?digest=commit` now folds everything one litellm catalog commit changed into a single item, and `?digest=1h` (`30m`, `4h`, `1d`) folds everything that landed in one clock-aligned window, so the channel gets one post per commit or per hour that reads like a release note.

For commit c319616 the digest item is

```
8 models added, 8 updated on 4 providers
• DeepSeek Flash Latest added on Fireworks AI
• GLM Fast Latest added on Fireworks AI
• ...
• Claude Mythos 5.1 on Azure AI Foundry: Web search price added: $0.01 / query, Web search enabled
• +7 more
```

The title counts the models added and updated (a new provider's bullet counts all of its models) and names their providers (or says `N providers` past three). The body has one bullet per model, regional aliases with the same name collapsed to one with their note written once, the notes of a model's price and capability items joined onto its one bullet, and it stops before Slack's 500-character cut (`DIGEST_BODY_LIMIT` 480) with a `+N more` line. A commit with one model yields that model's bullet as the title.

Per commit, the guid is `digest:<sha>` and the link stays the GitHub commit. Per window, the guid is `digest:1h:<window start ISO>`, the `pubDate` is the window's end, and the link is the commit when the window holds one and the changelog page (with the feed's utm tags) when it holds several. A window counts as closed once the changelog's `generatedAt` is past its end, not the wall clock, so a reader that posts an item the first time it sees its guid never posts an hour the next 10-minute build would still add a commit to. With the 5-minute CDN cache on the function, a window shows up 10 to 25 minutes after it closes.

### Following only the models a proxy runs

`?models=azure/gpt-5,claude-opus-4-5` narrows the feed to those models, next to `?kind=` and `?providers=`. Each value is compared by `modelKey`, the slug of its last path segment, and a listing matches on the key of its catalog id, the slug of the whole id, or the slug of its display name, so `azure/gpt-5`, `openai/gpt-5`, `gpt-5` and `GPT-5` all follow the catalog's `gpt-5`, and a proxy's `model:` strings work as they are. A multi-model addition is cut down to the matching listings and its headline recounted, and a new provider narrowed this way becomes a `model` item (`Alpha added on Newco`) rather than claiming the provider arrived with two models.

The `/changelog` page gets a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel (a `<details>` above the filters) that combines all four dimensions: the cadence (`DIGEST_OPTIONS`: every change, per commit, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d), change-type checkboxes, a provider picker with chips, and a textarea for the proxy's models. `parseModelList` takes the JSON of `/model/info` (`litellm_params.model`, falling back to `model_name`) or `/v1/models` (`id`), a `config.yaml` (its `model:` lines), or ids separated by commas, spaces or newlines, and the panel says how many of them changed in the last 30 days. `feedUrl(filter)` renders the URL with `/`, `:` and `@` kept readable, and the panel offers Copy URL and Copy Slack command (`/feed subscribe <url>`). Opening `/changelog?models=...&digest=1h` (any feed parameter) opens the panel prefilled, so a proxy's admin UI can link straight to a feed for its model list.

```ts
// src/changelogPresentation.ts
interface FeedFilter { kinds; providers; models; digest }
feedFilter(params)            // reads ?kind= ?providers= ?models= ?digest=
feedUrl(filter)               // https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?kind=price&models=azure/gpt-5,o3&digest=1h
parseModelList(text)          // ["azure/gpt-5", "vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929"]
filterChangelogItems(items, filter)  // kind, provider, then models (entries narrowed)

// api/changelog.ts
const entries = filter.digest
  ? digestFeedEntries(items, filter.digest, Date.parse(data.generatedAt))
  : items.map(feedEntry);
```

Filters apply before the digest, so `?digest=1h&kind=price&models=gpt-5` folds only GPT-5 price changes. An unknown `digest=` value falls back to the per-change feed. The default feed is unchanged, so existing readers keep their items and guids.

`changelogRss` now takes `FeedEntry[]` (id, link, timestamp, category, title, body) instead of `ChangelogItem[]`, with `feedEntry()` producing today's per-change item. `FeedFilter.digest` is the validated `digest=` token (`""`, `"commit"` or a span). `ChangelogItem` carries `providerName` so the digest can name providers without recomputing them. Two capability flags that fell through to the generic label are named now, so `Supports web search enabled` reads `Web search enabled`, and `supports_tool_choice` reads `Tool choice`.

Tracking: `middleware.ts` adds `digest`, and `models` next to `kind` and `providers`, to the Feed Fetched event when the query asks for them. The panel sends `Changelog Feed Builder Opened`, `Changelog Feed Builder Changed` (digest) and `Changelog Feed Copied` (what, digest, kind, providers, model count), never the pasted text.

To switch the channel over, unsubscribe the current feed and run `/feed subscribe https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?digest=1h` (or `digest=commit`), or build the URL on `/changelog`. Switching the default feed's shape instead would give every existing subscriber a flood of re-posted items, since the guids change.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Default `/changelog.xml` behavior is unchanged; new query params and UI are additive, with broad test coverage on feed shaping and filtering.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends `/changelog.xml` with **`?digest=`** (`commit`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d`) so Slack/RSS readers get one summarized item per catalog commit or clock window (bullets per model, Slack-length cap, open windows held until the build closes them), and **`?models=`** to narrow updates to specific catalog or proxy model ids (matched on last path segment).
> 
> The changelog page adds a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel: digest cadence, change types, providers, pasted proxy JSON/YAML/model lists via `parseModelList`, generated `feedUrl`, and copy-to-Slack support; query params prefill the panel. `changelogPresentation` gains `FeedEntry`, `digestFeedEntries`, model filtering, and `changelogRss` now renders entries instead of raw items; `api/changelog` and middleware apply the new filters and track `digest`/`models`. README documents the feed options; tests cover digest, model filter, and the UI builder.
>

issue.title: fix(router): re-check and reserve per-model rate limits on fallback targets
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

enforce model_rpm_limit and model_tpm_limit on retries and fallbacks

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Per-model TPM/RPM limits are checked once, on the requested model only
- A provider error fallback hands the caller the fallback model unchecked
- The caller can pass a per-model limit of 1 on the fallback model forever

How it solves it:

- New router hook `fallback_rate_limit_check`, next to `fallback_budget_check`
- The proxy wires it to the v3 limiter, which reserves the target model's per-model descriptors
- A fallback target over its per-model limit is skipped, and the error says so
- Same-model retries keep the admission reservation, so no double counting

## User Flow

Before: the caller's per-model limit on the fallback model is never checked when a provider failure triggers the fallback.

1. The admin gives a key `metadata.model_rpm_limit = {"luna": 1}` and configures `fallbacks: [{"opus": ["luna"]}]`
2. The caller sends three `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: opus` while the opus provider is down
3. All three return 200 served by luna, three times the caller's luna allowance

After: the second and later fallbacks into luna are refused.

1. Same key and config
2. The first call falls back to luna and returns 200
3. The second and third calls return the opus provider error with "Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it"

## Relevant issues

Pylon #11530 reported the same gap for key level per-model limits (LIT-10512).

The router settings reference row for `fallback_rate_limit_check` is https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/2909, which the `docs` CI job here needs merged first.

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10554
Resolves LIT-10512

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, two workers sharing one Redis, run from the repo root with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL` exported:

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa/config.yaml --port 4016 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>qa/config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key

      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY

    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

<summary>leg.sh, the client script (run as `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... ./leg.sh 4016`)</summary>

```bash
echo "## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "## call $i to opus"

done
echo "## redis counters for the key on luna"
redis-cli --scan --pattern "*model_per_key*luna*" | while read k; do echo "$k = $(redis-cli get "$k" 2>/dev/null)"; done
```

2. Observed:

```
## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna
## call 1 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 2 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 3 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## redis counters for the key on luna
{model_per_key:8a0e57bd...:luna}:tokens = 90
```

2. Observed:

```
## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna
## call 1 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 2 to opus

{"message": "litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'opus' failed with the error above. Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it.", "type": "internal_server_error", "param": null, "c
## call 3 to opus
HTTP 500
{"message": "litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'opus' failed with the error above. Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it.", "type": "internal_server_error", "param": null, "c

{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:tokens = 30
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:requests = 2
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:window = 1794348026
```

A caller-supplied chain with a repeated target (`fallbacks: ["B", "B"]`) reserves B once. Both walks now consult the attempted set before the reserving check, covered by `test_run_async_fallback_reserves_a_repeated_target_once`.

`tests/integration/routing/test_fallback_rate_limit_check.py` boots the proxy with two workers and two scripted upstreams (primary always 500, fallback healthy) and asserts the second fallback is refused. 🐛 Bug Fix

- A provider error fallback hands the caller the fallback model unchecked

- New router hook `fallback_rate_limit_check`, next to `fallback_budget_check`

issue.title: fix(cost-map): give the Gemini 4 Carbon rows the shared Gemini 3 search free tier
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

title

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Grounded Gemini 4 Carbon calls bill $0.014 per query from the first query
- Google gives Gemini 3 and newer 5,000 free grounding queries a month, shared
- `gemini/gemini-4-carbon` and both Vertex Carbon rows had no `search_free_requests`

How it solves it:

- Adds `{"count": 5000, "period": "month", "shared_group": "gemini-3"}` to the three Carbon rows
- Same allowance every Gemini 3.x grounding row already carries, in both catalog copies
- Regression test fails if any Carbon row drops or diverges from the Gemini 3 allowance

Follow-up to #50931 and #50942, where Cursor Bugbot flagged the missing allowance.

## User Flow

Before: a team on a proxy with the search free tier on pays for every grounded Carbon query

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gemini/gemini-4-carbon"` and the `googleSearch` tool
2. The response comes back grounded and the request lands in https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs with $0.014 of search spend on top of tokens
3. The same request on `gemini/gemini-3.8-flash` lands at token cost only, because it draws on the shared monthly allowance

After: the Carbon request draws on the same shared allowance as the Gemini 3 models

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "gemini/gemini-4-carbon"` and the `googleSearch` tool
2. The request lands in https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs at token cost only until the shared 5,000 queries for the month are used up
3. Query 5,001 across all Gemini 3 and newer models that month is the first one billed at $0.014

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

E2E exception at 670abef5ed. Data-only cost-map change, three rows gain one field that every Gemini 3.x grounding row already carries, so the search free tier hook reads it the same way it reads the Gemini 3 rows and no code path changes. Gemini 4 Carbon is early access and not callable from our Google project, so a live grounded call was not possible.

Sources, read on 2026-11-10 from the raw pages. The Gemini API pricing page says "5,000 free search requests per month (shared across all Gemini 3 and newer models)". The Vertex pricing page says "Includes 5,000 Grounding Queries per month at no charge, aggregated across all Gemini 3 and Gemini 4 models".

Focused checks at the tip

```
LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True uv run --no-sync pytest tests/unit/test_model_prices_and_context_window.py -q -k "search_free or carbon or synchronized"
5 passed, 97 deselected
```

Mutation check. Removing `search_free_requests` from `vertex_ai/gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive` in the main catalog makes `test_gemini_4_carbon_rows_share_the_gemini_3_search_allowance_in_both_cost_map_copies` fail on `assert carbon_rows <= main_rows.keys()`. Restoring the row makes it pass again.

Runtime check after `uv sync --reinstall-package litellm` (the native extension bakes the map in at build time)

```
uv run --no-sync python -c "import litellm; print({m: litellm.model_cost[m]['search_free_requests'] for m in ('gemini/gemini-4-carbon', 'vertex_ai/gemini-4-carbon', 'vertex_ai/gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive', 'vertex_ai/gemini-3.8-flash')})"
```

all four rows print `{'count': 5000, 'period': 'month', 'shared_group': 'gemini-3'}`.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- The three Gemini 4 Argon rows have the same gap and are not touched here

### Low

- Carbon promo token prices stay as merged, the cost map has no date-aware pricing

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

issue.title: fix(proxy): keep the upgrade notice off the request path and count area-labelled release notes
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

handle edge cases for version upgrade UI banner

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Upgrade notice says "0 new features, 0 fixes, and 0 other updates"
- Patch notes written as `- **Area:** Fixed ...` were never counted
- First dashboard request waited up to 5 seconds on an airgapped proxy

How it solves it:

- Counts `- **Area:** Added/Fixed/...` bullets next to the old `* fix(x):` ones
- Endpoint responds 502 once the fetch has failed (changelog or GitHub unreachable, or an unusable answer), and the bell shows nothing
- A release whose notes have nothing countable is announced with its version and link, without the counts
- Endpoint answers from the cache and fetches after the response is sent

Intentional product change: the first `GET /get/latest_release_info` after a proxy start, or after the one hour cache expires, now returns `null` and the next call returns the release. The dashboard keeps an answer for an hour, so the notice shows up on the next page load instead of the first one.

## User Flow

Before: an admin on an older proxy opens the bell and reads a count that is wrong, and on an airgapped proxy the request hangs first

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the page sends GET https://litellm-domain/get/latest_release_info
2. On a proxy whose firewall drops outbound packets, that request stays open for 5 seconds before returning `null`
3. With egress, it returns v1.108.4 with 162 new features, 511 fixes and 178 other updates, missing every change in v1.108.2 to v1.108.4
4. For a release whose notes are all in the new format, the bell reads "0 new features, 0 fixes, and 0 other updates"

After: the request returns right away, the counts include the new format, and a release with no countable notes is announced without counts

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the page sends GET https://litellm-domain/get/latest_release_info
2. On the airgapped proxy it returns `null` in about 50 ms, the proxy logs one warning 5 seconds later, and later calls respond 502 for the 5 minutes the failure is cached. The bell shows no upgrade notice and no error
3. With egress, the first call returns `null`, and the next returns v1.108.4 with 162 new features, 532 fixes and 180 other updates
4. For a release with no countable notes, the bell reads "v1.110.0 is available. Your current version is v1.109.0" with no counts

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, run once at each commit, with no database and no Redis because this endpoint only uses a per-process in-memory cache. `--detailed_debug` is off because one case measures latency.

```bash
# cfg.yaml
model_list: []

export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-<random hex>
env -u DATABASE_URL python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config cfg.yaml --port 4001   # 4002 for the After leg

call() { curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -w ' status=%{http_code} seconds=%{time_total}\n' localhost:$1/get/latest_release_info; }
```

For the airgapped case, `10.255.255.1 docs.litellm.ai` was added to `/etc/hosts` before the proxy started, so connections to the changelog hang until the 5 second timeout. The line was removed and both proxies restarted for the counts case, which read the real changelog feed and the real GitHub releases.

### Before (1d5e0c4be5)

#### Changelog unreachable

1. `call 4001` three times
```
null status=200 seconds=5.230930
null status=200 seconds=0.006274
null status=200 seconds=0.005349
```

issue.title: fix(proxy): keep the upgrade notice off the request path and count area-labelled release notes
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

handle edge cases for version upgrade UI banner

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Upgrade notice says "0 new features, 0 fixes, and 0 other updates"
- Patch notes written as `- **Area:** Fixed ...` were never counted
- First dashboard request waited up to 5 seconds on an airgapped proxy

How it solves it:

- Counts `- **Area:** Added/Fixed/...` bullets next to the old `* fix(x):` ones
- Endpoint responds 502 once the fetch has failed (changelog or GitHub unreachable, or an unusable answer), and the bell shows nothing
- A release whose notes have nothing countable is announced with its version and link, without the counts
- Endpoint answers from the cache and fetches after the response is sent

Intentional product change: the first `GET /get/latest_release_info` after a proxy start, or after the one hour cache expires, now returns `null` and the next call returns the release. The dashboard keeps an answer for an hour, so the notice shows up on the next page load instead of the first one.

## User Flow

Before: an admin on an older proxy opens the bell and reads a count that is wrong, and on an airgapped proxy the request hangs first

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the page sends GET https://litellm-domain/get/latest_release_info
2. On a proxy whose firewall drops outbound packets, that request stays open for 5 seconds before returning `null`
3. With egress, it returns v1.108.4 with 162 new features, 511 fixes and 178 other updates, missing every change in v1.108.2 to v1.108.4
4. For a release whose notes are all in the new format, the bell reads "0 new features, 0 fixes, and 0 other updates"

After: the request returns right away, the counts include the new format, and a release with no countable notes is announced without counts

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/ and the page sends GET https://litellm-domain/get/latest_release_info
2. On the airgapped proxy it returns `null` in about 50 ms, the proxy logs one warning 5 seconds later, and later calls respond 502 for the 5 minutes the failure is cached. The bell shows no upgrade notice and no error
3. With egress, the first call returns `null`, and the next returns v1.108.4 with 162 new features, 532 fixes and 180 other updates
4. For a release with no countable notes, the bell reads "v1.110.0 is available. Your current version is v1.109.0" with no counts

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, run once at each commit, with no database and no Redis because this endpoint only uses a per-process in-memory cache. `--detailed_debug` is off because one case measures latency.

```bash
# cfg.yaml
model_list: []

export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-<random hex>
env -u DATABASE_URL python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config cfg.yaml --port 4001   # 4002 for the After leg

call() { curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -w ' status=%{http_code} seconds=%{time_total}\n' localhost:$1/get/latest_release_info; }
```

For the airgapped case, `10.255.255.1 docs.litellm.ai` was added to `/etc/hosts` before the proxy started, so connections to the changelog hang until the 5 second timeout. issue.title: chore(cost-map): add fal_ai image and video rows priced from the fal.ai model pages (first fal-ai sync)
issue.body:
First fal-ai sync. The fal-ai lane is list-only, so every id below is priced from its own fal.ai model page `https://fal.ai/models/<id>/llms.txt` (fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-10), kind page, with `source` set to `https://fal.ai/models/<id>`. The unit on each page was cross-checked against `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing?endpoint_id=<id>` (which returns one base price per endpoint and the billing unit); the page wins when they differ, and the API's base price is the lowest tier for tiered endpoints.

Of the 1078 new ids in the diff, 612 get a row here (601 plus the 11 promotional rows below): 197 billed per image (`output_cost_per_image`), 189 billed per megapixel (`output_cost_per_image` at the 1 MP default plus `output_cost_per_pixel` = price / 1048576, the shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux/dev`), 113 billed at one rate per second of generated video (`output_cost_per_second`), and 102 billed per second with resolution tiers (`output_cost_per_second_<480p|720p|768p|1080p|2k|4k>`, the shape of `fal_ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video`, with `output_cost_per_second` set to the page's default `resolution` tier, or the highest tier when the page's default is auto or unstated, as noted in each row's metadata). Tiers the catalog has no field for (360p, 540p, 580p, 1440p, 2160p) are named in the row's metadata comment and left unpriced. 5 existing fal_ai rows are updated because their page price differs from the catalog (listed under Changed). Mode is `image_generation` for text-to-image and image-to-image ids and `video_generation` for the video ids; `supported_endpoints`, `supported_modalities` and `supports_vision` follow the existing fal_ai siblings for the same category.

392 ids are left out because fal bills them in a unit the catalog has no field for, and 82 ids are left out because the page states a conditional or compound price (per clip, audio on/off, promotional, first-megapixel-plus-extra, per layer, and so on); both groups are listed at the bottom with their unit so Kerry can rule on them. ### New rows (row-by-row evidence with the quoted page sentence is posted as the first comments on this PR, the body limit does not fit 583 rows)

- New rows billed per megapixel: 189 rows, evidence in the PR comments

issue.title: chore(cost-map): add fal_ai image and video rows priced from the fal.ai model pages (first fal-ai sync)
issue.body:
First fal-ai sync. The fal-ai lane is list-only, so every id below is priced from its own fal.ai model page `https://fal.ai/models/<id>/llms.txt` (fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-10), kind page, with `source` set to `https://fal.ai/models/<id>`. The unit on each page was cross-checked against `https://api.fal.ai/v1/models/pricing?endpoint_id=<id>` (which returns one base price per endpoint and the billing unit); the page wins when they differ, and the API's base price is the lowest tier for tiered endpoints.

Of the 1078 new ids in the diff, 612 get a row here (601 plus the 11 promotional rows below): 197 billed per image (`output_cost_per_image`), 189 billed per megapixel (`output_cost_per_image` at the 1 MP default plus `output_cost_per_pixel` = price / 1048576, the shape of `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux/dev`), 113 billed at one rate per second of generated video (`output_cost_per_second`), and 102 billed per second with resolution tiers (`output_cost_per_second_<480p|720p|768p|1080p|2k|4k>`, the shape of `fal_ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video`, with `output_cost_per_second` set to the page's default `resolution` tier, or the highest tier when the page's default is auto or unstated, as noted in each row's metadata). Tiers the catalog has no field for (360p, 540p, 580p, 1440p, 2160p) are named in the row's metadata comment and left unpriced. 5 existing fal_ai rows are updated because their page price differs from the catalog (listed under Changed). Mode is `image_generation` for text-to-image and image-to-image ids and `video_generation` for the video ids; `supported_endpoints`, `supported_modalities` and `supports_vision` follow the existing fal_ai siblings for the same category.

392 ids are left out because fal bills them in a unit the catalog has no field for, and 82 ids are left out because the page states a conditional or compound price (per clip, audio on/off, promotional, first-megapixel-plus-extra, per layer, and so on); both groups are listed at the bottom with their unit so Kerry can rule on them. Delisted is empty by design for fal-ai (the list omits some live endpoints). 11 ids have no model page at all (HTTP 404 or redirect) and stay out.

### Test change
`tests/unit/test_utils.py::test_aaamodel_prices_and_context_window_json_is_valid` caps every cost field at $1 unless the key is in its exceptions list. The three `fal_ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/us/*` rows state $1.164 per second at 1080p on their page (the same rate the existing `fal_ai/bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video` row carries), so they are added to that list next to the seedance-2.0 rows that are already there.

- `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1`: output_cost_per_image=0.04 -> output_cost_per_image=0.04, output_cost_per_pixel=3.8147e-08. Page: "- Price: $0.04 per megapixels"

- `fal_ai/fal-ai/nano-banana`: output_cost_per_image=0.039 -> output_cost_per_image=0.0398. Page: "Each image costs $0.0398. For $1.00, you can generate 25 images."
- `fal_ai/fal-ai/stable-diffusion-v35-medium`: output_cost_per_image=0.0398 -> output_cost_per_image=0.02, output_cost_per_pixel=1.90735e-08. Page: "- Price: $0.02 per megapixels"
- 7 other ids in the diff already match their page (`fal_ai/fal-ai/flux-lora-depth`, `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux-pro/v1.1-ultra`, `fal_ai/fal-ai/flux/dev`, `fal_ai/fal-ai/ideogram/v3`, `fal_ai/fal-ai/nano-banana-2`, `fal_ai/fal-ai/nano-banana-pro`, `fal_ai/minimax/h3/text-to-video`), not rewritten

- New rows billed per image: 197 rows, evidence in the PR comments
- New rows billed per megapixel: 189 rows, evidence in the PR comments
- New rows billed per second of video, single rate: 113 rows, evidence in the PR comments
- New rows billed per second of video with resolution tiers: 102 rows, evidence in the PR comments

11 ids whose page states a time-limited promotion take the rate live on 2026-11-10 (flux-3-max 50% off through 2026-11-22, MiniMax H3 Max 30% off through 2026-11-15), or the regular rate when the promotion has ended (flux-3-max keyframes, HeyGen). issue.title: feat: add claude mythos 5.2 to vertex ai cost map
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

title

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Claude Mythos 5.2 on Vertex AI had no cost-map row, so `vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2` fails model lookup and bills $0

How it solves it:

- Adds `vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2` and `vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2@default` as copies of the Vertex Fable 5.2 rows
- $8/$40 per MTok, $10 5m and $16 1h cache writes, $0.20 cache reads, 50% batch, 1.1x regional uplift
- Same 1M context, 128K output, adaptive thinking and 2027-11-09 retirement as the Fable 5.2 rows
- Like the Vertex Fable 5.2 rows, no `fast` multiplier, since the Vertex cost path does not bill fast mode

## User Flow

issue.title: perf(spend): narrow user and team spend log reads to the owner's api_keys so the (api_key, startTime) index is used
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

rework the UI queries that still use spendlogs so that it uses indexed spendlogs columns instead of scanning all rows

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` has no index on `"user"` or `team_id`
- `/spend/logs/ui` with `user_id` or `team_id` scans the whole date window
- `/team/spend/by_user` (Usage > Team > Spend Per User) does the same, no row cap
- On a busy proxy both get slower with traffic, not with the user's own usage

How it solves it:

- Resolve the user or team to its api_keys first (indexed lookup)
- Add `api_key = ANY($keys)` so Postgres uses the existing `(api_key, "startTime")` index
- Keys come from `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` / `LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend` rows in the window plus live keys, so deleted keys still count
- The original `"user"` / `team_id` filter stays, so results are byte-for-byte identical
- No known keys, more than 5000 keys, or a `search` lookup falls back to today's query unchanged
- The key lookup runs under the same 30s statement timeout as the log reads

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin filtering spend logs to one person on a proxy with months of traffic waits for a full scan of the date range, and on a large table gets a 503

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?client=claude-code and pick a person in the Client Usage panel
2. The panel calls GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui?user_id=...&start_date=...&end_date=...&page_size=1000
3. Postgres walks every spend log in the date range newest first, discarding every row that is not that person's, until it finds 1000
4. On a big table this runs past the 30s statement timeout and the panel shows "Spend logs took longer than 30s. Pick a shorter date range"
5. Same on https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?view=team&team=..., whose "Spend Per User Within Team" card calls GET /team/spend/by_user and sums that team's rows out of a full scan

After: the same clicks return the same numbers, and the work is proportional to that person's or team's own rows

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?client=claude-code and pick a person in the Client Usage panel
2. The panel calls the same GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui?user_id=... URL
3. Postgres reads only the rows written under that person's keys in the date range and returns the same 1000-row page
4. The team Usage page's "Spend Per User Within Team" card loads the same way, same rows, same totals

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. Local Postgres (`DATABASE_URL`), the proxy started as `uv run --no-sync litellm --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --port 4000 --use_v2_migration_resolver` with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set. This change only alters two read-only SQL statements, so both legs ran one worker with no Redis and no `--reload`, the same on both sides. Seed data: team `platform-eng` with users alice, bob, carol, one key each, 11 `POST /v1/chat/completions` calls to `anthropic-haiku-4-5` through the proxy with `User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.263 (external, cli)`, `claude-cli/2.1.263 (external, claude-desktop-3p)` and `curl/8.5.0`. Postgres statement logging on with `ALTER SYSTEM SET log_min_duration_statement = 0` so the exact SQL and bind parameters the proxy sent are in `/var/log/postgresql/postgresql-14-main.log`. The three calls, run identically on both sides with `$KEY` the master key, `$ALICE` alice's user_id and `$TEAM` the team_id:

```
curl -s -G http://localhost:4000/spend/logs/ui --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-11-03 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-11-11 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "user_id=$ALICE" -d page=1 -d page_size=1000 -d sort_by=startTime -d sort_order=desc -d group_by_session=false -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
curl -s -G http://localhost:4000/spend/logs/ui --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-11-03 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-11-11 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "team_id=$TEAM" -d page=1 -d page_size=1000 -d sort_by=startTime -d sort_order=desc -d group_by_session=false -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
curl -s -G http://localhost:4000/team/spend/by_user --data-urlencode "team_ids=$TEAM" -d start_date=2026-11-03 -d end_date=2026-11-10 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

### Before (9fb29c7e38)

#### /spend/logs/ui?user_id

1. Response: `total: 6`, 6 rows, saved to `before_user.json`
2. SQL the proxy sent (from the Postgres log), filter on the unindexed `"user"` column only:

```
WHERE "startTime" >= ($1::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "startTime" <= ($2::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "user" = $3
ORDER BY "startTime" DESC
LIMIT $4 OFFSET $5
parameters: $1 = '2026-11-03T00:00:00+00:00', $2 = '2026-11-11T00:00:00+00:00', $3 = 'd4f04bb9-...', $4 = '1000', $5 = '0'
```

#### /spend/logs/ui?team_id

1. Response: `total: 11`, 11 rows, saved to `before_team.json`
2. SQL: same shape with `AND team_id = $3`

#### /team/spend/by_user

1. Response: alice 6 requests / 190 tokens, bob 3 / 97, carol 2 / 70, saved to `before_teamuser.json`
2. SQL:

```
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" sl
LEFT JOIN "LiteLLM_UserTable" u ON u.user_id = sl."user"
WHERE sl."startTime" >= $1::timestamp
    AND sl."startTime" < $2::timestamp + INTERVAL '1 day'
    AND sl.team_id IN ($3)
parameters: $1 = '2026-11-03', $2 = '2026-11-10', $3 = '4afd452f-...'
```

### After (91fc0e7d33)

#### /spend/logs/ui?user_id

1. Response identical to Before (`json.load(after) == json.load(before)` is `True` for all three files)
2. New key lookup the proxy sent first (inside the same statement-timeout transaction as the log read), every column indexed:

```
SELECT DISTINCT api_key FROM (
    SELECT api_key FROM "LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend"
    WHERE user_id = $1 AND date >= $2 AND date <= $3
    UNION ALL
    SELECT token AS api_key FROM "LiteLLM_VerificationToken" WHERE user_id = $1
) owned
LIMIT $4
parameters: $1 = 'd4f04bb9-...', $2 = '2026-11-02', $3 = '2026-11-12', $4 = '5001'
```

3. The spend log query now carries the key list next to the unchanged user filter:

```
WHERE "startTime" >= ($1::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "startTime" <= ($2::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "user" = $3 AND api_key = ANY($4::text[])
ORDER BY "startTime" DESC
LIMIT $5 OFFSET $6
```

#### /spend/logs/ui?team_id

1. Response identical to Before
2. Lookup hits `LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend` with `$1 = '{4afd452f-...}', $2 = '2026-11-02', $3 = '2026-11-12', $4 = '5001'`
3. Spend log query: `... AND team_id = $3 AND api_key = ANY($4::text[])` with `$4 = '{2a935b68...,c6376820...,d6bc85d4...}'` (the team's three key hashes)

#### /team/spend/by_user

1. Response identical to Before
2. SQL: `AND sl.team_id IN ($3) AND sl.api_key = ANY($4::text[])` with the same three key hashes

#### Plans at scale

The seed table is too small for the planner to care, so the same four statements ran against a 1,500,000 row copy of `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` with the production index set (`startTime`, `(startTime, request_id)`, `(api_key, startTime)`), 2000 keys, 500 users, 50 teams, 60 days of rows, 30 day window, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`:

<details>
<summary>Before and After plans</summary>

```
== BEFORE /spend/logs/ui user_id (main)
Index Scan Backward using startTime_idx
  Filter: ("user" = 'user7'::text)
  Rows Removed by Filter: 166914 (per worker, x3)
  Buffers: shared hit=2468 read=13613
Execution Time: 88.788 ms

== AFTER /spend/logs/ui user_id (this PR)
Bitmap Heap Scan
  Filter: ("user" = 'user7'::text)
  -> Bitmap Index Scan on api_key_startTime_idx (actual rows=3000)
  Buffers: shared hit=995 read=2029
Execution Time: 26.105 ms

== BEFORE /team/spend/by_user (main)
Parallel Seq Scan
  Rows Removed by Filter: 490000 (per worker, x3)
  Buffers: shared hit=14021 read=22868
Execution Time: 107.667 ms

== AFTER /team/spend/by_user (this PR)
Bitmap Heap Scan
  Filter: (team_id = 'team7'::text)
  -> Bitmap Index Scan on api_key_startTime_idx (actual rows=30000)
  Buffers: shared hit=8975 read=21262
Execution Time: 169.540 ms
```

</details>

The user case drops from 16k buffers to 3k and stops discarding rows. The team case in this synthetic table is 2% of all rows spread evenly over every page, so the heap reads barely move and the bitmap costs a little more wall time there; the gain shows up when a team is a small share of a large table, and when the key list covers most of the table the planner picks the old plan on its own.

Tests: `tests/unit/proxy/spend_tracking/test_spend_management_endpoints.py -k ui_view_spend_logs` (87 passed) and `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_endpoints.py -k team_spend_by_user` (13 passed). The `/spend/logs/ui` tests model daily rows and live keys as separate lookup sources and the fake page filter honors the key list, so a deleted key known only from daily rows, or a live key with no daily rows yet, dropping out of the result fails the test. Mutation: dropping the `api_key = ANY(...)` clause from either query fails the four new/updated tests (`test_ui_view_spend_logs_user_filter_reads_spend_logs_through_the_users_api_keys`, `..._team_filter_reads_spend_logs_through_the_teams_api_keys`, `test_get_team_spend_by_user_admin_groups_spend_logs_by_team_and_user`, `test_get_team_spend_by_user_plain_member_only_sees_own_row`), restoring it turns them green.

## Type

🧹 Refactoring

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- A request whose spend log row was written but whose daily spend row was not, under a key deleted since, is no longer matched. Live keys are always included, so this only affects deleted keys, and it is the same gap the daily Usage views already have

### Low

- One extra indexed query per request on the two endpoints
- An owner with no known keys, or more than 5000 keys in the window, gets today's unnarrowed query
- `/spend/logs/ui` with `search` is never narrowed, since the request_id match there spans all time
- The non-admin own-rows scope (`"user" = $x OR team_id = ANY(...)`) is not narrowed here, only explicit `user_id` / `team_id` filters

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/59b50a5f0e3f48fba54c6d66c4ceec96
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/59b50a5f0e3f48fba54c6d66c4ceec96?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes read paths and query semantics for spend logs; edge cases around deleted keys without daily rows could omit rows that the previous full scan would include.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`spend_log_api_key_scope`**, which resolves a user or team's API keys from daily spend tables plus live verification tokens (with a 5000-key cap and fallback to the old query shape).
> 
> **`/spend/logs/ui`** and **`/team/spend/by_user`** now run that lookup first, then add `api_key = ANY($keys)` alongside the existing `user` / `team_id` filters so reads can use the `(api_key, startTime)` index instead of scanning the date window. Search-based UI queries skip narrowing so old keys outside the window still match.
> 
> Unit tests assert the new SQL clauses, lookup parameters, and fallback when no usable key list exists.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 91fc0e7d3358fddf7ecaa83cc86d147942ce0118. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

#### /spend/logs/ui?team_id

1. Response: `total: 11`, 11 rows, saved to `before_team.json`
2. SQL: same shape with `AND team_id = $3`

#### /team/spend/by_user

1. Response: alice 6 requests / 190 tokens, bob 3 / 97, carol 2 / 70, saved to `before_teamuser.json`
2. SQL:

```
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" sl
LEFT JOIN "LiteLLM_UserTable" u ON u.user_id = sl."user"
WHERE sl."startTime" >= $1::timestamp
    AND sl."startTime" < $2::timestamp + INTERVAL '1 day'
    AND sl.team_id IN ($3)
parameters: $1 = '2026-11-03', $2 = '2026-11-10', $3 = '4afd452f-...'
```

### After (91fc0e7d33)

#### /spend/logs/ui?user_id

1. Response identical to Before (`json.load(after) == json.load(before)` is `True` for all three files)
2. New key lookup the proxy sent first (inside the same statement-timeout transaction as the log read), every column indexed:

```
SELECT DISTINCT api_key FROM (
    SELECT api_key FROM "LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend"
    WHERE user_id = $1 AND date >= $2 AND date <= $3
    UNION ALL
    SELECT token AS api_key FROM "LiteLLM_VerificationToken" WHERE user_id = $1
) owned
LIMIT $4
parameters: $1 = 'd4f04bb9-...', $2 = '2026-11-02', $3 = '2026-11-12', $4 = '5001'
```

3. The spend log query now carries the key list next to the unchanged user filter:

```
WHERE "startTime" >= ($1::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "startTime" <= ($2::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "user" = $3 AND api_key = ANY($4::text[])
ORDER BY "startTime" DESC
LIMIT $5 OFFSET $6
```

#### /spend/logs/ui?team_id

1. Response identical to Before
2. Lookup hits `LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend` with `$1 = '{4afd452f-...}', $2 = '2026-11-02', $3 = '2026-11-12', $4 = '5001'`
3. Spend log query: `... AND team_id = $3 AND api_key = ANY($4::text[])` with `$4 = '{2a935b68...,c6376820...,d6bc85d4...}'` (the team's three key hashes)

#### /team/spend/by_user

1. Response identical to Before
2. SQL: `AND sl.team_id IN ($3) AND sl.api_key = ANY($4::text[])` with the same three key hashes

#### Plans at scale

The seed table is too small for the planner to care, so the same four statements ran against a 1,500,000 row copy of `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` with the production index set (`startTime`, `(startTime, request_id)`, `(api_key, startTime)`), 2000 keys, 500 users, 50 teams, 60 days of rows, 30 day window, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`:

<details>
<summary>Before and After plans</summary>

```
== BEFORE /spend/logs/ui user_id (main)
Index Scan Backward using startTime_idx
  Filter: ("user" = 'user7'::text)
  Rows Removed by Filter: 166914 (per worker, x3)
  Buffers: shared hit=2468 read=13613
Execution Time: 88.788 ms

== AFTER /spend/logs/ui user_id (this PR)
Bitmap Heap Scan
  Filter: ("user" = 'user7'::text)
  -> Bitmap Index Scan on api_key_startTime_idx (actual rows=3000)
  Buffers: shared hit=995 read=2029
Execution Time: 26.105 ms

== BEFORE /team/spend/by_user (main)
Parallel Seq Scan
  Rows Removed by Filter: 490000 (per worker, x3)
  Buffers: shared hit=14021 read=22868
Execution Time: 107.667 ms

== AFTER /team/spend/by_user (this PR)
Bitmap Heap Scan
  Filter: (team_id = 'team7'::text)
  -> Bitmap Index Scan on api_key_startTime_idx (actual rows=30000)
  Buffers: shared hit=8975 read=21262
Execution Time: 169.540 ms
```

</details>

The user case drops from 16k buffers to 3k and stops discarding rows. The team case in this synthetic table is 2% of all rows spread evenly over every page, so the heap reads barely move and the bitmap costs a little more wall time there; the gain shows up when a team is a small share of a large table, and when the key list covers most of the table the planner picks the old plan on its own.

Tests: `tests/unit/proxy/spend_tracking/test_spend_management_endpoints.py -k ui_view_spend_logs` (87 passed) and `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_endpoints.py -k team_spend_by_user` (13 passed). The `/spend/logs/ui` tests model daily rows and live keys as separate lookup sources and the fake page filter honors the key list, so a deleted key known only from daily rows, or a live key with no daily rows yet, dropping out of the result fails the test. Mutation: dropping the `api_key = ANY(...)` clause from either query fails the four new/updated tests (`test_ui_view_spend_logs_user_filter_reads_spend_logs_through_the_users_api_keys`, `..._team_filter_reads_spend_logs_through_the_teams_api_keys`, `test_get_team_spend_by_user_admin_groups_spend_logs_by_team_and_user`, `test_get_team_spend_by_user_plain_member_only_sees_own_row`), restoring it turns them green.

## Type

🧹 Refactoring

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- A request whose spend log row was written but whose daily spend row was not, under a key deleted since, is no longer matched. Live keys are always included, so this only affects deleted keys, and it is the same gap the daily Usage views already have

### Low

- One extra indexed query per request on the two endpoints
- An owner with no known keys, or more than 5000 keys in the window, gets today's unnarrowed query
- `/spend/logs/ui` with `search` is never narrowed, since the request_id match there spans all time
- The non-admin own-rows scope (`"user" = $x OR team_id = ANY(...)`) is not narrowed here, only explicit `user_id` / `team_id` filters

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>
