issue.title: feat(gemini): file-backed batch jobs on /v1/batches with output download
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `custom_llm_provider: gemini` 400s on `POST /v1/batches`, so Gemini Developer API batches cannot run through the gateway
- Gemini file content download is unimplemented, so a batch output file cannot be read through `/v1/files`
- A customer asked for Gemini batches through LiteLLM so spend lands on their virtual keys (Pylon #11681)

How it solves it:

- `GeminiBatchesConfig` creates `models/{model}:batchGenerateContent` jobs from an uploaded file and maps the operation to the OpenAI batch object
- `GoogleAIStudioFilesHandler` downloads a file through `download/v1beta/files/{id}:download?alt=media`
- Gemini runs the OpenAI-shaped JSONL the proxy uploads today unchanged and writes OpenAI-shaped output rows, so nothing changes on the upload side
- Scope is the minimal end-to-end flow (upload, create, poll, download). List, cancel and `CheckBatchCost` pricing of Gemini output rows are follow-ups

## User Flow

Before: a developer uploads a batch file for a Gemini deployment and cannot start the batch

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch`, header `x-litellm-model: gemini-3.8-flash` and a JSONL of `/v1/chat/completions` rows, and get back a `file-...` id
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that `input_file_id` and `"model": "gemini-3.8-flash"`
3. They get 400 `LiteLLM doesn't support custom_llm_provider=gemini for 'create_batch'`

After: the same developer runs the batch to completion and reads the results through the gateway

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files and get back a `file-...` id
2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches and get 200 with a `batch_...` id, `status: validating` and `request_counts.total` equal to their row count
3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{id} and see `in_progress`, then `completed` with `completed_at`, `request_counts.completed` and an `output_file_id`
4. They send GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content and get the JSONL back, one `{"custom_id", "response": {"status_code", "body": {chat.completion}}}` row per request

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10619

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. Real proxy, real Postgres, real Redis, real Gemini Developer API calls on `gemini-3.8-flash`, no mocks. Env vars set: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`. Two uvicorn workers were serving in both legs (`Started server process` printed twice).

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log
```

<details>
<summary>qa_config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini-3.8-flash
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-3.8-flash
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379

litellm_settings:
  drop_params: True
```

</details>

Virtual key: `POST /key/generate` with the master key and `{"models": ["gemini-3.8-flash"]}`, used as `VIRTUAL_KEY` below.

<details>
<summary>flow.py (the client, run as VIRTUAL_KEY=... python flow.py)</summary>

```python
"""End-user flow through the proxy with a virtual key: upload JSONL, create gemini batch, poll, download output."""
import json, os, sys, time, httpx
PROXY = os.environ.get("PROXY", "http://127.0.0.1:4000"); KEY = os.environ["VIRTUAL_KEY"]; MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash"
H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}"}
rows = [{"custom_id": f"r{i}", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions",
         "body": {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"Reply with the number {i} only."}]}} for i in range(2)]
jsonl = ("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in rows) + "\n").encode()
with httpx.Client(timeout=120) as c:
    up = c.post(f"{PROXY}/v1/files", headers={**H, "x-litellm-model": MODEL}, files={"file": ("in.jsonl", jsonl, "application/jsonl")},
                data={"purpose": "batch"})
    print("UPLOAD", up.status_code, up.text[:300]); up.raise_for_status()
    file_id = up.json()["id"]
    cr = c.post(f"{PROXY}/v1/batches", headers=H, json={"input_file_id": file_id, "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
                                                        "completion_window": "24h", "model": MODEL,
                                                        "metadata": {"display_name": "litellm-proof"}})
    print("CREATE", cr.status_code, cr.text[:400])
    if cr.status_code != 200: sys.exit(1)
    batch_id = cr.json()["id"]
    for _ in range(60):
        time.sleep(15)
        b = c.get(f"{PROXY}/v1/batches/{batch_id}", headers=H); bj = b.json()
        print("POLL", b.status_code, bj.get("status"), json.dumps(bj.get("request_counts")))
        if bj.get("status") in ("completed", "failed", "expired", "cancelled"): break
    print("BATCH", json.dumps({k: bj.get(k) for k in ("id", "status", "input_file_id", "output_file_id", "created_at", "completed_at", "request_counts", "metadata")}))
    out = c.get(f"{PROXY}/v1/files/{bj['output_file_id']}/content", headers=H)
    print("OUTPUT", out.status_code)
    for line in out.text.splitlines():
        j = json.loads(line); print(" ", j["custom_id"], j["response"]["status_code"], j["response"]["body"]["choices"][0]["message"]["content"], j["response"]["body"].get("usage"))
```

</details>

### Before (9fb29c7e38)

1. `python flow.py`
2. Observed:

```
UPLOAD 200 {"id":"file-bGl0ZWxsbTpo...","bytes":368,"created_at":1794346345,"filename":"in.jsonl","object":"file","purpose":"user_data","status":"uploaded","expires_at":null,"status_details":null
CREATE 400 {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: LiteLLM doesn't support custom_llm_provider=gemini for 'create_batch'","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":"400"}}
```

### After (e6f99bb4a4)

1. `python flow.py`
2. Observed (poll every 15s, two rows, each answered with its number):

```
UPLOAD 200 {"id":"file-bGl0ZWxsbTpo...","bytes":368,"created_at":1794346670,"filename":"in.jsonl","object":"file","purpose":"user_data","status":"uploaded","expires_at":null,"status_details":null
CREATE 200 {"id":"batch_bGl0ZWxsbTpv...","completion_window":"24h","created_at":1794346670,"endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","input_file_id":"file-bGl0ZWxsbTpo...","object":"batch","status":"validating","cancelled_at":nu
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 in_progress {"completed": 0, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
POLL 200 completed {"completed": 2, "failed": 0, "total": 2}
BATCH {"id": "batch_bGl0ZWxsbTpv...", "status": "completed", "input_file_id": "file-bGl0ZWxsbTpw...", "output_file_id": "file-bGl0ZWxsbTpi...", "created_at": 1794346670, "completed_at": 1794346809, "request_counts": {"completed": 2, "failed": 0, "total": 2}, "metadata": {"display_name": "litellm-proof"}}
OUTPUT 200
  r0 200 0 {'promptTokens': 9, 'totalTokens': 75, 'completionTokens': 1}
  r1 200 1 {'promptTokens': 9, 'totalTokens': 98, 'completionTokens': 1}
```

Red leg. With `litellm/` at the merge base and only the new tests applied: `tests/unit/llms/gemini/batches` fails to import `GeminiBatchesConfig`, and the 6 new tests in `tests/unit/llms/gemini/files/test_gemini_files_transformation.py` and `tests/unit/batches/test_main.py` fail (`NotImplementedError` on file content, `BadRequestError: LiteLLM doesn't support custom_llm_provider=gemini`). At the tip all 125 tests in the three files pass. `make lint` gates (ruff strict, LIT, TQ, OA, basedpyright) report no rule grew past the merge base.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- The batch rate limiter cannot count rows in a Gemini input file: Gemini only lets GENERATED files be downloaded (`400 Only GENERATED files can be downloaded.`), so it logs the error and lets the request through, same as before this PR (file content raised `NotImplementedError`). Upload-time JSONL validation still applies
- Spend is not tracked yet. `CheckBatchCost` prices Gemini output rows in the follow-up PR. The output usage block is camelCase (`promptTokens`, `completionTokens`), so that PR needs a small mapping

### Low

- Gemini output files expire after about 48 hours and are downloaded on demand, not copied into LiteLLM storage
- Only file-backed input. Inline `requests` batches, list and cancel are not wired for gemini
- Ids cross the LiteLLM boundary bare: `batches/<id>` becomes `<id>`, `files/batch-<id>` becomes `batch-<id>`. Both forms are accepted on the way back in
- `endpoint` is reported as `/v1/chat/completions` since Gemini does not echo the rows' `url`

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>


Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/6eacfc98ff0b45ccb0b2a8111b970281
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/6eacfc98ff0b45ccb0b2a8111b970281?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches provider routing and external Gemini batch/file APIs; spend tracking and batch rate limiting for Gemini output files remain follow-ups per the PR notes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **Gemini batch support** through a new `GeminiBatchesConfig` that creates `models/{model}:batchGenerateContent` jobs from an uploaded input file, polls `v1beta/batches/{id}`, and maps Gemini operations to OpenAI-shaped `LiteLLMBatch` objects (status, request counts, bare batch/file ids, `x-goog-api-key` auth).
> 
> **Gemini file handling** gains a shared `gemini_file_name()` normalizer and working `/v1/files/.../content` via `download/v1beta/files/{id}:download?alt=media`, enabling batch output JSONL to be read through the gateway.
> 
> `ProviderConfigManager` now returns `GeminiBatchesConfig` for `custom_llm_provider=gemini`, so create/retrieve batch calls route through the generic HTTP handler when a `model` is supplied—same pattern as Mistral/Bedrock. Unit tests cover transformations and dispatch.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e6f99bb4a48614a8d74f6fd4be75eef29524ce4d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379

  drop_params: True
```

</details>

Virtual key: `POST /key/generate` with the master key and `{"models": ["gemini-3.8-flash"]}`, used as `VIRTUAL_KEY` below.

<details>
<summary>flow.py (the client, run as VIRTUAL_KEY=... python flow.py)</summary>

```python
"""End-user flow through the proxy with a virtual key: upload JSONL, create gemini batch, poll, download output."""
import json, os, sys, time, httpx
PROXY = os.environ.get("PROXY", "http://127.0.0.1:4000"); KEY = os.environ["VIRTUAL_KEY"]; MODEL = "gemini-3.8-flash"
H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {KEY}"}
rows = [{"custom_id": f"r{i}", "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions",
         "body": {"model": MODEL, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"Reply with the number {i} only."}]}} for i in range(2)]
jsonl = ("\n".join(json.dumps(r) for r in rows) + "\n").encode()
with httpx.Client(timeout=120) as c:
    up = c.post(f"{PROXY}/v1/files", headers={**H, "x-litellm-model": MODEL}, files={"file": ("in.jsonl", jsonl, "application/jsonl")},
                data={"purpose": "batch"})
    print("UPLOAD", up.status_code, up.text[:300]); up.raise_for_status()
    file_id = up.json()["id"]
    cr = c.post(f"{PROXY}/v1/batches", headers=H, json={"input_file_id": file_id, "endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions",
                                                        "completion_window": "24h", "model": MODEL,
                                                        "metadata": {"display_name": "litellm-proof"}})
    print("CREATE", cr.status_code, cr.text[:400])
    if cr.status_code != 200: sys.exit(1)
    batch_id = cr.json()["id"]
    for _ in range(60):
        time.sleep(15)
        b = c.get(f"{PROXY}/v1/batches/{batch_id}", headers=H); bj = b.json()
        print("POLL", b.status_code, bj.get("status"), json.dumps(bj.get("request_counts")))
        if bj.get("status") in ("completed", "failed", "expired", "cancelled"): break
    print("BATCH", json.dumps({k: bj.get(k) for k in ("id", "status", "input_file_id", "output_file_id", "created_at", "completed_at", "request_counts", "metadata")}))
    out = c.get(f"{PROXY}/v1/files/{bj['output_file_id']}/content", headers=H)
    print("OUTPUT", out.status_code)
    for line in out.text.splitlines():
        j = json.loads(line); print(" ", j["custom_id"], j["response"]["status_code"], j["response"]["body"]["choices"][0]["message"]["content"], j["response"]["body"].get("usage"))
```

</details>

### Before (9fb29c7e38)

2. Observed:

OUTPUT 200
  r0 200 0 {'promptTokens': 9, 'totalTokens': 75, 'completionTokens': 1}
  r1 200 1 {'promptTokens': 9, 'totalTokens': 98, 'completionTokens': 1}
```

Red leg. With `litellm/` at the merge base and only the new tests applied: `tests/unit/llms/gemini/batches` fails to import `GeminiBatchesConfig`, and the 6 new tests in `tests/unit/llms/gemini/files/test_gemini_files_transformation.py` and `tests/unit/batches/test_main.py` fail (`NotImplementedError` on file content, `BadRequestError: LiteLLM doesn't support custom_llm_provider=gemini`). At the tip all 125 tests in the three files pass. `make lint` gates (ruff strict, LIT, TQ, OA, basedpyright) report no rule grew past the merge base.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- The batch rate limiter cannot count rows in a Gemini input file: Gemini only lets GENERATED files be downloaded (`400 Only GENERATED files can be downloaded.`), so it logs the error and lets the request through, same as before this PR (file content raised `NotImplementedError`). Upload-time JSONL validation still applies
- Spend is not tracked yet. `CheckBatchCost` prices Gemini output rows in the follow-up PR. The output usage block is camelCase (`promptTokens`, `completionTokens`), so that PR needs a small mapping

### Low

- Gemini output files expire after about 48 hours and are downloaded on demand, not copied into LiteLLM storage
- Only file-backed input. Inline `requests` batches, list and cancel are not wired for gemini
- Ids cross the LiteLLM boundary bare: `batches/<id>` becomes `<id>`, `files/batch-<id>` becomes `batch-<id>`. Both forms are accepted on the way back in
- `endpoint` is reported as `/v1/chat/completions` since Gemini does not echo the rows' `url`

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

issue.title: feat(changelog): add ?digest= and ?models= feed views and a subscribe builder on the changelog page
issue.body:
## Summary

The #shipped Slack channel subscribes to `/changelog.xml` through Slack's RSS app, and today's registry audit commit produced 13 separate items, each titled by one model and each ending in a truncated list of raw `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/...` ids. `/changelog.xml?digest=commit` now folds everything one litellm catalog commit changed into a single item, and `?digest=1h` (`30m`, `4h`, `1d`) folds everything that landed in one clock-aligned window, so the channel gets one post per commit or per hour that reads like a release note.

For commit c319616 the digest item is

```
8 models added, 8 updated on 4 providers
• DeepSeek Flash Latest added on Fireworks AI
• GLM Fast Latest added on Fireworks AI
• ...
• Claude Mythos 5.1 on Azure AI Foundry: Web search price added: $0.01 / query, Web search enabled
• +7 more
```

The title counts the models added and updated (a new provider's bullet counts all of its models) and names their providers (or says `N providers` past three). The body has one bullet per model, regional aliases with the same name collapsed to one with their note written once, the notes of a model's price and capability items joined onto its one bullet, and it stops before Slack's 500-character cut (`DIGEST_BODY_LIMIT` 480) with a `+N more` line. A commit with one model yields that model's bullet as the title.

Per commit, the guid is `digest:<sha>` and the link stays the GitHub commit. Per window, the guid is `digest:1h:<window start ISO>`, the `pubDate` is the window's end, and the link is the commit when the window holds one and the changelog page (with the feed's utm tags) when it holds several. A window counts as closed once the changelog's `generatedAt` is past its end, not the wall clock, so a reader that posts an item the first time it sees its guid never posts an hour the next 10-minute build would still add a commit to. With the 5-minute CDN cache on the function, a window shows up 10 to 25 minutes after it closes.

### Following only the models a proxy runs

`?models=azure/gpt-5,claude-opus-4-5` narrows the feed to those models, next to `?kind=` and `?providers=`. Each value is compared by `modelKey`, the slug of its last path segment, and a listing matches on the key of its catalog id, the slug of the whole id, or the slug of its display name, so `azure/gpt-5`, `openai/gpt-5`, `gpt-5` and `GPT-5` all follow the catalog's `gpt-5`, and a proxy's `model:` strings work as they are. A multi-model addition is cut down to the matching listings and its headline recounted, and a new provider narrowed this way becomes a `model` item (`Alpha added on Newco`) rather than claiming the provider arrived with two models.

The `/changelog` page gets a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel (a `<details>` above the filters) that combines all four dimensions: the cadence (`DIGEST_OPTIONS`: every change, per commit, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d), change-type checkboxes, a provider picker with chips, and a textarea for the proxy's models. `parseModelList` takes the JSON of `/model/info` (`litellm_params.model`, falling back to `model_name`) or `/v1/models` (`id`), a `config.yaml` (its `model:` lines), or ids separated by commas, spaces or newlines, and the panel says how many of them changed in the last 30 days. `feedUrl(filter)` renders the URL with `/`, `:` and `@` kept readable, and the panel offers Copy URL and Copy Slack command (`/feed subscribe <url>`). Opening `/changelog?models=...&digest=1h` (any feed parameter) opens the panel prefilled, so a proxy's admin UI can link straight to a feed for its model list.

```ts
// src/changelogPresentation.ts
interface FeedFilter { kinds; providers; models; digest }
feedFilter(params)            // reads ?kind= ?providers= ?models= ?digest=
feedUrl(filter)               // https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?kind=price&models=azure/gpt-5,o3&digest=1h
parseModelList(text)          // ["azure/gpt-5", "vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929"]
filterChangelogItems(items, filter)  // kind, provider, then models (entries narrowed)

// api/changelog.ts
const entries = filter.digest
  ? digestFeedEntries(items, filter.digest, Date.parse(data.generatedAt))
  : items.map(feedEntry);
```

Filters apply before the digest, so `?digest=1h&kind=price&models=gpt-5` folds only GPT-5 price changes. An unknown `digest=` value falls back to the per-change feed. The default feed is unchanged, so existing readers keep their items and guids.

`changelogRss` now takes `FeedEntry[]` (id, link, timestamp, category, title, body) instead of `ChangelogItem[]`, with `feedEntry()` producing today's per-change item. `FeedFilter.digest` is the validated `digest=` token (`""`, `"commit"` or a span). `ChangelogItem` carries `providerName` so the digest can name providers without recomputing them. Two capability flags that fell through to the generic label are named now, so `Supports web search enabled` reads `Web search enabled`, and `supports_tool_choice` reads `Tool choice`.

Tracking: `middleware.ts` adds `digest`, and `models` next to `kind` and `providers`, to the Feed Fetched event when the query asks for them. The panel sends `Changelog Feed Builder Opened`, `Changelog Feed Builder Changed` (digest) and `Changelog Feed Copied` (what, digest, kind, providers, model count), never the pasted text.

To switch the channel over, unsubscribe the current feed and run `/feed subscribe https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?digest=1h` (or `digest=commit`), or build the URL on `/changelog`. Switching the default feed's shape instead would give every existing subscriber a flood of re-posted items, since the guids change.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Default `/changelog.xml` behavior is unchanged; new query params and UI are additive, with broad test coverage on feed shaping and filtering.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends `/changelog.xml` with **`?digest=`** (`commit`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d`) so Slack/RSS readers get one summarized item per catalog commit or clock window (bullets per model, Slack-length cap, open windows held until the build closes them), and **`?models=`** to narrow updates to specific catalog or proxy model ids (matched on last path segment).
> 
> The changelog page adds a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel: digest cadence, change types, providers, pasted proxy JSON/YAML/model lists via `parseModelList`, generated `feedUrl`, and copy-to-Slack support; query params prefill the panel. `changelogPresentation` gains `FeedEntry`, `digestFeedEntries`, model filtering, and `changelogRss` now renders entries instead of raw items; `api/changelog` and middleware apply the new filters and track `digest`/`models`. README documents the feed options; tests cover digest, model filter, and the UI builder.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 468a3428ec22b995e2bdd8dc9b329a785a7e0463. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

issue.title: perf(spend): narrow user and team spend log reads to the owner's api_keys so the (api_key, startTime) index is used
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

rework the UI queries that still use spendlogs so that it uses indexed spendlogs columns instead of scanning all rows

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` has no index on `"user"` or `team_id`
- `/spend/logs/ui` with `user_id` or `team_id` scans the whole date window
- `/team/spend/by_user` (Usage > Team > Spend Per User) does the same, no row cap
- On a busy proxy both get slower with traffic, not with the user's own usage

How it solves it:

- Resolve the user or team to its api_keys first (indexed lookup)
- Add `api_key = ANY($keys)` so Postgres uses the existing `(api_key, "startTime")` index
- Keys come from `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` / `LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend` rows in the window plus live keys, so deleted keys still count
- The original `"user"` / `team_id` filter stays, so results are byte-for-byte identical
- No known keys, more than 5000 keys, or a `search` lookup falls back to today's query unchanged
- The key lookup runs under the same 30s statement timeout as the log reads

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin filtering spend logs to one person on a proxy with months of traffic waits for a full scan of the date range, and on a large table gets a 503

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?client=claude-code and pick a person in the Client Usage panel
2. The panel calls GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui?user_id=...&start_date=...&end_date=...&page_size=1000
3. Postgres walks every spend log in the date range newest first, discarding every row that is not that person's, until it finds 1000
4. On a big table this runs past the 30s statement timeout and the panel shows "Spend logs took longer than 30s. Pick a shorter date range"
5. Same on https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?view=team&team=..., whose "Spend Per User Within Team" card calls GET /team/spend/by_user and sums that team's rows out of a full scan

After: the same clicks return the same numbers, and the work is proportional to that person's or team's own rows

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?client=claude-code and pick a person in the Client Usage panel
2. The panel calls the same GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui?user_id=... URL
3. Postgres reads only the rows written under that person's keys in the date range and returns the same 1000-row page
4. The team Usage page's "Spend Per User Within Team" card loads the same way, same rows, same totals

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup. Local Postgres (`DATABASE_URL`), the proxy started as `uv run --no-sync litellm --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --port 4000 --use_v2_migration_resolver` with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set. This change only alters two read-only SQL statements, so both legs ran one worker with no Redis and no `--reload`, the same on both sides. Seed data: team `platform-eng` with users alice, bob, carol, one key each, 11 `POST /v1/chat/completions` calls to `anthropic-haiku-4-5` through the proxy with `User-Agent: claude-cli/2.1.263 (external, cli)`, `claude-cli/2.1.263 (external, claude-desktop-3p)` and `curl/8.5.0`. Postgres statement logging on with `ALTER SYSTEM SET log_min_duration_statement = 0` so the exact SQL and bind parameters the proxy sent are in `/var/log/postgresql/postgresql-14-main.log`. The three calls, run identically on both sides with `$KEY` the master key, `$ALICE` alice's user_id and `$TEAM` the team_id:

```
curl -s -G http://localhost:4000/spend/logs/ui --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-11-03 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-11-11 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "user_id=$ALICE" -d page=1 -d page_size=1000 -d sort_by=startTime -d sort_order=desc -d group_by_session=false -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
curl -s -G http://localhost:4000/spend/logs/ui --data-urlencode "start_date=2026-11-03 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "end_date=2026-11-11 00:00:00" --data-urlencode "team_id=$TEAM" -d page=1 -d page_size=1000 -d sort_by=startTime -d sort_order=desc -d group_by_session=false -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
curl -s -G http://localhost:4000/team/spend/by_user --data-urlencode "team_ids=$TEAM" -d start_date=2026-11-03 -d end_date=2026-11-10 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

### Before (9fb29c7e38)

#### /spend/logs/ui?user_id

1. Response: `total: 6`, 6 rows, saved to `before_user.json`
2. SQL the proxy sent (from the Postgres log), filter on the unindexed `"user"` column only:

```
WHERE "startTime" >= ($1::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "startTime" <= ($2::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "user" = $3
ORDER BY "startTime" DESC
LIMIT $4 OFFSET $5
parameters: $1 = '2026-11-03T00:00:00+00:00', $2 = '2026-11-11T00:00:00+00:00', $3 = 'd4f04bb9-...', $4 = '1000', $5 = '0'
```

#### /spend/logs/ui?team_id

1. Response: `total: 11`, 11 rows, saved to `before_team.json`
2. SQL: same shape with `AND team_id = $3`

#### /team/spend/by_user

1. Response: alice 6 requests / 190 tokens, bob 3 / 97, carol 2 / 70, saved to `before_teamuser.json`
2. SQL:

```
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" sl
LEFT JOIN "LiteLLM_UserTable" u ON u.user_id = sl."user"
WHERE sl."startTime" >= $1::timestamp
    AND sl."startTime" < $2::timestamp + INTERVAL '1 day'
    AND sl.team_id IN ($3)
parameters: $1 = '2026-11-03', $2 = '2026-11-10', $3 = '4afd452f-...'
```

### After (91fc0e7d33)

#### /spend/logs/ui?user_id

1. Response identical to Before (`json.load(after) == json.load(before)` is `True` for all three files)
2. New key lookup the proxy sent first (inside the same statement-timeout transaction as the log read), every column indexed:

```
SELECT DISTINCT api_key FROM (
    SELECT api_key FROM "LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend"
    WHERE user_id = $1 AND date >= $2 AND date <= $3
    UNION ALL
    SELECT token AS api_key FROM "LiteLLM_VerificationToken" WHERE user_id = $1
) owned
LIMIT $4
parameters: $1 = 'd4f04bb9-...', $2 = '2026-11-02', $3 = '2026-11-12', $4 = '5001'
```

3. The spend log query now carries the key list next to the unchanged user filter:

```
WHERE "startTime" >= ($1::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "startTime" <= ($2::timestamptz AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND "user" = $3 AND api_key = ANY($4::text[])
ORDER BY "startTime" DESC
LIMIT $5 OFFSET $6
```

#### /spend/logs/ui?team_id

1. Response identical to Before
2. Lookup hits `LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend` with `$1 = '{4afd452f-...}', $2 = '2026-11-02', $3 = '2026-11-12', $4 = '5001'`
3. Spend log query: `... AND team_id = $3 AND api_key = ANY($4::text[])` with `$4 = '{2a935b68...,c6376820...,d6bc85d4...}'` (the team's three key hashes)

#### /team/spend/by_user

1. Response identical to Before
2. SQL: `AND sl.team_id IN ($3) AND sl.api_key = ANY($4::text[])` with the same three key hashes

#### Plans at scale

The seed table is too small for the planner to care, so the same four statements ran against a 1,500,000 row copy of `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` with the production index set (`startTime`, `(startTime, request_id)`, `(api_key, startTime)`), 2000 keys, 500 users, 50 teams, 60 days of rows, 30 day window, `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)`:

<details>
<summary>Before and After plans</summary>

```
== BEFORE /spend/logs/ui user_id (main)
Index Scan Backward using startTime_idx
  Filter: ("user" = 'user7'::text)
  Rows Removed by Filter: 166914 (per worker, x3)
  Buffers: shared hit=2468 read=13613
Execution Time: 88.788 ms

== AFTER /spend/logs/ui user_id (this PR)
Bitmap Heap Scan
  Filter: ("user" = 'user7'::text)
  -> Bitmap Index Scan on api_key_startTime_idx (actual rows=3000)
  Buffers: shared hit=995 read=2029
Execution Time: 26.105 ms

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` has no index on `"user"` or `team_id`
- `/spend/logs/ui` with `user_id` or `team_id` scans the whole date window
- `/team/spend/by_user` (Usage > Team > Spend Per User) does the same, no row cap
- On a busy proxy both get slower with traffic, not with the user's own usage

How it solves it:

- Resolve the user or team to its api_keys first (indexed lookup)
- Add `api_key = ANY($keys)` so Postgres uses the existing `(api_key, "startTime")` index
- Keys come from `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` / `LiteLLM_DailyTeamSpend` rows in the window plus live keys, so deleted keys still count
- The original `"user"` / `team_id` filter stays, so results are byte-for-byte identical
- No known keys, more than 5000 keys, or a `search` lookup falls back to today's query unchanged
- The key lookup runs under the same 30s statement timeout as the log reads

## User Flow

Before: a proxy admin filtering spend logs to one person on a proxy with months of traffic waits for a full scan of the date range, and on a large table gets a 503

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?client=claude-code and pick a person in the Client Usage panel
2. The panel calls GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui?user_id=...&start_date=...&end_date=...&page_size=1000
3. Postgres walks every spend log in the date range newest first, discarding every row that is not that person's, until it finds 1000
4. On a big table this runs past the 30s statement timeout and the panel shows "Spend logs took longer than 30s. Pick a shorter date range"
5. Same on https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?view=team&team=..., whose "Spend Per User Within Team" card calls GET /team/spend/by_user and sums that team's rows out of a full scan

After: the same clicks return the same numbers, and the work is proportional to that person's or team's own rows

1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/usage?client=claude-code and pick a person in the Client Usage panel
2. The panel calls the same GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui?user_id=... URL
3. Postgres reads only the rows written under that person's keys in the date range and returns the same 1000-row page
4. The team Usage page's "Spend Per User Within Team" card loads the same way, same rows, same totals

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

issue.title: feat(changelog): add ?digest= and ?models= feed views and a subscribe builder on the changelog page
issue.body:
## Summary

The #shipped Slack channel subscribes to `/changelog.xml` through Slack's RSS app, and today's registry audit commit produced 13 separate items, each titled by one model and each ending in a truncated list of raw `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/...` ids. `/changelog.xml?digest=commit` now folds everything one litellm catalog commit changed into a single item, and `?digest=1h` (`30m`, `4h`, `1d`) folds everything that landed in one clock-aligned window, so the channel gets one post per commit or per hour that reads like a release note.

For commit c319616 the digest item is

```
8 models added, 8 updated on 4 providers
• DeepSeek Flash Latest added on Fireworks AI
• GLM Fast Latest added on Fireworks AI
• ...
• Claude Mythos 5.1 on Azure AI Foundry: Web search price added: $0.01 / query, Web search enabled
• +7 more
```

The title counts the models added and updated (a new provider's bullet counts all of its models) and names their providers (or says `N providers` past three). The body has one bullet per model, regional aliases with the same name collapsed to one with their note written once, the notes of a model's price and capability items joined onto its one bullet, and it stops before Slack's 500-character cut (`DIGEST_BODY_LIMIT` 480) with a `+N more` line. A commit with one model yields that model's bullet as the title.

Per commit, the guid is `digest:<sha>` and the link stays the GitHub commit. Per window, the guid is `digest:1h:<window start ISO>`, the `pubDate` is the window's end, and the link is the commit when the window holds one and the changelog page (with the feed's utm tags) when it holds several. A window counts as closed once the changelog's `generatedAt` is past its end, not the wall clock, so a reader that posts an item the first time it sees its guid never posts an hour the next 10-minute build would still add a commit to. With the 5-minute CDN cache on the function, a window shows up 10 to 25 minutes after it closes.

### Following only the models a proxy runs

`?models=azure/gpt-5,claude-opus-4-5` narrows the feed to those models, next to `?kind=` and `?providers=`. Each value is compared by `modelKey`, the slug of its last path segment, and a listing matches on the key of its catalog id, the slug of the whole id, or the slug of its display name, so `azure/gpt-5`, `openai/gpt-5`, `gpt-5` and `GPT-5` all follow the catalog's `gpt-5`, and a proxy's `model:` strings work as they are. A multi-model addition is cut down to the matching listings and its headline recounted, and a new provider narrowed this way becomes a `model` item (`Alpha added on Newco`) rather than claiming the provider arrived with two models.

The `/changelog` page gets a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel (a `<details>` above the filters) that combines all four dimensions: the cadence (`DIGEST_OPTIONS`: every change, per commit, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d), change-type checkboxes, a provider picker with chips, and a textarea for the proxy's models. `parseModelList` takes the JSON of `/model/info` (`litellm_params.model`, falling back to `model_name`) or `/v1/models` (`id`), a `config.yaml` (its `model:` lines), or ids separated by commas, spaces or newlines, and the panel says how many of them changed in the last 30 days. `feedUrl(filter)` renders the URL with `/`, `:` and `@` kept readable, and the panel offers Copy URL and Copy Slack command (`/feed subscribe <url>`). Opening `/changelog?models=...&digest=1h` (any feed parameter) opens the panel prefilled, so a proxy's admin UI can link straight to a feed for its model list.

```ts
// src/changelogPresentation.ts
interface FeedFilter { kinds; providers; models; digest }
feedFilter(params)            // reads ?kind= ?providers= ?models= ?digest=
feedUrl(filter)               // https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?kind=price&models=azure/gpt-5,o3&digest=1h
parseModelList(text)          // ["azure/gpt-5", "vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929"]
filterChangelogItems(items, filter)  // kind, provider, then models (entries narrowed)

// api/changelog.ts
const entries = filter.digest
  ? digestFeedEntries(items, filter.digest, Date.parse(data.generatedAt))
  : items.map(feedEntry);
```

Filters apply before the digest, so `?digest=1h&kind=price&models=gpt-5` folds only GPT-5 price changes. An unknown `digest=` value falls back to the per-change feed. The default feed is unchanged, so existing readers keep their items and guids.

`changelogRss` now takes `FeedEntry[]` (id, link, timestamp, category, title, body) instead of `ChangelogItem[]`, with `feedEntry()` producing today's per-change item. `FeedFilter.digest` is the validated `digest=` token (`""`, `"commit"` or a span). `ChangelogItem` carries `providerName` so the digest can name providers without recomputing them. Two capability flags that fell through to the generic label are named now, so `Supports web search enabled` reads `Web search enabled`, and `supports_tool_choice` reads `Tool choice`.

Tracking: `middleware.ts` adds `digest`, and `models` next to `kind` and `providers`, to the Feed Fetched event when the query asks for them. The panel sends `Changelog Feed Builder Opened`, `Changelog Feed Builder Changed` (digest) and `Changelog Feed Copied` (what, digest, kind, providers, model count), never the pasted text.

To switch the channel over, unsubscribe the current feed and run `/feed subscribe https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?digest=1h` (or `digest=commit`), or build the URL on `/changelog`. Switching the default feed's shape instead would give every existing subscriber a flood of re-posted items, since the guids change.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Default `/changelog.xml` behavior is unchanged; new query params and UI are additive, with broad test coverage on feed shaping and filtering.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends `/changelog.xml` with **`?digest=`** (`commit`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d`) so Slack/RSS readers get one summarized item per catalog commit or clock window (bullets per model, Slack-length cap, open windows held until the build closes them), and **`?models=`** to narrow updates to specific catalog or proxy model ids (matched on last path segment).
> 
> The changelog page adds a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel: digest cadence, change types, providers, pasted proxy JSON/YAML/model lists via `parseModelList`, generated `feedUrl`, and copy-to-Slack support; query params prefill the panel. `changelogPresentation` gains `FeedEntry`, `digestFeedEntries`, model filtering, and `changelogRss` now renders entries instead of raw items; `api/changelog` and middleware apply the new filters and track `digest`/`models`. README documents the feed options; tests cover digest, model filter, and the UI builder.
>

issue.title: fix(router): re-check and reserve per-model rate limits on fallback targets
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

enforce model_rpm_limit and model_tpm_limit on retries and fallbacks

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Per-model TPM/RPM limits are checked once, on the requested model only
- A provider error fallback hands the caller the fallback model unchecked
- The caller can pass a per-model limit of 1 on the fallback model forever

How it solves it:

- New router hook `fallback_rate_limit_check`, next to `fallback_budget_check`
- The proxy wires it to the v3 limiter, which reserves the target model's per-model descriptors
- A fallback target over its per-model limit is skipped, and the error says so
- Same-model retries keep the admission reservation, so no double counting

## User Flow

Before: the caller's per-model limit on the fallback model is never checked when a provider failure triggers the fallback.

1. The admin gives a key `metadata.model_rpm_limit = {"luna": 1}` and configures `fallbacks: [{"opus": ["luna"]}]`
2. The caller sends three `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: opus` while the opus provider is down
3. All three return 200 served by luna, three times the caller's luna allowance

After: the second and later fallbacks into luna are refused.

1. Same key and config
2. The first call falls back to luna and returns 200
3. The second and third calls return the opus provider error with "Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it"

## Relevant issues

Pylon #11530 reported the same gap for key level per-model limits (LIT-10512).

The router settings reference row for `fallback_rate_limit_check` is https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/2909, which the `docs` CI job here needs merged first.

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10554
Resolves LIT-10512

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, two workers sharing one Redis, run from the repo root with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL` exported:

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa/config.yaml --port 4016 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>qa/config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9/v1
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379
  num_retries: 0
  fallbacks: [{"opus": ["luna"]}]

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>leg.sh, the client script (run as `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... ./leg.sh 4016`)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
P=${1:-4016}; S=${2:-main}; H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"; C="Content-Type: application/json"; U=http://127.0.0.1:$P
K=$(curl -s -X POST $U/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"key_alias":"fb-'$S'","metadata":{"model_rpm_limit":{"luna":1}}}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
echo "## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "## call $i to opus"
  curl -s -o /tmp/leg4_body -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST $U/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "$C" -d '{"model":"opus","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi '$i'"}]}'
  python3 -c 'import json;d=json.load(open("/tmp/leg4_body"));print(json.dumps(d.get("error") or {"model": d.get("model"), "content": d["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]})[:300])'
done
echo "## redis counters for the key on luna"
redis-cli --scan --pattern "*model_per_key*luna*" | while read k; do echo "$k = $(redis-cli get "$k" 2>/dev/null)"; done
```

</details>

### Before (3539c0afc9)

1. Start the proxy and run `leg.sh 4016 main`
2. Observed:

```
## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna
## call 1 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 2 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 3 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## redis counters for the key on luna
{model_per_key:8a0e57bd...:luna}:tokens = 90
```

Three fallbacks into luna on a limit of 1, and the only luna counter is the post-call token settlement.

### After (cfc26bbf9a)

1. Start the proxy from this branch and run `leg.sh 4016 after`
2. Observed:

```
## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna
## call 1 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 2 to opus
HTTP 500
{"message": "litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'opus' failed with the error above. Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it.", "type": "internal_server_error", "param": null, "c
## call 3 to opus
HTTP 500
{"message": "litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'opus' failed with the error above. Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it.", "type": "internal_server_error", "param": null, "c
## redis counters for the key on luna
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:tokens = 30
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:requests = 2
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:window = 1794348026
```

The fallback reserves a luna request before it is taken, so the second and third calls are refused and the caller sees why. Only the admitted call settled tokens.

### Tests

A caller-supplied chain with a repeated target (`fallbacks: ["B", "B"]`) reserves B once. Both walks now consult the attempted set before the reserving check, covered by `test_run_async_fallback_reserves_a_repeated_target_once`.

`tests/integration/routing/test_fallback_rate_limit_check.py` boots the proxy with two workers and two scripted upstreams (primary always 500, fallback healthy) and asserts the second fallback is refused. Red on main (second call 200 where the skip was expected), green at the tip. Mutations, each killing one unit test: limiter verdict forced to OK, proxy callback returning True on a limiter error, router ignoring the hook.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- A skipped fallback surfaces the original provider error, not a 429. Mapping it is LIT-10555
- The fallback check reserves the target's request slot and checks its TPM window the way admission does without `LITELLM_TPM_TOKEN_RESERVATION_ENABLED`. It does not reserve the token estimate on the target, because post-call reconciliation still settles against the requested model group and would never refund it. Settling against the model that served the request, and reserving its estimate, is LIT-10513

### Low

- Only the default v3 limiter wires the hook. The legacy limiter (`LEGACY_MULTI_INSTANCE_RATE_LIMITING=true`) is unchanged
- The hook reserves a request slot on the fallback target even when the target then fails

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

Claude Mythos 5.2 on Vertex is handled separately in #50940 and is not touched here.

| model id | gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive | model page differences table "Model ID / gemini-4-carbon / gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive", "Access ... Allowlist only (Fairwind Program)" |

Every other field matches the `vertex_ai/gemini-4-carbon` row above and its quotes (the model page says 4 Carbon for cyber is "a version of Gemini 4 Carbon" that differs only in the table quoted). Model versions page row: `gemini-4-carbon-cyber-permissive | November 10, 2026 | No retirement date announced`, so no `deprecation_date`.

## Notes for the reviewer

- No `*_flex` fields on either row. The pricing page's Gemini 4 section has three tabs, "Standard Model", "Priority" and "Batch", while the Gemini 3 section has "Flex/Batch". issue.title: fix(router): re-check and reserve per-model rate limits on fallback targets
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

enforce model_rpm_limit and model_tpm_limit on retries and fallbacks

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Per-model TPM/RPM limits are checked once, on the requested model only
- A provider error fallback hands the caller the fallback model unchecked
- The caller can pass a per-model limit of 1 on the fallback model forever

How it solves it:

- New router hook `fallback_rate_limit_check`, next to `fallback_budget_check`
- The proxy wires it to the v3 limiter, which reserves the target model's per-model descriptors
- A fallback target over its per-model limit is skipped, and the error says so
- Same-model retries keep the admission reservation, so no double counting

## User Flow

Before: the caller's per-model limit on the fallback model is never checked when a provider failure triggers the fallback.

1. The admin gives a key `metadata.model_rpm_limit = {"luna": 1}` and configures `fallbacks: [{"opus": ["luna"]}]`
2. The caller sends three `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `model: opus` while the opus provider is down
3. All three return 200 served by luna, three times the caller's luna allowance

After: the second and later fallbacks into luna are refused.

1. Same key and config
2. The first call falls back to luna and returns 200
3. The second and third calls return the opus provider error with "Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it"

## Relevant issues

Pylon #11530 reported the same gap for key level per-model limits (LIT-10512).

The router settings reference row for `fallback_rate_limit_check` is https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/2909, which the `docs` CI job here needs merged first.

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10554
Resolves LIT-10512

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, two workers sharing one Redis, run from the repo root with `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL` exported:

```
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa/config.yaml --port 4016 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>qa/config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9/v1
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379
  num_retries: 0
  fallbacks: [{"opus": ["luna"]}]

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>leg.sh, the client script (run as `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... ./leg.sh 4016`)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
P=${1:-4016}; S=${2:-main}; H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"; C="Content-Type: application/json"; U=http://127.0.0.1:$P
K=$(curl -s -X POST $U/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"key_alias":"fb-'$S'","metadata":{"model_rpm_limit":{"luna":1}}}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
echo "## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  echo "## call $i to opus"
  curl -s -o /tmp/leg4_body -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST $U/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $K" -H "$C" -d '{"model":"opus","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi '$i'"}]}'
  python3 -c 'import json;d=json.load(open("/tmp/leg4_body"));print(json.dumps(d.get("error") or {"model": d.get("model"), "content": d["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]})[:300])'
done
echo "## redis counters for the key on luna"
redis-cli --scan --pattern "*model_per_key*luna*" | while read k; do echo "$k = $(redis-cli get "$k" 2>/dev/null)"; done
```

</details>

### Before (3539c0afc9)

1. Start the proxy and run `leg.sh 4016 main`
2. Observed:

```
## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna
## call 1 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 2 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 3 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## redis counters for the key on luna
{model_per_key:8a0e57bd...:luna}:tokens = 90
```

Three fallbacks into luna on a limit of 1, and the only luna counter is the post-call token settlement.

### After (cfc26bbf9a)

1. Start the proxy from this branch and run `leg.sh 4016 after`
2. Observed:

```
## key with model_rpm_limit {luna: 1}; opus is unreachable and falls back to luna
## call 1 to opus
HTTP 200
{"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "content": "hello from luna"}
## call 2 to opus
HTTP 500
{"message": "litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'opus' failed with the error above. Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it.", "type": "internal_server_error", "param": null, "c
## call 3 to opus
HTTP 500
{"message": "litellm.InternalServerError: InternalServerError: OpenAIException - Connection error.\n\nLiteLLM: model group 'opus' failed with the error above. Fallback to luna was skipped because the caller is over its per-model rate limit for it.", "type": "internal_server_error", "param": null, "c
## redis counters for the key on luna
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:tokens = 30
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:requests = 2
{model_per_key:aa623774...:luna}:window = 1794348026
```

The fallback reserves a luna request before it is taken, so the second and third calls are refused and the caller sees why. Only the admitted call settled tokens.

### Tests

A caller-supplied chain with a repeated target (`fallbacks: ["B", "B"]`) reserves B once. Both walks now consult the attempted set before the reserving check, covered by `test_run_async_fallback_reserves_a_repeated_target_once`.

`tests/integration/routing/test_fallback_rate_limit_check.py` boots the proxy with two workers and two scripted upstreams (primary always 500, fallback healthy) and asserts the second fallback is refused. Red on main (second call 200 where the skip was expected), green at the tip. Mutations, each killing one unit test: limiter verdict forced to OK, proxy callback returning True on a limiter error, router ignoring the hook.

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- A skipped fallback surfaces the original provider error, not a 429. Mapping it is LIT-10555
- The fallback check reserves the target's request slot and checks its TPM window the way admission does without `LITELLM_TPM_TOKEN_RESERVATION_ENABLED`. It does not reserve the token estimate on the target, because post-call reconciliation still settles against the requested model group and would never refund it. Settling against the model that served the request, and reserving its estimate, is LIT-10513

### Low

- Only the default v3 limiter wires the hook. The legacy limiter (`LEGACY_MULTI_INSTANCE_RATE_LIMITING=true`) is unchanged
- The hook reserves a request slot on the fallback target even when the target then fails

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

issue.title: feat(changelog): add ?digest= and ?models= feed views and a subscribe builder on the changelog page
issue.body:
## Summary

The #shipped Slack channel subscribes to `/changelog.xml` through Slack's RSS app, and today's registry audit commit produced 13 separate items, each titled by one model and each ending in a truncated list of raw `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/routers/...` ids. `/changelog.xml?digest=commit` now folds everything one litellm catalog commit changed into a single item, and `?digest=1h` (`30m`, `4h`, `1d`) folds everything that landed in one clock-aligned window, so the channel gets one post per commit or per hour that reads like a release note.

For commit c319616 the digest item is

```
8 models added, 8 updated on 4 providers
• DeepSeek Flash Latest added on Fireworks AI
• GLM Fast Latest added on Fireworks AI
• ...
• Claude Mythos 5.1 on Azure AI Foundry: Web search price added: $0.01 / query, Web search enabled
• +7 more
```

The title counts the models added and updated (a new provider's bullet counts all of its models) and names their providers (or says `N providers` past three). The body has one bullet per model, regional aliases with the same name collapsed to one with their note written once, the notes of a model's price and capability items joined onto its one bullet, and it stops before Slack's 500-character cut (`DIGEST_BODY_LIMIT` 480) with a `+N more` line. A commit with one model yields that model's bullet as the title.

Per commit, the guid is `digest:<sha>` and the link stays the GitHub commit. Per window, the guid is `digest:1h:<window start ISO>`, the `pubDate` is the window's end, and the link is the commit when the window holds one and the changelog page (with the feed's utm tags) when it holds several. A window counts as closed once the changelog's `generatedAt` is past its end, not the wall clock, so a reader that posts an item the first time it sees its guid never posts an hour the next 10-minute build would still add a commit to. With the 5-minute CDN cache on the function, a window shows up 10 to 25 minutes after it closes.

### Following only the models a proxy runs

`?models=azure/gpt-5,claude-opus-4-5` narrows the feed to those models, next to `?kind=` and `?providers=`. Each value is compared by `modelKey`, the slug of its last path segment, and a listing matches on the key of its catalog id, the slug of the whole id, or the slug of its display name, so `azure/gpt-5`, `openai/gpt-5`, `gpt-5` and `GPT-5` all follow the catalog's `gpt-5`, and a proxy's `model:` strings work as they are. A multi-model addition is cut down to the matching listings and its headline recounted, and a new provider narrowed this way becomes a `model` item (`Alpha added on Newco`) rather than claiming the provider arrived with two models.

The `/changelog` page gets a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel (a `<details>` above the filters) that combines all four dimensions: the cadence (`DIGEST_OPTIONS`: every change, per commit, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d), change-type checkboxes, a provider picker with chips, and a textarea for the proxy's models. `parseModelList` takes the JSON of `/model/info` (`litellm_params.model`, falling back to `model_name`) or `/v1/models` (`id`), a `config.yaml` (its `model:` lines), or ids separated by commas, spaces or newlines, and the panel says how many of them changed in the last 30 days. `feedUrl(filter)` renders the URL with `/`, `:` and `@` kept readable, and the panel offers Copy URL and Copy Slack command (`/feed subscribe <url>`). Opening `/changelog?models=...&digest=1h` (any feed parameter) opens the panel prefilled, so a proxy's admin UI can link straight to a feed for its model list.

```ts
// src/changelogPresentation.ts
interface FeedFilter { kinds; providers; models; digest }
feedFilter(params)            // reads ?kind= ?providers= ?models= ?digest=
feedUrl(filter)               // https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?kind=price&models=azure/gpt-5,o3&digest=1h
parseModelList(text)          // ["azure/gpt-5", "vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929"]
filterChangelogItems(items, filter)  // kind, provider, then models (entries narrowed)

// api/changelog.ts
const entries = filter.digest
  ? digestFeedEntries(items, filter.digest, Date.parse(data.generatedAt))
  : items.map(feedEntry);
```

Filters apply before the digest, so `?digest=1h&kind=price&models=gpt-5` folds only GPT-5 price changes. An unknown `digest=` value falls back to the per-change feed. The default feed is unchanged, so existing readers keep their items and guids.

`changelogRss` now takes `FeedEntry[]` (id, link, timestamp, category, title, body) instead of `ChangelogItem[]`, with `feedEntry()` producing today's per-change item. `FeedFilter.digest` is the validated `digest=` token (`""`, `"commit"` or a span). `ChangelogItem` carries `providerName` so the digest can name providers without recomputing them. Two capability flags that fell through to the generic label are named now, so `Supports web search enabled` reads `Web search enabled`, and `supports_tool_choice` reads `Tool choice`.

Tracking: `middleware.ts` adds `digest`, and `models` next to `kind` and `providers`, to the Feed Fetched event when the query asks for them. The panel sends `Changelog Feed Builder Opened`, `Changelog Feed Builder Changed` (digest) and `Changelog Feed Copied` (what, digest, kind, providers, model count), never the pasted text.

To switch the channel over, unsubscribe the current feed and run `/feed subscribe https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?digest=1h` (or `digest=commit`), or build the URL on `/changelog`. Switching the default feed's shape instead would give every existing subscriber a flood of re-posted items, since the guids change.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/0d9181069b5e49cb9263b181cb369211?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Default `/changelog.xml` behavior is unchanged; new query params and UI are additive, with broad test coverage on feed shaping and filtering.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends `/changelog.xml` with **`?digest=`** (`commit`, `30m`, `1h`, `4h`, `1d`) so Slack/RSS readers get one summarized item per catalog commit or clock window (bullets per model, Slack-length cap, open windows held until the build closes them), and **`?models=`** to narrow updates to specific catalog or proxy model ids (matched on last path segment).
> 
> The changelog page adds a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel: digest cadence, change types, providers, pasted proxy JSON/YAML/model lists via `parseModelList`, generated `feedUrl`, and copy-to-Slack support; query params prefill the panel. `changelogPresentation` gains `FeedEntry`, `digestFeedEntries`, model filtering, and `changelogRss` now renders entries instead of raw items; `api/changelog` and middleware apply the new filters and track `digest`/`models`. README documents the feed options; tests cover digest, model filter, and the UI builder.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 468a3428ec22b995e2bdd8dc9b329a785a7e0463. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

issue.title: fix(cost-map): sync together_ai together/Tev1-4B-experimental input price with /v1/models
issue.body:
## Summary

Moves together_ai/together/Tev1-4B-experimental input_cost_per_token from 4e-08 to 4.2e-08, the price GET https://api.together.ai/v1/models returns and the one Together's own docs publish. The row's source moves from the marketing pricing page to the models API

## Rows

together_ai/together/Tev1-4B-experimental (changed, kind api)

input_cost_per_token 4.2e-08 and output_cost_per_token 0 come from GET https://api.together.ai/v1/models, id together/Tev1-4B-experimental, pricing.input = 0.042, pricing.output = 0. The serverless models table on https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless-models agrees, "Together AI Tev1 4B Experimental together/Tev1-4B-experimental 32768 $0.042 - Free - - -", as does the September 23, 2026 changelog entry on https://docs.together.ai/docs/changelog, "together/Tev1-4B-experimental : 32,768 context length. Pricing: $0.042 input / free output (per 1M tokens)."

The marketing page https://www.together.ai/pricing shows "Tev1 4B Experimental $0.04 Free", which is where the old 4e-08 came from. Together's docs catalog, changelog and API all carry $0.042, so the row follows them under ruling together-ai-kimi-k3-qwen38-flash-switch-to-published (switch once the published price and /v1/models agree). If the two-decimal marketing figure should win instead, this PR can be closed

## Not changed

The November 5, 2026 changelog entry (moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro, $2.00 input / $10.00 output / $0.20 cached input, 1,048,576 context) already matches the catalog row, and the October 22 deprecations of meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 already carry deprecation_date 2026-10-22 with their successors. The other 78 ids /v1/models prices match the catalog

## Delisted by the provider

together-ai-up-to-4b, together-ai-4.1b-8b, together-ai-8.1b-21b, together-ai-21.1b-41b, together-ai-41.1b-80b, together-ai-81.1b-110b, together-ai-embedding-up-to-150m and together-ai-embedding-151m-to-350m are generic size tier keys that /v1/models never lists, so this is a coverage gap and not a delisting. They are left in place

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Data-only cost-map correction with no runtime or security impact; only affects billing estimates for one Together model.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns **together_ai/together/Tev1-4B-experimental** pricing in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and its backup with Together’s **GET /v1/models** data.
> 
> **input_cost_per_token** moves from `4e-08` to **`4.2e-08`** ($0.042 per 1M tokens). The row’s **source** is updated from the marketing pricing page to **`https://api.together.ai/v1/models`** so LiteLLM cost tracking matches the published API/docs figure instead of the rounded $0.04 on the website.
>

Per window, the guid is `digest:1h:<window start ISO>`, the `pubDate` is the window's end, and the link is the commit when the window holds one and the changelog page (with the feed's utm tags) when it holds several. A window counts as closed once the changelog's `generatedAt` is past its end, not the wall clock, so a reader that posts an item the first time it sees its guid never posts an hour the next 10-minute build would still add a commit to. With the 5-minute CDN cache on the function, a window shows up 10 to 25 minutes after it closes.

### Following only the models a proxy runs

`?models=azure/gpt-5,claude-opus-4-5` narrows the feed to those models, next to `?kind=` and `?providers=`. Each value is compared by `modelKey`, the slug of its last path segment, and a listing matches on the key of its catalog id, the slug of the whole id, or the slug of its display name, so `azure/gpt-5`, `openai/gpt-5`, `gpt-5` and `GPT-5` all follow the catalog's `gpt-5`, and a proxy's `model:` strings work as they are. A multi-model addition is cut down to the matching listings and its headline recounted, and a new provider narrowed this way becomes a `model` item (`Alpha added on Newco`) rather than claiming the provider arrived with two models.

The `/changelog` page gets a **Build a feed for the models you run** panel (a `<details>` above the filters) that combines all four dimensions: the cadence (`DIGEST_OPTIONS`: every change, per commit, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d), change-type checkboxes, a provider picker with chips, and a textarea for the proxy's models. `parseModelList` takes the JSON of `/model/info` (`litellm_params.model`, falling back to `model_name`) or `/v1/models` (`id`), a `config.yaml` (its `model:` lines), or ids separated by commas, spaces or newlines, and the panel says how many of them changed in the last 30 days. `feedUrl(filter)` renders the URL with `/`, `:` and `@` kept readable, and the panel offers Copy URL and Copy Slack command (`/feed subscribe <url>`). Opening `/changelog?models=...&digest=1h` (any feed parameter) opens the panel prefilled, so a proxy's admin UI can link straight to a feed for its model list.

feedFilter(params)            // reads ?kind= ?providers= ?models= ?digest=
feedUrl(filter)               // https://models.litellm.ai/changelog.xml?kind=price&models=azure/gpt-5,o3&digest=1h
parseModelList(text)          // ["azure/gpt-5", "vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929"]
filterChangelogItems(items, filter)  // kind, provider, then models (entries narrowed)

// api/changelog.ts
const entries = filter.digest
  ? digestFeedEntries(items, filter.digest, Date.parse(data.generatedAt))
  : items.map(feedEntry);
```

Tracking: `middleware.ts` adds `digest`, and `models` next to `kind` and `providers`, to the Feed Fetched event when the query asks for them. The panel sends `Changelog Feed Builder Opened`, `Changelog Feed Builder Changed` (digest) and `Changelog Feed Copied` (what, digest, kind, providers, model count), never the pasted text.
