issue.title: feat(openai)!: honor per-deployment workload identity on non-chat routes (#39966) [lts/1.108.x]
issue.body:
## TLDR

Backport of https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/39966 to `lts/1.108.x`. Cherry-picked from `b39eadcb8228e05b76506df78fa2723628494669` on main with the source author kept

Problem this solves:

- On 1.108.x, OpenAI workload identity only applied to chat, responses and image generations
- `/v1/images/edits` on a keyless WIF deployment sent `Authorization: Bearer None` and got a 401
- Same gap on audio, moderations, files, batches, fine tuning, vector stores, videos and realtime
- A partial WIF trio with no static key failed with the same unhelpful 401

How it solves it:

- Every OpenAI route now resolves its bearer token through the same per-deployment WIF resolver
- Partial trio with no static key returns a 401 naming the missing params
- Non-admin callers can no longer smuggle the WIF params through `user_config` or multipart `param[]` fields

Intentional product change: a request from a non-admin key that carries `openai_identity_provider_id`, `openai_service_account_id`, `openai_identity_token_file` (or the Anthropic and OAuth equivalents) inside `user_config` or as a `field[]` multipart key now gets a 401. Those carriers bypassed the existing server-owned param check, so no supported setup loses anything

## User Flow

Before: an operator runs 1.108.x with an `openai/gpt-image-*` deployment that has the WIF trio and no `api_key`, and image edits fail

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations with `{"model": "gpt-image", "prompt": "a red square"}` and get a 200 with an image
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/edits as multipart with `model=gpt-image`, `image=@square.png`, `prompt=make it blue`
3. They get a 401 whose body says `Incorrect API key provided: None`
4. They have to keep a static `OPENAI_API_KEY` around just for image edits

After: the same keyless deployment serves image edits

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/generations and get a 200 with an image
2. They send the same multipart POST https://litellm-domain/v1/images/edits
3. They get a 200 with the edited image, no static key anywhere in the config or the environment

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10596

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Verbatim pick. `diff <(git show b39eadcb82) <(git show 099b914e16)` with index and hunk headers stripped differs in exactly one line, the import block of `tests/unit/proxy/batches_endpoints/test_endpoints.py`, where the LTS file already imported `Final` and the pick adds `Path`

On the worktree at `099b914e16`, `uv run pytest` over the 12 picked test files plus the OpenAI, proxy auth, router types and batches test trees ran 2261 passed, 1 skipped. The picked integration tests (`tests/integration/compatibility/test_audio_transcriptions_wire.py`, `tests/integration/routing/test_user_config_routing.py`) ran through `tests/integration/run.py` and passed. `BASE_REF=origin/lts/1.108.x make check` passed. Grype on the resolved lock is identical to main, no bump needed

Live before and after on this line with placeholder WIF credentials. The real identity provider, service account and signed subject token used for the source PR's QA are not in the shared QA vault, so both legs ran the customer shape with a fake `idp_` id, a fake `sa_` id and an unsigned JWT in the token file, and no `OPENAI_API_KEY` anywhere in the proxy environment. That cannot produce a 200, but it does show which code path each route takes, and the before leg reproduces the reported error byte for byte

<details>
<summary>Config and commands, identical for both legs</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-image
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare
      openai_identity_provider_id: os.environ/OPENAI_WIF_IDP_ID
      openai_service_account_id: os.environ/OPENAI_WIF_SA_ID
      openai_identity_token_file: /home/ubuntu/wifqa/subject_token.jwt
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-wifqa-1234
router_settings:
  disable_cooldowns: true
```

```bash
# in the worktree, OPENAI_WIF_IDP_ID / OPENAI_WIF_SA_ID set to placeholder ids, token file holds an unsigned JWT
env -u OPENAI_API_KEY PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/enterprise:$PWD/litellm-proxy-extras" \
  python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4100
curl -s localhost:4100/v1/images/generations -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-wifqa-1234" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-image","prompt":"a red square","size":"1024x1024"}'
curl -s localhost:4100/v1/images/edits -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-wifqa-1234" \
  -F model=gpt-image -F image=@square.png -F "prompt=make it blue" -F size=1024x1024
```

`disable_cooldowns` is on because the first 401 otherwise puts the single deployment in cooldown and the edits call gets a 429 instead of its own answer. `PYTHONPATH` is set because the shared venv's editable install points at another checkout

</details>

<details>
<summary>Before, lts/1.108.x at 2a56160037</summary>

```text
POST /v1/images/generations -> 401
OpenAIException - The api_key client option must be set either by passing api_key to the client or by setting the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable

POST /v1/images/edits -> 401
OpenAIException - {"error": {"message": "Incorrect API key provided: None. ...", "type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "invalid_api_key"}}

proxy.log lines mentioning Bearer None or Incorrect API key: 2
```

Neither image route reads the deployment trio. Edits sends `Authorization: Bearer None` to OpenAI, which is the reported error

</details>

<details>
<summary>After, this PR at 099b914e16</summary>

```text
POST /v1/images/generations -> 401
OpenAIException - Invalid identity_provider_id for workload identity token exchange.

POST /v1/images/edits -> 401
OpenAIException - Invalid identity_provider_id for workload identity token exchange.

proxy.log lines mentioning Bearer None or Incorrect API key: 0
```

Both routes now read the deployment trio and run the token exchange against `auth.openai.com`, which rejects the placeholder identity provider id as expected. With a real trio this is the point where the exchange returns a bearer token and the request proceeds, which is the flow proven live on #39966

</details>

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Caveats (if any)

### Severe

- Auth change, non-admin `user_config` or `param[]` carriers of WIF params now 401 (see TLDR)

### Medium

- The live run on this line used placeholder WIF credentials, so it proves the routing into the token exchange, not a 200 with an image. The 200 is proven live on #39966 with a real identity provider
- Long running batches via WIF still hit https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/50185, keep a static key for batches

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

+        litellm_call_id="call-stream",
+        function_id="fn",
+    )
+    mock_user_api_key_dict = MagicMock(spec=UserAPIKeyAuth)
+    mock_request_data = {

+        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "test"}],

+    mock_chunks = [

+        {"choices": [{"delta": {"content": " world"}}]},
+        {"choices": [{"delta": {"content": " more"}}]},
+    ]
+
+    mock_proxy_logging_obj = MagicMock(spec=ProxyLogging)

+    async def mock_streaming_iterator(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> AsyncIterator[object]:
+        for chunk in mock_chunks:
+            yield chunk
+
+    async def slow_hook(**kwargs: object) -> object:
+        clock.advance(0.02)
+        return kwargs.get("response")
+
+    mock_proxy_logging_obj.async_post_call_streaming_iterator_hook = mock_streaming_iterator
+    mock_proxy_logging_obj.needs_per_chunk_streaming_hook = MagicMock(return_value=True)
+    mock_proxy_logging_obj.async_post_call_streaming_hook = AsyncMock(side_effect=slow_hook)
+    mock_proxy_logging_obj.post_call_failure_hook = AsyncMock(return_value=None)
comment.body: Fixed in 3bba741b3c, both tests now run a real ProxyLogging with a CustomLogger whose streaming hook advances the fake clock, no doubles on our code.

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Claude Mythos 5.2 on Vertex AI had no cost-map row, so `vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2` fails model lookup and bills $0

How it solves it:

- Adds `vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2` and `vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2@default` as copies of the Vertex Fable 5.2 rows
- $8/$40 per MTok, $10 5m and $16 1h cache writes, $0.20 cache reads, 50% batch, 1.1x regional uplift
- Same 1M context, 128K output, adaptive thinking and 2027-11-09 retirement as the Fable 5.2 rows
- Like the Vertex Fable 5.2 rows, no `fast` multiplier, since the Vertex cost path does not bill fast mode

## User Flow

Before: a Vertex AI user calling Mythos 5.2 through the gateway gets no cost on the request

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2"`

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "vertex_ai/claude-mythos-5-2"`
2. `x-litellm-response-cost` carries the cost at $8/$40 per MTok (1.1x on a regional endpoint)

issue.title: feat(cost-map): add gemini/gemini-4-carbon from the Gemini API pricing page
issue.body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Google released Gemini 4 Carbon (`gemini-4-carbon`) as GA on November 10, 2026 and the catalog has no row for it, so requests to it are not cost tracked

How it solves it:

- Adds `gemini/gemini-4-carbon` with the Standard, Batch, Flex and Priority prices from the Gemini API pricing page, the token limits and capability flags from the model docs, and the implicit cache minimum from the caching docs
- Same edit in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json`

## Rows added

`gemini/gemini-4-carbon`, kind page. The id is not in the list API yet (it still lists only the confidential `gemini-4-carbon-eap` and `gemini-4-carbon-mcdi-eap`), so the row is built from the release note, the pricing page and the model docs, all fetched raw with a cache buster on 2026-11-10. `https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing` now redirects to `https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing`, so that is the url on the row. Every price is the page's per 1M figure divided by 1e6

Release note, https://aistudio.google.com/docs/changelog, November 10, 2026: "Gemini 4 Carbon (`gemini-4-carbon`) generally available (GA) ... available at introductory pricing of $2.00 per 1M input tokens and $10.00 per 1M output tokens through November 30, 2026"

| Field | Value | Evidence | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input_cost_per_token` | 2e-06 | Pricing page, section "Gemini 4 Carbon", Standard tab, "Input price ... $2.00 through November 30, 2026" | page |
| `output_cost_per_token`, `output_cost_per_reasoning_token` | 1e-05 | Standard tab, "Output price (including thinking tokens) ... $10.00 through November 30, 2026" | page |
| `cache_read_input_token_cost` | 1e-07 | Standard tab, "Context caching price ... $0.10 through November 30, 2026. Implicit caching only (explicit caching is not supported)" | page |
| `input_cost_per_token_batches`, `output_cost_per_token_batches`, `cache_read_input_token_cost_batches` | 1e-06, 5e-06, 5e-08 | Batch tab, "Input price ... $1.00", "Output price (including thinking tokens) ... $5.00", "Context caching price ... $0.05" | page |
| `input_cost_per_token_flex`, `output_cost_per_token_flex`, `cache_read_input_token_cost_flex` | 1e-06, 5e-06, 5e-08 | Flex tab, "Input price ... $1.00", "Output price (including thinking tokens) ... $5.00", "Context caching price ... $0.05" | page |
| `input_cost_per_token_priority`, `output_cost_per_token_priority`, `cache_read_input_token_cost_priority` | 3.6e-06, 1.8e-05, 1.8e-07 | Priority tab, "Input price ... $3.60", "Output price (including thinking tokens) ... $18.00", "Context caching price ... $0.18" | page |
| `search_context_cost_per_query` (low, medium, high) and `web_search_billing_unit: per_query` | 0.014 | Standard tab, "Grounding with Google Search ... then $14 per 1,000 requests" | page |
| `google_maps_grounding_cost_per_query` | 0.014 | Standard tab, "Grounding with Google Maps ... then $14 / 1,000 search queries" | page |
| `max_input_tokens` | 1048576 | Model docs https://aistudio.google.com/docs/models/gemini-4-carbon, "Context window (unified input and output token limit) 1,048,576" | page |
| `max_output_tokens` | 1048576 | Model docs, "Max output 65,536 (default synchronous) / up to 1,048,576 (with long decode)". The row takes the long decode ceiling so valid long decode requests are not clamped, the same value and reasoning as `gemini/gemini-4-argon` under ruling `gemini-4-argon-max-output-tokens-wait-long-decode-field` | page |
| `prompt_cache_min_tokens` | 4096 | Caching docs https://aistudio.google.com/docs/caching, implicit caching table, "Gemini 4 Carbon | 4,096" | page |
| `supported_modalities` text, image, audio, video and `supports_vision`, `supports_video_input`, `supports_audio_input`, `supports_pdf_input` true, `supports_audio_output` false, `supported_output_modalities` text | | Model docs, "Inputs Text, Image, Video, Audio, and PDF", "Output Text", "Audio generation ... not supported" | page |
| `supports_function_calling`, `supports_response_schema`, `supports_reasoning`, `supports_web_search`, `supports_url_context`, `supports_computer_use`, `supports_prompt_caching` true | | Model docs capability badges, "Function calling ... supported", "Structured outputs ... supported", "Thinking ... Supported (low, medium, high)", "Grounding with Google Search ... supported", "URL context ... supported", "Computer use ... supported", "Context caching ... Supported (Implicit only)" | page |
| `supports_minimal_reasoning_effort` false | | Model docs, "Thinking ... Supported (low, medium, high)", no minimal level | page |
| `supports_continuation` true | | What's new page https://aistudio.google.com/docs/whats-new-gemini-4-carbon, "Generate past 64K tokens with background execution: Standard synchronous responses stop at 65,536 tokens. To generate longer responses, set `background=True` and raise `max_output_tokens`" | page |
| `mode: chat`, `litellm_provider: gemini`, `supported_endpoints`, `supports_system_messages`, `supports_tool_choice`, `supports_parallel_function_calling`, `supports_native_streaming`, `rpm: 2000`, `tpm: 800000` | | `inherited_from: gemini/gemini-4-argon`. The rate limits page is now spend based and only lists batch enqueued tokens (5,000,000 for Gemini 4 Carbon at Tier 1), it publishes no per model rpm or tpm | inherited |

The pricing page also states "$4.00 starting December 1, 2026" input, "$20.00 starting December 1, 2026" output and doubled Batch, Flex, Priority and caching prices from that date. Those are not pre-staged, per rulings `gemini-price-change-2027-keep-current` and `gemini-4-argon-dec-2026-price-change-keep-current` (the same introductory then doubled schedule on the sibling). The Contributor tab is left out per ruling `gemini-contributor-tier-prices-leave-out`. The deprecations page lists `gemini-4-carbon` with "No shutdown date announced", so no `deprecation_date`

The `prices gemini` command reports no structured price API for this provider, so every value above comes from the quoted pages. The rest of the pricing page matches the catalog's gemini rows, and every dated gemini/ row on the deprecations page already carries that date in the catalog

Other rulings applied: `gemini-4-carbon-eap-leave-out-for-now` and `gemini-4-carbon-mcdi-eap-wait-until-priced` (the two confidential Carbon EAP ids stay out, this row is the separate GA id), `gemini-aqa-leave-out`, `antigravity-leave-out`, `gemini-decision-eap-leave-out-until-priced`, `gemini-chatter-leave-out-until-priced`, `gemini-file-processing-eap-leave-out-until-priced`, `gemini-4-hydrogen-eap-leave-out`, `gemini-delisted-no-date-keep`

## Delisted by the provider

No deprecation date is published for these ids, so their rows are kept unchanged per ruling `gemini-delisted-no-date-keep`: gemini-exp-1206, gemini/gemini-exp-1114, gemini/gemini-gemma-2-27b-it, gemini/gemini-gemma-2-9b-it, gemini/gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview-native-audio-09-2025, gemini/gemma-3-27b-it, gemini/imagen-3.0-fast-generate-001, gemini/imagen-3.0-generate-001, gemini/learnlm-1.5-pro-experimental, gemini/lyria-3.5-clip-preview, gemini/lyria-3.5-pro-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-fast-generate-001, gemini/veo-3.1-generate-001. The three veo-3.1 preview ids (gemini/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-generate-preview, gemini/veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview) already carry deprecation_date 2026-10-22 and successor gemini/gemini-omni-1.2-flash from the deprecations page

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] Cost map only, no code change, no new tests needed

## Type

Cost map update

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Data-only cost map addition with no runtime code changes; mispriced fields could affect billing estimates but not auth or core request handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a new **`gemini/gemini-4-carbon`** catalog row so LiteLLM can cost-track the GA Gemini 4 Carbon model. The same block is duplicated in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json`.
> 
> The row carries **Standard, Batch, Flex, and Priority** per-token pricing (plus reasoning output costs), **implicit context-cache** read pricing and **`prompt_cache_min_tokens` 4096**, **Search/Maps grounding** per-query costs, and **1M-token** input/output limits. Capability flags match the model docs (multimodal input, reasoning, tools, web search, computer use, continuation, etc.), with **rpm/tpm** inherited from the sibling **`gemini/gemini-4-argon`** pattern.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 13be8e883040c8eeb7cd983afc349a645fa02194. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

issue.title: feat(rate-limit): enforce per-customer per-model tpm and rpm limits in the v3 limiter
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

enforce customer model_rpm_limit and model_tpm_limit

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer `model_tpm_limit` and `model_rpm_limit` maps (#50797) are stored but never enforced
- A customer could burn one model's allowance through many keys and replicas unchecked

How it solves it:

- New v3 limiter scope `model_per_end_user` keyed `<customer>:<model group>`
- Reads the maps already loaded on the request's customer budget
- Same Redis sliding window as every other scope, shared across keys, teams and workers
- Actual tokens settle against the same counter after the call
- Models without an entry and other customers are untouched

## User Flow

Before: a customer with a per-model TPM cap keeps getting served past it, whatever key sends the traffic

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `{"user_id": "acme", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 60}}` and gets 200 with the map on the budget
2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 again, now 60 tokens in the window
4. A third call still gets 200, the cap is never applied

After: the second key is refused once the customer's allowance for that model is spent

1. Admin sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new and gets 200
2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and gets 429 `Rate limit exceeded for model_per_end_user: acme:opus. Limit type: tokens. Current limit: 60, Remaining: 30`
4. Customer `globex` on `opus`, and `acme` on `luna` (no entry), still get 200

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10553

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, two uvicorn workers sharing one Redis (`127.0.0.1:6379`) for router state and rate-limit counters, Postgres on `127.0.0.1:5432`, mock responses so no provider spend. Env vars: `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /home/ubuntu/qa/config2.yaml --port 4013 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>config2.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from opus"
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>leg2.sh, the client script run against each build (`./leg2.sh 4013 <suffix>`)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: leg2.sh <port> <suffix>
P=${1:-4013}; S=${2:-main}; H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"; C="Content-Type: application/json"
echo "## customer acme-$S with model_tpm_limit opus=60, customer globex-$S with none; two keys"
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/customer/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d "{\"user_id\":\"acme-$S\",\"model_tpm_limit\":{\"opus\":60}}"; echo
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/customer/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d "{\"user_id\":\"globex-$S\"}"; echo
K1=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"key_alias":"svc-a-'$S'"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
K2=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"key_alias":"svc-b-'$S'"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
call() { # key customer model label
  echo "## $4"
  curl -s -o /tmp/leg2_body -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "$C" -d "{\"model\":\"$3\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],\"max_tokens\":40,\"user\":\"$2\"}"
  python3 -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(open("/tmp/leg2_body"));print(d.get("usage") or d.get("error",{}).get("message"))'
}
call $K1 acme-$S opus "acme via key 1 on opus (first call, reserves ~41 tokens of 60)"
call $K2 acme-$S opus "acme via key 2 on opus (shared allowance, should be 429 after fix)"
call $K1 globex-$S opus "globex via key 1 on opus (own allowance, 200)"
call $K1 acme-$S luna "acme via key 1 on luna (no entry, 200)"
echo "## redis counters for acme"
redis-cli --scan --pattern "*acme-$S*" | sort | while read k; do echo "$k = $(redis-cli get "$k")"; done
```

</details>

### Before (84b0a4297a, main)

The same three `opus` calls for one customer all return 200 and Redis holds no counter keyed on customer plus model.

<details>
<summary>Output</summary>

```
## customer acme with model_tpm_limit opus=60, customer globex with none; two keys
{"user_id":"acme","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":"ff4fe4be-3827-4a9f-a720-af9ffcb192e2","litellm_budget_table":{"budget_id":"ff4fe4be-3827-4a9f-a720-af9ffcb192e2","soft_budget":null,"max_budget":null,"max_parallel_requests":null,"tpm_limit":null,"rpm_limit":null,"tpd_limit":null,"model_max_budget":null,"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":60},"model_rpm_limit":null,"budget_duration":null,"allowed_models":[],"temp_budget_increase":null,"temp_budget_expiry":null,"budget_reset_at":null,"created_at":"2026-11-10T06:26:34.339000Z"},"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
{"user_id":"globex","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":null,"litellm_budget_table":null,"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
## acme via key 1 on opus (first call, reserves ~41 tokens of 60)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## acme via key 2 on opus (shared allowance, should be 429 after fix)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## globex via key 1 on opus (own allowance, 200)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## acme via key 1 on luna (no entry, 200)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## redis counters for acme
spend:end_user:acme = 0.0004635
{end_user:acme}:tokens = 90
```

</details>

### After (0f2402534c, tip 8a9b824ca7)

The tip only reshapes how the settlement target list is built, no behavior change, and the 229 limiter unit tests covering it pass at the tip.

The second key is refused with 429 naming `model_per_end_user: acme:opus`, the other customer and the unconfigured model pass, and Redis shows the shared `{model_per_end_user:acme:opus}` counter written by both workers.

<details>
<summary>Output</summary>

```
## customer acme with model_tpm_limit opus=60, customer globex with none; two keys
{"user_id":"acme","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":"a9b9cc53-8492-4c9a-b952-c88c4453d28b","litellm_budget_table":{"budget_id":"a9b9cc53-8492-4c9a-b952-c88c4453d28b","soft_budget":null,"max_budget":null,"max_parallel_requests":null,"tpm_limit":null,"rpm_limit":null,"tpd_limit":null,"model_max_budget":null,"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":60},"model_rpm_limit":null,"budget_duration":null,"allowed_models":[],"temp_budget_increase":null,"temp_budget_expiry":null,"budget_reset_at":null,"created_at":"2026-11-10T06:27:30.056000Z"},"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
{"user_id":"globex","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":null,"litellm_budget_table":null,"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
## acme via key 1 on opus (first call, reserves ~41 tokens of 60)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## acme via key 2 on opus (shared allowance, should be 429 after fix)
HTTP 429
Rate limit exceeded for model_per_end_user: acme:opus. Limit type: tokens. Current limit: 60, Remaining: 30. Limit resets at: 2026-11-10 06:28:30 UTC

```

</details>

Integration test `tests/integration/management/test_customer_model_limits.py` fails on main (`assert 200 == 429`) and passes at the tip against a real proxy. New integration files first run on main after merge, so this one shows up in the scheduled integration workflow rather than on this PR.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Retries and fallbacks are not re-checked against this scope yet, LIT-10554
- No remaining-allowance headers or metrics for this scope yet, LIT-10556

### Low

- A map keyed by an alias name limits only requests that use that alias, same as key and team maps

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8?variant=devin

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes request gating and usage accounting for customer traffic in a core proxy hook; mis-keying could block legitimate requests, but scope is narrow and well covered by tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> The v3 parallel request limiter now **enforces customer (end-user) per-model RPM/TPM** using a new **`model_per_end_user`** scope keyed as `customer:model group`, reading `end_user_model_*_limit` already attached to the request auth.
> 
> Descriptor construction follows the other model-scoped limits, and **post-call token settlement** registers the same scope via a small refactor that builds model-scoped targets from a shared owner list (including end users).
> 
> **Tests** cover unit RPM sharing across keys per customer, alias bucketing, plus an integration test that asserts 429s when a customer's per-model RPM is exhausted across different API keys.

issue.title: fix(cost): backport usage.seconds billing and the unsized FLAC guard to stable/1.106.x for v1.106.8
issue.body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A FLAC encoded to a pipe has no sample count, libsndfile reports 2**63-1 frames
- The line billed that as 576460752303423.5 seconds, about 43 billion dollars per request
- One such request exhausts the key's budget and blocks every later call
- Duration-billed transcriptions ignored the seconds the provider itself billed

How it solves it:

- `_transcription_duration_for_cost` bills validated `usage.seconds` first, then the measured length, else 0
- `normalized_audio_duration_seconds` rejects bool, non-numbers, negatives, NaN, inf and overflow
- `calculate_request_duration` and the Transcribe passthrough return None for the unknown frame count
- Backport onto stable/1.106.x as v1.106.8, for a customer pinned to v1.106.6

## User Flow

Before: a developer sends a pipe-encoded FLAC through the proxy and their key is dead for the month

1. They POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `file=piped.flac`, `response_format=json` on a key with a 500 dollar budget
2. The transcript comes back 200 with `x-litellm-response-cost: 43234556422.75676` and the spend log row says the same
3. Their next POST to the same URL with a normal 11.5 s file returns 422 `Budget has been exceeded! ... Current cost: 43234556422.758484, Max budget: 500.0`

After: the same request is billed the 12 seconds OpenAI billed and the key keeps working

1. They POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `file=piped.flac`, `response_format=json` on a key with a 500 dollar budget
2. The transcript comes back 200 with `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0009` (12.0 s times 0.000075), and `response_format=text` on the same file bills 0 because neither the provider nor the file states a length

issue.title: fix(cost): backport usage.seconds billing and the unsized FLAC guard to stable/1.106.x for v1.106.8
issue.body:
## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A FLAC encoded to a pipe has no sample count, libsndfile reports 2**63-1 frames
- The line billed that as 576460752303423.5 seconds, about 43 billion dollars per request
- One such request exhausts the key's budget and blocks every later call
- Duration-billed transcriptions ignored the seconds the provider itself billed

How it solves it:

- `_transcription_duration_for_cost` bills validated `usage.seconds` first, then the measured length, else 0
- `normalized_audio_duration_seconds` rejects bool, non-numbers, negatives, NaN, inf and overflow
- `calculate_request_duration` and the Transcribe passthrough return None for the unknown frame count
- Backport onto stable/1.106.x as v1.106.8, for a customer pinned to v1.106.6

## User Flow

Before: a developer sends a pipe-encoded FLAC through the proxy and their key is dead for the month

1. They POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `file=piped.flac`, `response_format=json` on a key with a 500 dollar budget
2. The transcript comes back 200 with `x-litellm-response-cost: 43234556422.75676` and the spend log row says the same
3. Their next POST to the same URL with a normal 11.5 s file returns 422 `Budget has been exceeded! ... Current cost: 43234556422.758484, Max budget: 500.0`

After: the same request is billed the 12 seconds OpenAI billed and the key keeps working

1. They POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `file=piped.flac`, `response_format=json` on a key with a 500 dollar budget
2. The transcript comes back 200 with `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0009` (12.0 s times 0.000075), and `response_format=text` on the same file bills 0 because neither the provider nor the file states a length
3. Their next POST with the normal file returns 200 at 0.0009, the key's spend after seven calls is 0.0059625

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10595

## Backport checklist (simple-backport lane, stable/1.106.x)

Source PR https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/50842 merged on main as `3daeb8daf2` while this backport was being prepared, so the main-first ordering holds.

Commits on this branch, in order, all authored and committed as `devin-ai-integration[bot]`:

- `7cdd73dc4e` fix(cost): bill transcriptions by the seconds the provider reports. Hand port of the #35600 (`ecb8ef5ca8`) and #50727 (`dfb1aac8b1`) helpers, taken from `76539f9156` on the lts/1.108.x backport branch. One conflict, the import block in `litellm/cost_calculator.py`: the source also imported `cost_discount` and `decisions_pricing`, which this line does not have, so only `normalized_audio_duration_seconds`, `as_str_mapping` and `attribute_or_none` were kept. The line lacked `attribute_or_none`, so main's four-line definition was added to `litellm/litellm_core_utils/core_helpers.py` in the same commit
- `7b44a17b39` fix(transcription): treat libsndfile's unknown frame count as no duration, cherry-picked from `e6a0534785`. Conflict: the line had deleted `tests/integration/cost_calculation/cases/openai.py` in favour of `cost_tracking_cases.json`, so the `unsized_flac` case was added to the JSON file instead, with the same `UnsizedFlacUpload` schema and `_unsized_flac_bytes` helper as main. The pick also dropped `from typing import Final` in `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_audio_utils.py` because the line's copy of that file never imported it (main's does), caught by gauntlet-mini and `make check` as F821 and fixed inside this pick
- `e0c600c1d5` refactor(transcription): inline the unknown frame count check, cherry-picked clean from `b6d25f2752`
- `89c7792613` fix(transcription): read the frame count once to keep the type gate flat, cherry-picked clean from `54dcd9230f`
- `ab859d789b` test(transcription): annotate the new passthrough test's locals as Final, cherry-picked clean from `eb0f251b47`
- `8151a3704d` chore(deps): bump oauthlib to 4.0.1, lock-only grype bump
- `0f2dcbd291` bump: version 1.106.8 (v1.106.7 is the newest 1.106 release)

Gates:

- Picked tests and every test file reaching changed code, run with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/enterprise"`: 841 passed. The line tip with its own tests: 825 passed. No pass-to-fail transition
- `ruff check --select F821,F811` on every changed Python file: clean. AST importer scan for dropped module-level names: 0 hits
- `BASE_REF=origin/stable/1.106.x make check`: every gate green except `lint-ruff`, which fails on 13 pre-existing F821 `Final` errors in `tests/unit/integrations/otel/test_otel_v2_components.py`. The untouched line tip fails the same way (`ruff check --config ruff-tests.toml tests` on `25fc8bfefc` reports the same 13), so this PR adds nothing to it
- grype v0.100.0, line vs main `uv.lock`: `oauthlib 4.0.0 -> 4.0.1`. Nothing else to bump, pillow 12.3.0 and tornado 6.5.10 are on main at the same versions and filelock's fix (4.2.1) is outside the line's `filelock<4.0` constraint
- gauntlet-mini (degraded mode, the five lenses run sequentially by the session itself since there is no Agent tool here) at reviewed sha `8151a3704d`, BASE `25fc8bfefc`: SURVIVED after one fix. 5/5 lenses, 1 confirmed finding (the dropped `Final` import above, reproduced with ruff F821, fixed in the owning pick `7b44a17b39` before the push, the fix surface re-checked clean), 4 rejected, 0 flippers unverified. Strongest dissent: whisper-1 cost changes between the legs (0.00115 to 0.0012), rejected because OpenAI's whisper replies now carry `usage.seconds = 12.0` and billing the provider's seconds is sub-claim 1. The bump commit `0f2dcbd291` sits after the reviewed sha and touches only `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`
- Integration harness, `tests/integration/run.py cost` on the four whisper cases of `test_cost_tracking.py` with `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2`: 4 passed on the backport, the new `whisper-next-transcriptions-unsized-flac-no-usage` case fails on the line tip at cost 57646075230.342354

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes)

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Two live proxies against real OpenAI, no mocks. Before is the line tip `25fc8bfefc` from `/tmp/wt_stable_1_106_x_base` on port 4111 with database `bp106_before`. After is `8151a3704d` from `/tmp/wt_stable_1_106_x` on port 4112 with database `bp106_after` (the tip `0f2dcbd291` adds only the version bump). Each proxy had its own empty Postgres database, both shared one dedicated Redis on 127.0.0.1:6390, both ran `--num_workers 2`. With `--reload` both checkouts print `WARNING: "workers" flag is ignored when reloading is enabled`, so `--reload` was dropped and each log shows two `Started server process` PIDs. Rates from the line's cost map: `gpt-transcribe` 0.000075 per second, `whisper-1` 0.0001 per second. `normal.flac` is 11.5 s of espeak speech at 16 kHz, `piped.flac` is `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`, the same audio with STREAMINFO total_samples 0, which libsndfile reports as 9223372036854775807 frames. OpenAI billed both as `usage.seconds = 12.0`.

QA config `/tmp/bp106/qa/qa_config.yaml` (OPENAI_API_KEY and LITELLM_MASTER_KEY come from the environment):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-transcribe
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-transcribe
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
  - model_name: whisper-1
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/whisper-1
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6390

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6390
```

Fixtures, made in `/tmp/bp106/qa`:

`speech.wav` was synthesized with espeak from the sentence "This is a ten second test recording for the LiteLLM transcription billing backport, the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog, and the proxy should bill the seconds the provider reports", then converted with ffmpeg to 16 kHz mono `normal.flac`. The unsized file and the frame counts:

```bash
ffmpeg -loglevel error -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac
python -c "import soundfile as sf; [print(p, len(a), a.samplerate, len(a)/a.samplerate) for p in ('normal.flac','piped.flac') for a in [sf.SoundFile(p)]]"
# normal.flac 184000 16000 11.5
# piped.flac 9223372036854775807 16000 576460752303423.5
```

Databases and Redis:

```bash
createdb -h localhost -U postgres bp106_before; createdb -h localhost -U postgres bp106_after
redis-server --port 6390 --daemonize yes
```

Proxy command, run from each worktree root (DATABASE_URL points at that leg's database, port 4111 for before and 4112 for after):

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/enterprise" LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/bp106_<leg> \
STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True \
python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/bp106/qa/qa_config.yaml --port <port> --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

Driver `/tmp/bp106/qa/repro.sh` (the fresh-key variants only drop cases from the `transcribe` list):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... ./repro.sh <port> <database_url>   (run from the directory holding normal.flac and piped.flac)
PORT=$1; DB=$2; B=http://localhost:$PORT; ALIAS=flac-$PORT-$(date +%s)
q() { psql "$DB" -Atc "$1"; }
KEY=$(curl -s $B/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"max_budget\": 500, \"key_alias\": \"$ALIAS\"}" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
echo "key alias $ALIAS, max_budget 500"
transcribe() {
  local label=$1 model=$2 file=$3 fmt=$4
  local http
  http=$(curl -s -D /tmp/h_$PORT.txt -o /tmp/b_$PORT.txt -w "%{http_code}" $B/v1/audio/transcriptions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -F model=$model -F file=@$file -F response_format=$fmt)
  local cost; cost=$(grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost' /tmp/h_$PORT.txt | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}')
  local callid; callid=$(grep -i '^x-litellm-call-id' /tmp/h_$PORT.txt | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}')
  sleep 6
  local spend; spend=$(q "select spend from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" where request_id='$callid'")
  local keyspend; keyspend=$(curl -s "$B/key/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["info"]["spend"])')
  echo "CASE $label | model=$model file=$file response_format=$fmt | http=$http | x-litellm-response-cost=${cost:-<absent>} | spend_logs.spend=${spend:-<no row>} | key.spend=$keyspend"
  echo "  body: $(head -c 300 /tmp/b_$PORT.txt | tr '\n' ' ')"
}
transcribe 1 gpt-transcribe normal.flac json
transcribe 2 gpt-transcribe normal.flac text
transcribe 3 gpt-transcribe piped.flac json
transcribe 4 gpt-transcribe piped.flac text
transcribe 5 gpt-transcribe normal.flac json
transcribe 6a whisper-1 normal.flac json
transcribe 6b whisper-1 normal.flac verbose_json
transcribe 7 gpt-transcribe normal.flac verbose_json
```


Every row is one `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` on a fresh virtual key with `max_budget: 500`. `cost` is the `x-litellm-response-cost` header, `row` is `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.spend` for that `x-litellm-call-id`, `key` is the key's `spend` in `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` at the end.

| Case | Model, file, response_format | Before (25fc8bfefc) | After (8151a3704d) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | gpt-transcribe, normal.flac, json | 200, cost 0.0008624999999999999 (11.5 s measured), row 0.0008624999999999999 | 200, cost 0.0009 (usage.seconds 12.0), row 0.0009 |
| 2 | gpt-transcribe, normal.flac, text | 200, cost 0.0008624999999999999, row 0.0008624999999999999 | 200, cost 0.0008624999999999999 (measured, text reply has no usage), row 0.0008624999999999999 |
| 3 | gpt-transcribe, piped.flac, json | 200, cost 43234556422.75676, row 43234556422.75676, key then 43234556422.758484 over its 500 budget | 200, cost 0.0009 (usage.seconds 12.0), row 0.0009 |
| 4 | gpt-transcribe, piped.flac, text | on the key from case 3: 422 budget_exceeded. On a fresh key: 200, cost 43234556422.75676, row 43234556422.75676, key 43234556422.75676 | 200, `x-litellm-response-cost` header absent, row 0, key unchanged |
| 5 | gpt-transcribe, normal.flac, json, same key after the piped calls | 422 budget_exceeded, no row | 200, cost 0.0009, row 0.0009 |
| 6a | whisper-1, normal.flac, json | on the case-3 key: 422. On a fresh key: 200, cost 0.00115 (11.5 s measured), row 0.00115 | 200, cost 0.0012000000000000001 (usage.seconds 12.0), row 0.0012 |
| 6b | whisper-1, normal.flac, verbose_json | fresh key: 200, cost 0.00115, row 0.00115, body duration 11.5 | 200, cost 0.0012000000000000001, row 0.0012, body duration 11.5 and usage.seconds 12.0 |
| 7 | gpt-transcribe, normal.flac, verbose_json | 400 from OpenAI, response_format verbose_json is not compatible with gpt-transcribe | 400, same provider error, row 0 |
| key spend at the end | | first key 43234556422.758484, fresh piped-text key 43234556422.75676, whisper key 0.0023 | single key 0.005962499999999999 (sum of the seven billed rows) |


Observations that differ from the brief's expectations. Case 4 on the line's tip only shows the 43 billion cost on a fresh key because case 3 already exhausted the first key. On the backport the text reply for the unsized FLAC bills 0 and the header is absent rather than reading 0 (the line writes the header through the same path for every cost, the DB row records 0). whisper-1 replies from OpenAI now carry `usage: {type: duration, seconds: 12.0}`, so the whisper cost is not unchanged between legs, the after leg bills the provider's 12.0 s (0.0012) where the before leg billed the measured 11.5 s (0.00115). That is the backport doing what it says, bill the seconds the provider reports.

issue.title: feat(rate-limit): enforce per-customer per-model tpm and rpm limits in the v3 limiter
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

enforce customer model_rpm_limit and model_tpm_limit

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer `model_tpm_limit` and `model_rpm_limit` maps (#50797) are stored but never enforced
- A customer could burn one model's allowance through many keys and replicas unchecked

How it solves it:

- New v3 limiter scope `model_per_end_user` keyed `<customer>:<model group>`
- Reads the maps already loaded on the request's customer budget
- Same Redis sliding window as every other scope, shared across keys, teams and workers
- Actual tokens settle against the same counter after the call
- Models without an entry and other customers are untouched

## User Flow

Before: a customer with a per-model TPM cap keeps getting served past it, whatever key sends the traffic

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `{"user_id": "acme", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 60}}` and gets 200 with the map on the budget
2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 again, now 60 tokens in the window
4. A third call still gets 200, the cap is never applied

After: the second key is refused once the customer's allowance for that model is spent

1. Admin sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new and gets 200
2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and gets 429 `Rate limit exceeded for model_per_end_user: acme:opus. Limit type: tokens. Current limit: 60, Remaining: 30`
4. Customer `globex` on `opus`, and `acme` on `luna` (no entry), still get 200

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10553

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, two uvicorn workers sharing one Redis (`127.0.0.1:6379`) for router state and rate-limit counters, Postgres on `127.0.0.1:5432`, mock responses so no provider spend. Env vars: `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /home/ubuntu/qa/config2.yaml --port 4013 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>config2.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from opus"
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>leg2.sh, the client script run against each build (`./leg2.sh 4013 <suffix>`)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: leg2.sh <port> <suffix>
P=${1:-4013}; S=${2:-main}; H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"; C="Content-Type: application/json"
echo "## customer acme-$S with model_tpm_limit opus=60, customer globex-$S with none; two keys"
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/customer/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d "{\"user_id\":\"acme-$S\",\"model_tpm_limit\":{\"opus\":60}}"; echo
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/customer/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d "{\"user_id\":\"globex-$S\"}"; echo
K1=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"key_alias":"svc-a-'$S'"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
K2=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/key/generate -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"key_alias":"svc-b-'$S'"}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])')
call() { # key customer model label
  echo "## $4"
  curl -s -o /tmp/leg2_body -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $1" -H "$C" -d "{\"model\":\"$3\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],\"max_tokens\":40,\"user\":\"$2\"}"
  python3 -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(open("/tmp/leg2_body"));print(d.get("usage") or d.get("error",{}).get("message"))'
}
call $K1 acme-$S opus "acme via key 1 on opus (first call, reserves ~41 tokens of 60)"
call $K2 acme-$S opus "acme via key 2 on opus (shared allowance, should be 429 after fix)"
call $K1 globex-$S opus "globex via key 1 on opus (own allowance, 200)"
call $K1 acme-$S luna "acme via key 1 on luna (no entry, 200)"
echo "## redis counters for acme"
redis-cli --scan --pattern "*acme-$S*" | sort | while read k; do echo "$k = $(redis-cli get "$k")"; done
```

</details>

### Before (84b0a4297a, main)

The same three `opus` calls for one customer all return 200 and Redis holds no counter keyed on customer plus model.

<details>
<summary>Output</summary>

```
## customer acme with model_tpm_limit opus=60, customer globex with none; two keys
{"user_id":"acme","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":"ff4fe4be-3827-4a9f-a720-af9ffcb192e2","litellm_budget_table":{"budget_id":"ff4fe4be-3827-4a9f-a720-af9ffcb192e2","soft_budget":null,"max_budget":null,"max_parallel_requests":null,"tpm_limit":null,"rpm_limit":null,"tpd_limit":null,"model_max_budget":null,"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":60},"model_rpm_limit":null,"budget_duration":null,"allowed_models":[],"temp_budget_increase":null,"temp_budget_expiry":null,"budget_reset_at":null,"created_at":"2026-11-10T06:26:34.339000Z"},"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
{"user_id":"globex","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":null,"litellm_budget_table":null,"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
## acme via key 1 on opus (first call, reserves ~41 tokens of 60)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## acme via key 2 on opus (shared allowance, should be 429 after fix)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## globex via key 1 on opus (own allowance, 200)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## acme via key 1 on luna (no entry, 200)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## redis counters for acme
spend:end_user:acme = 0.0004635
{end_user:acme}:tokens = 90
```

</details>

### After (0f2402534c, tip 8a9b824ca7)

The tip only reshapes how the settlement target list is built, no behavior change, and the 229 limiter unit tests covering it pass at the tip.

The second key is refused with 429 naming `model_per_end_user: acme:opus`, the other customer and the unconfigured model pass, and Redis shows the shared `{model_per_end_user:acme:opus}` counter written by both workers.

<details>
<summary>Output</summary>

```
## customer acme with model_tpm_limit opus=60, customer globex with none; two keys
{"user_id":"acme","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":"a9b9cc53-8492-4c9a-b952-c88c4453d28b","litellm_budget_table":{"budget_id":"a9b9cc53-8492-4c9a-b952-c88c4453d28b","soft_budget":null,"max_budget":null,"max_parallel_requests":null,"tpm_limit":null,"rpm_limit":null,"tpd_limit":null,"model_max_budget":null,"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":60},"model_rpm_limit":null,"budget_duration":null,"allowed_models":[],"temp_budget_increase":null,"temp_budget_expiry":null,"budget_reset_at":null,"created_at":"2026-11-10T06:27:30.056000Z"},"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
{"user_id":"globex","blocked":false,"alias":null,"spend":0.0,"allowed_model_region":null,"default_model":null,"models":[],"budget_id":null,"litellm_budget_table":null,"object_permission_id":null,"object_permission":null}
## acme via key 1 on opus (first call, reserves ~41 tokens of 60)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## acme via key 2 on opus (shared allowance, should be 429 after fix)
HTTP 429
Rate limit exceeded for model_per_end_user: acme:opus. Limit type: tokens. Current limit: 60, Remaining: 30. Limit resets at: 2026-11-10 06:28:30 UTC
## globex via key 1 on opus (own allowance, 200)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## acme via key 1 on luna (no entry, 200)
HTTP 200
{'completion_tokens': 20, 'prompt_tokens': 10, 'total_tokens': 30}
## redis counters for acme
spend:end_user:acme = 0.0002385
{end_user:acme}:tokens = 60
{model_per_end_user:acme:luna}:tokens = 30
{model_per_end_user:acme:opus}:tokens = 30
{model_per_end_user:acme:opus}:window = 1794292050
```

</details>

Integration test `tests/integration/management/test_customer_model_limits.py` fails on main (`assert 200 == 429`) and passes at the tip against a real proxy. New integration files first run on main after merge, so this one shows up in the scheduled integration workflow rather than on this PR.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Retries and fallbacks are not re-checked against this scope yet, LIT-10554
- No remaining-allowance headers or metrics for this scope yet, LIT-10556

### Low

- A map keyed by an alias name limits only requests that use that alias, same as key and team maps

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

> Changes request gating and usage accounting for customer traffic in a core proxy hook; mis-keying could block legitimate requests, but scope is narrow and well covered by tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> The v3 parallel request limiter now **enforces customer (end-user) per-model RPM/TPM** using a new **`model_per_end_user`** scope keyed as `customer:model group`, reading `end_user_model_*_limit` already attached to the request auth.
>

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes request gating and usage accounting for customer traffic in a core proxy hook; mis-keying could block legitimate requests, but scope is narrow and well covered by tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> The v3 parallel request limiter now **enforces customer (end-user) per-model RPM/TPM** using a new **`model_per_end_user`** scope keyed as `customer:model group`, reading `end_user_model_*_limit` already attached to the request auth.

issue.title: fix(cost): backport usage.seconds billing and the unsized FLAC guard to lts/1.108.x
issue.body:
## TLDR Backport of the transcription billing fix to `lts/1.108.x`. The main side is #35600, #50727 (the `usage.seconds` slice, hand-ported as one commit) and #50842 (the unsized FLAC guard, picked as its four commits). #50842 has merged on main. Problem this solves: - A FLAC encoded to a pipe has no sample count in its header - libsndfile reports 2**63 - 1 frames for it, so one request bills $43,234,556,422.76 - The key is then over budget and every later request fails with 422 - On this line that hits both `json` and `text` responses How it solves it: - Transcriptions bill the provider's `usage.seconds` first when it is a valid positive number - Otherwise the measured length, otherwise 0 - An unknown frame count is treated as no duration, not as 576 trillion seconds - The Amazon Transcribe passthrough duration helper gets the same guard ## User Flow Before: a developer who transcribes a FLAC that was encoded to a pipe is billed about $43 billion for one request, and the key stops working 1. They run `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`, which writes a FLAC with no sample count in its header 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `response_format=json` and `piped.flac`, and get 200 with the transcript 3. The response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 43234556422.75676` and the key's spend jumps to the same amount against its $500 budget 4. Their next POST on that key, with any file, returns 422 `Budget has been exceeded! ... Current cost: 43234556422.76061, Max budget: 500.0` After: the same request bills the 11 seconds OpenAI reports, and the key keeps working 1. They run `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`, which writes a FLAC with no sample count in its header 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `response_format=json` and `piped.flac`, and get 200 with the transcript 3. The response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0008249999999999999` (11 s x $0.000075) and the key's spend rises by that amount. With `response_format=text` there is no `usage`, so that request bills $0 and carries no cost header 4. Their next POST on that key with `normal.flac` returns 200 and bills $0.000825 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-10595 ## Backport checklist - Line `lts/1.108.x`, base `2a56160037` (v1.108.4 + 11). No LiteLLM version bump on the LTS line, `enterprise/` and `litellm-proxy-extras/` untouched so no subpackage bump - `76539f9156` `fix(cost): bill transcriptions by the seconds the provider reports`, hand-ported slice of #35600 and #50727, clean - `70f388a8ab` `fix(transcription): treat libsndfile's unknown frame count as no duration`, cherry-pick of e6a0534785, adapted to the line: the line's `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_audio_utils.py` lacks main's `from typing import Final`, so `make check` (ruff on the test tree) reported F821 on the new `streaminfo: Final`. The import was added inside this pick - `3f50c8734e` `refactor(transcription): inline the unknown frame count check`, cherry-pick of b6d25f2752, clean - `0e5241c504` `fix(transcription): read the frame count once to keep the type gate flat`, cherry-pick of 54dcd9230f, clean - `0633730678` `test(transcription): annotate the new passthrough test's locals as Final`, cherry-pick of eb0f251b47, clean - Picked tests green on the line: 825 passed across the 10 unit test files that reach the changed code, with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/enterprise"`. No pass-to-fail transition against the line tip - `BASE_REF=origin/lts/1.108.x make check`: PASS at the tip (the first run at the pre-fix tip failed only on the F821 above) - `ruff check --select F821,F811` on the changed `litellm/` files clean, scoped `ruff format --check` clean, AST importer scan found no dropped module-level name - grype v0.100.0 on the line's `uv.lock` vs main's: nothing to bump. Every finding (pillow 12.3.0, dnspython 2.8.0, filelock 3.20.3, tornado 6.5.10) is at the same version on main, and the one line-only finding, diskcache 5.6.3 GHSA-w8v5-vhqr-4h9v, has no fixed release - gauntlet-mini (degraded mode, 5 lenses run by hand, no Agent tool): CONFIRMED, 5/5 lenses clear, 1 finding (the missing `Final` import) reproduced by running ruff on the test tree and fixed inside its pick, 0 dissent. Identifiers resolve on the line, picked tests pass, no line-only caller of `_transcription_duration_for_cost`, `calculate_request_duration` or `media_file_seconds` breaks (`main.py` guards `None`, the Azure speech handler does `or 0.0`, the Transcribe handler already routes `None` to its max-job-cost path) - Integration harness on the line, `python tests/integration/run.py cost --workers 2` with the three whisper cases `whisper-next-transcriptions-per-second`, `whisper-next-transcriptions-unsized-flac-no-usage`, `whisper-verbose-next-transcriptions-duration`: 3 passed ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs ran against a live proxy with real OpenAI `gpt-transcribe` and `whisper-1` calls, Postgres, one dedicated Redis on port 6390 and two workers. Each leg had its own empty database. The line prints `"workers" flag is ignored when reloading is enabled` and starts one worker with `--reload`, so both proxies ran without `--reload` and each logged two `Started server process` lines. Proxy command, run from a checkout of each commit, port 4111 for Before and 4112 for After. Env vars set were `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL` and `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`. ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port 4111 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver ``` `qa_config.yaml` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-transcribe litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-transcribe api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: whisper-1 litellm_params: model: openai/whisper-1 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 6390 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6390 ``` `normal.flac` is 11.000 s of real speech (OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts` wav, `ffmpeg -ar 16000 -ac 1`), `piped.flac` is `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`. soundfile reads `normal.flac` as 176000 frames at 16 kHz and `piped.flac` as 9223372036854775807 frames. Rates from this line's cost map: `gpt-transcribe` $0.000075/s, `whisper-1` $0.0001/s, so 11 s is $0.000825 and $0.0011. Key A (`max_budget: 500`) runs cases 1, 2, 6a, 6b, 7, 3, 5a in that order. Key B (fresh, `max_budget: 500`) runs 4 then 5b, so the text case is not masked by key A already being over budget on Before. Each row reads status, `x-litellm-response-cost`, the `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row's `spend`, and the key's `spend` from `/key/info`. | Case | Before (2a56160037) | After (0633730678) | |---|---|---| | 1. normal.flac, gpt-transcribe, json | 200, 0.000825, 0.000825, 0.000825 | 200, 0.000825, 0.000825, 0.000825 | | 2. normal.flac, gpt-transcribe, text | 200, 0.000825, 0.000825, 0.00165 | 200, 0.000825, 0.000825, 0.00165 | | 6a. normal.flac, whisper-1, json | 200, 0.0011, 0.0011, 0.00275 | 200, 0.0011, 0.0011, 0.00275 | | 6b. normal.flac, whisper-1, verbose_json | 200, 0.0011, 0.0011, 0.00385 | 200, 0.0011, 0.0011, 0.00385 | | 7. normal.flac, gpt-transcribe, verbose_json | 400 from OpenAI, `verbose_json` is not compatible with `gpt-transcribe`, no header, failure row 0, 0.00385 | same 400, no header, failure row 0, 0.00385 | | 3. piped.flac, gpt-transcribe, json | 200, 43234556422.75676, 43234556422.75676, 43234556422.76061 | 200, 0.000825, 0.000825, 0.004675 | | 5a. normal.flac, gpt-transcribe, json, key A after 3 | 422 budget exceeded, no header, failure row 0, 43234556422.76061 | 200, 0.000825, 0.000825, 0.0055 | | 4. piped.flac, gpt-transcribe, text, key B | 200, 43234556422.75676, 43234556422.75676, 43234556422.75676 | 200, header absent, success row 0, 0.0 | | 5b. normal.flac, gpt-transcribe, json, key B after 4 | 422 budget exceeded, no header, failure row 0, 43234556422.75676 | 200, 0.000825, 0.000825, 0.000825 |

Observed live: the header is absent, because `proxy_server.py` already passes `hidden_params.get("response_cost") or ""` into the header builder here. Same user-visible result as main - The Transcribe passthrough change is covered by a unit test only, with no live AWS run (carried from #50842) - That path charges such a file as the longest media AWS accepts, as it does for unreadable media - `gpt-transcribe` rejects `response_format=verbose_json` upstream (400), so that case could not be billed on either leg ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/46b12279387447c08b2cc007358bb400 Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/46b12279387447c08b2cc007358bb400?variant=devin Requested by: @kerry-berri --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes spend-tracking and budget enforcement for transcription and Transcribe passthrough; incorrect duration logic could under- or over-charge, though the fix tightens validation and adds regression tests. > > **Overview** > Fixes transcription spend that could treat **pipe-encoded FLAC** (no sample count in the header) as billions of seconds when libsndfile reports `2**63 - 1` frames, blowing API key budgets. > > **Transcription billing** now resolves billable seconds via `_transcription_duration_for_cost`: prefer validated provider `usage.type=duration` / `usage.seconds`, then measured duration from `_hidden_params` or response `duration`, else **0**. Malformed seconds (negative, NaN, inf, overflow) are dropped through `normalized_audio_duration_seconds`. > > **Duration probing** in `calculate_request_duration` and Amazon Transcribe passthrough `media_file_seconds` returns **no duration** when frame count is at or above `LIBSNDFILE_UNKNOWN_FRAME_COUNT`, so cost/logging does not infer length from unknown headers. > > Integration and unit tests cover unsized FLAC ($0 spend), provider-reported seconds over measured length, and the passthrough path. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 06337306783f1972f7b749768b03a1c2df6d52c5. issue.title: fix(cost): backport usage.seconds billing and the unsized FLAC guard to lts/1.108.x
issue.body:
## TLDR Backport of the transcription billing fix to `lts/1.108.x`. The main side is #35600, #50727 (the `usage.seconds` slice, hand-ported as one commit) and #50842 (the unsized FLAC guard, picked as its four commits). #50842 has merged on main. Problem this solves: - A FLAC encoded to a pipe has no sample count in its header - libsndfile reports 2**63 - 1 frames for it, so one request bills $43,234,556,422.76 - The key is then over budget and every later request fails with 422 - On this line that hits both `json` and `text` responses How it solves it: - Transcriptions bill the provider's `usage.seconds` first when it is a valid positive number - Otherwise the measured length, otherwise 0 - An unknown frame count is treated as no duration, not as 576 trillion seconds - The Amazon Transcribe passthrough duration helper gets the same guard ## User Flow Before: a developer who transcribes a FLAC that was encoded to a pipe is billed about $43 billion for one request, and the key stops working 1. They run `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`, which writes a FLAC with no sample count in its header 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `response_format=json` and `piped.flac`, and get 200 with the transcript 3. The response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 43234556422.75676` and the key's spend jumps to the same amount against its $500 budget 4. Their next POST on that key, with any file, returns 422 `Budget has been exceeded! ... Current cost: 43234556422.76061, Max budget: 500.0` After: the same request bills the 11 seconds OpenAI reports, and the key keeps working 1. They run `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`, which writes a FLAC with no sample count in its header 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `response_format=json` and `piped.flac`, and get 200 with the transcript 3. The response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 0.0008249999999999999` (11 s x $0.000075) and the key's spend rises by that amount. With `response_format=text` there is no `usage`, so that request bills $0 and carries no cost header 4. Their next POST on that key with `normal.flac` returns 200 and bills $0.000825 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-10595 ## Backport checklist - Line `lts/1.108.x`, base `2a56160037` (v1.108.4 + 11). No LiteLLM version bump on the LTS line, `enterprise/` and `litellm-proxy-extras/` untouched so no subpackage bump - `76539f9156` `fix(cost): bill transcriptions by the seconds the provider reports`, hand-ported slice of #35600 and #50727, clean - `70f388a8ab` `fix(transcription): treat libsndfile's unknown frame count as no duration`, cherry-pick of e6a0534785, adapted to the line: the line's `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_audio_utils.py` lacks main's `from typing import Final`, so `make check` (ruff on the test tree) reported F821 on the new `streaminfo: Final`. The import was added inside this pick - `3f50c8734e` `refactor(transcription): inline the unknown frame count check`, cherry-pick of b6d25f2752, clean - `0e5241c504` `fix(transcription): read the frame count once to keep the type gate flat`, cherry-pick of 54dcd9230f, clean - `0633730678` `test(transcription): annotate the new passthrough test's locals as Final`, cherry-pick of eb0f251b47, clean - Picked tests green on the line: 825 passed across the 10 unit test files that reach the changed code, with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/enterprise"`. No pass-to-fail transition against the line tip - `BASE_REF=origin/lts/1.108.x make check`: PASS at the tip (the first run at the pre-fix tip failed only on the F821 above) - `ruff check --select F821,F811` on the changed `litellm/` files clean, scoped `ruff format --check` clean, AST importer scan found no dropped module-level name - grype v0.100.0 on the line's `uv.lock` vs main's: nothing to bump. Every finding (pillow 12.3.0, dnspython 2.8.0, filelock 3.20.3, tornado 6.5.10) is at the same version on main, and the one line-only finding, diskcache 5.6.3 GHSA-w8v5-vhqr-4h9v, has no fixed release - gauntlet-mini (degraded mode, 5 lenses run by hand, no Agent tool): CONFIRMED, 5/5 lenses clear, 1 finding (the missing `Final` import) reproduced by running ruff on the test tree and fixed inside its pick, 0 dissent. Identifiers resolve on the line, picked tests pass, no line-only caller of `_transcription_duration_for_cost`, `calculate_request_duration` or `media_file_seconds` breaks (`main.py` guards `None`, the Azure speech handler does `or 0.0`, the Transcribe handler already routes `None` to its max-job-cost path) - Integration harness on the line, `python tests/integration/run.py cost --workers 2` with the three whisper cases `whisper-next-transcriptions-per-second`, `whisper-next-transcriptions-unsized-flac-no-usage`, `whisper-verbose-next-transcriptions-duration`: 3 passed ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs ran against a live proxy with real OpenAI `gpt-transcribe` and `whisper-1` calls, Postgres, one dedicated Redis on port 6390 and two workers. Each leg had its own empty database. The line prints `"workers" flag is ignored when reloading is enabled` and starts one worker with `--reload`, so both proxies ran without `--reload` and each logged two `Started server process` lines. Proxy command, run from a checkout of each commit, port 4111 for Before and 4112 for After. Env vars set were `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL` and `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`. ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port 4111 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver ``` `qa_config.yaml` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-transcribe litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-transcribe api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: whisper-1 litellm_params: model: openai/whisper-1 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 6390 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6390 ``` `normal.flac` is 11.000 s of real speech (OpenAI `gpt-4o-mini-tts` wav, `ffmpeg -ar 16000 -ac 1`), `piped.flac` is `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`. soundfile reads `normal.flac` as 176000 frames at 16 kHz and `piped.flac` as 9223372036854775807 frames. Rates from this line's cost map: `gpt-transcribe` $0.000075/s, `whisper-1` $0.0001/s, so 11 s is $0.000825 and $0.0011. Key A (`max_budget: 500`) runs cases 1, 2, 6a, 6b, 7, 3, 5a in that order. Key B (fresh, `max_budget: 500`) runs 4 then 5b, so the text case is not masked by key A already being over budget on Before. Malformed seconds (negative, NaN, inf, overflow) are dropped through `normalized_audio_duration_seconds`. > > **Duration probing** in `calculate_request_duration` and Amazon Transcribe passthrough `media_file_seconds` returns **no duration** when frame count is at or above `LIBSNDFILE_UNKNOWN_FRAME_COUNT`, so cost/logging does not infer length from unknown headers. > > Integration and unit tests cover unsized FLAC ($0 spend), provider-reported seconds over measured length, and the passthrough path. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 06337306783f1972f7b749768b03a1c2df6d52c5.
