issue.title: fix(completion): backport the hosted tool_choice fix to lts/1.108.x on top of #50726
issue.body:
## TLDR

Stacked on #50726 (base branch `litellm_backport_allowed_tools_tool_choice_lts_1_108_x`). It must merge after #50726 and gets retargeted to `lts/1.108.x` once that lands. It edits `allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`, which #50726 brings to the line

Problem this solves:

- `litellm.completion` rejected `tool_choice={"type": "web_search"}` with 400 "Invalid tool choice" before any provider call
- The Responses API already accepted that choice, so chat callers on the line could not force a hosted tool
- Anthropic silently dropped the dict and Bedrock sent a tool named "", so a forced hosted tool had no clear error elsewhere

How it solves it:

- Backport of #50578 (squash 7e6479b3a0 on main), one pick commit
- `validate_chat_completion_tool_choice` lets a hosted type through unchanged
- `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported` gives a 400 naming the provider gate off OpenAI, Azure and litellm_proxy
- `drop_params` does not drop it, since that would let the model answer without the tool the request required

## User Flow

Before: a developer who wants the model to search the web gets a 400 before anything reaches OpenAI

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `tools=[{"type": "web_search"}, a function tool]` and `tool_choice={"type": "web_search"}`
2. They get 400 "Invalid tool choice, tool_choice={'type': 'web_search'}. Please ensure tool_choice follows the OpenAI spec"
3. Sending the same choice to an Anthropic model gets the same generic 400

After: the same request runs the web search on OpenAI and gets a clear gate error elsewhere

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions
2. They get 200 with a text answer carrying url annotations and `x-litellm-response-cost` above zero
3. Sending the same choice to an Anthropic model gets 400 "tool_choice type 'web_search' forces an OpenAI hosted tool and is only supported for azure, litellm_proxy, openai"

## Backport checklist

Pick `ff68ba4c2f`, author Kerry Lu, committer devin-ai-integration[bot], body "Backport of #50578 to lts/1.108.x. Cherry-picked from 7e6479b3a0 (main)". No extra adaptation commits were needed, every adaptation is inside the conflict resolution. No litellm version bump (LTS line) and no `enterprise/` or `litellm-proxy-extras/` bump, both are untouched

`git cherry-pick -n 7e6479b3a0` conflicted in five files, resolved the way main has it, using the line's helper names from #50726

- `litellm/litellm_core_utils/allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`: added `HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_TYPES`, `hosted_tool_choice_type` and `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported`, kept the line's `parse_allowed_tools_tool_choice` family and did not pull in main's `parse_chat_allowed_tools_tool_choice`
- `litellm/main.py`: kept the line's import of `drops_unsupported_allowed_tools_tool_choice` and `parse_allowed_tools_tool_choice`, added `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported`, which is called right after the line's `drops_unsupported_allowed_tools_tool_choice` call in `completion`
- `litellm/utils.py`: added `HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_TYPES` to the line's import list, and the condition in `validate_chat_completion_tool_choice` became `if not forces_hosted_tool and (tool_choice_type is None or tool_choice.get("function") is None)`. Main also has `tool_choice_type != "allowed_tools"` there, the line handles `allowed_tools` earlier in the same function so that clause does not exist here
- `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`: kept the line's imports and tests, added `hosted_tool_choice_type` and `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported` plus the hosted tests
- `tests/unit/test_main.py`: kept the line's `allowed_tools` tests, appended the hosted tests. `tests/unit/test_utils.py`, the responses transformation test and `tests/integration/providers/test_hosted_tool_choice_wire.py` applied clean

Gates, all from the worktree with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/enterprise"`

- Picked tests (`test_allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`, `test_utils.py`, `test_main.py`, `test_litellm_completion_responses.py`): 1531 collected, 0 failed on the pick, 1503 collected, 0 failed on the base tip 185dc2dca6. No pass-to-fail
- Ten test files of line-only callers of the changed helpers (responses mcp handlers, agentic loop, tool_loop, azure gpt transformation, code interpreter handler, responses bridge): 280 passed on both the pick and the base
- `tests/integration/providers/test_hosted_tool_choice_wire.py` through `tests/integration/run.py providers` with `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2` and Postgres: 4 passed on the pick, 4 failed on the base with only the test file checked out (400 "Invalid tool choice")
- `ruff check --select F821,F811` on the three changed `litellm/` files: clean. `ruff format --check` on them: clean (the repo formats with ruff, `tests/` is excluded by `ruff.toml` on the base as well). The skill's ast importer scan found no dropped name reached by any file on the line
- Mutation: emptying `HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_TYPES` turns 19 of the hosted tests red, restoring turns them green
- `BASE_REF=origin/litellm_backport_allowed_tools_tool_choice_lts_1_108_x make check`: the strict ruff, LIT, TQ and OA gates all report no rule grew past the merge-base. The run ends FAIL on `lint-ruff` with one F811 (duplicate `ScriptedBedrockInvoke`) in `tests/unit/llms/bedrock/messages/invoke_transformations/test_anthropic_claude3_transformation.py`, a file this PR does not touch and which is red the same way on the base tip
- grype v0.100.0 (checksum verified) on the worktree vs main: 98 rows vs 97. The only line-only finding is GHSA-w8v5-vhqr-4h9v in diskcache 5.6.3 (optional `caching` extra, state not-fixed, no fixed release exists, main no longer locks diskcache). Nothing to bump, and it predates this PR on the base branch
- gauntlet-mini: SURVIVED | degraded mode, no Agent tool, 5 lenses run by hand (conflict resolution vs main, identifiers and imports, picked tests plus mutation, line-only callers, live wire and proxy) | BASE 185dc2dca6 HEAD ff68ba4c2f | 0 verified refutations | rejected candidates: `file_search` answering 404 after the pick (the request now reaches OpenAI, which rejects the placeholder vector store id), and the `make check` lint red (pre-existing on the base)

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Two proxies, each with its own empty Postgres database and its own Redis, started with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config <config> --port <port> --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver --detailed_debug`. Before runs the base tip 185dc2dca6 on port 4100, After runs this branch at ff68ba4c2f on port 4200. Config has `gpt-5.6` as `openai/gpt-5.6` and `claude-sonnet-5-5` as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (newest Sonnet in the cost map), master key in `general_settings`, `router_settings.redis_host` and `redis_port` pointing at that leg's Redis. Real provider calls, real spend, no mocks

Each case is one `client.chat.completions.with_raw_response.create(model=..., messages=..., tools=..., tool_choice=...)` through the OpenAI python SDK with `base_url=http://localhost:<port>/v1`. Hosted cases use `tools=[{"type": "<hosted>"}, get_time function tool]` and the question "What is the top headline on the BBC News front page right now?". Function, required, allowed_tools and invalid cases use `tools=[get_time]` and "What time is it in Paris?". The `allowed_tools` choice is `{"type": "allowed_tools", "mode": "auto", "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "get_time"}]}` from the #50726 proof. The `file_search` case sends `{"type": "file_search", "vector_store_ids": ["vs_does_not_exist"]}` and runs last, since its provider error puts the deployment in cooldown. issue.title: fix(completion): backport the hosted tool_choice fix to lts/1.108.x on top of #50726
issue.body:
## TLDR

Stacked on #50726 (base branch `litellm_backport_allowed_tools_tool_choice_lts_1_108_x`). It must merge after #50726 and gets retargeted to `lts/1.108.x` once that lands. It edits `allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`, which #50726 brings to the line

Problem this solves:

- `litellm.completion` rejected `tool_choice={"type": "web_search"}` with 400 "Invalid tool choice" before any provider call
- The Responses API already accepted that choice, so chat callers on the line could not force a hosted tool
- Anthropic silently dropped the dict and Bedrock sent a tool named "", so a forced hosted tool had no clear error elsewhere

How it solves it:

- Backport of #50578 (squash 7e6479b3a0 on main), one pick commit
- `validate_chat_completion_tool_choice` lets a hosted type through unchanged
- `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported` gives a 400 naming the provider gate off OpenAI, Azure and litellm_proxy
- `drop_params` does not drop it, since that would let the model answer without the tool the request required

## User Flow

Before: a developer who wants the model to search the web gets a 400 before anything reaches OpenAI

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `tools=[{"type": "web_search"}, a function tool]` and `tool_choice={"type": "web_search"}`
2. They get 400 "Invalid tool choice, tool_choice={'type': 'web_search'}. Please ensure tool_choice follows the OpenAI spec"
3. Sending the same choice to an Anthropic model gets the same generic 400

After: the same request runs the web search on OpenAI and gets a clear gate error elsewhere

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions
2. They get 200 with a text answer carrying url annotations and `x-litellm-response-cost` above zero
3. Sending the same choice to an Anthropic model gets 400 "tool_choice type 'web_search' forces an OpenAI hosted tool and is only supported for azure, litellm_proxy, openai"

## Backport checklist

Pick `ff68ba4c2f`, author Kerry Lu, committer devin-ai-integration[bot], body "Backport of #50578 to lts/1.108.x. Cherry-picked from 7e6479b3a0 (main)". No extra adaptation commits were needed, every adaptation is inside the conflict resolution. No litellm version bump (LTS line) and no `enterprise/` or `litellm-proxy-extras/` bump, both are untouched

`git cherry-pick -n 7e6479b3a0` conflicted in five files, resolved the way main has it, using the line's helper names from #50726

- `litellm/litellm_core_utils/allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`: added `HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_TYPES`, `hosted_tool_choice_type` and `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported`, kept the line's `parse_allowed_tools_tool_choice` family and did not pull in main's `parse_chat_allowed_tools_tool_choice`
- `litellm/main.py`: kept the line's import of `drops_unsupported_allowed_tools_tool_choice` and `parse_allowed_tools_tool_choice`, added `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported`, which is called right after the line's `drops_unsupported_allowed_tools_tool_choice` call in `completion`
- `litellm/utils.py`: added `HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_TYPES` to the line's import list, and the condition in `validate_chat_completion_tool_choice` became `if not forces_hosted_tool and (tool_choice_type is None or tool_choice.get("function") is None)`. Main also has `tool_choice_type != "allowed_tools"` there, the line handles `allowed_tools` earlier in the same function so that clause does not exist here
- `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`: kept the line's imports and tests, added `hosted_tool_choice_type` and `raise_if_hosted_tool_choice_unsupported` plus the hosted tests
- `tests/unit/test_main.py`: kept the line's `allowed_tools` tests, appended the hosted tests. `tests/unit/test_utils.py`, the responses transformation test and `tests/integration/providers/test_hosted_tool_choice_wire.py` applied clean

Gates, all from the worktree with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/enterprise"`

- Picked tests (`test_allowed_tools_tool_choice.py`, `test_utils.py`, `test_main.py`, `test_litellm_completion_responses.py`): 1531 collected, 0 failed on the pick, 1503 collected, 0 failed on the base tip 185dc2dca6. No pass-to-fail
- Ten test files of line-only callers of the changed helpers (responses mcp handlers, agentic loop, tool_loop, azure gpt transformation, code interpreter handler, responses bridge): 280 passed on both the pick and the base
- `tests/integration/providers/test_hosted_tool_choice_wire.py` through `tests/integration/run.py providers` with `INTEGRATION_WORKERS=2` and Postgres: 4 passed on the pick, 4 failed on the base with only the test file checked out (400 "Invalid tool choice")
- `ruff check --select F821,F811` on the three changed `litellm/` files: clean. `ruff format --check` on them: clean (the repo formats with ruff, `tests/` is excluded by `ruff.toml` on the base as well). The skill's ast importer scan found no dropped name reached by any file on the line
- Mutation: emptying `HOSTED_TOOL_CHOICE_TYPES` turns 19 of the hosted tests red, restoring turns them green
- `BASE_REF=origin/litellm_backport_allowed_tools_tool_choice_lts_1_108_x make check`: the strict ruff, LIT, TQ and OA gates all report no rule grew past the merge-base. The run ends FAIL on `lint-ruff` with one F811 (duplicate `ScriptedBedrockInvoke`) in `tests/unit/llms/bedrock/messages/invoke_transformations/test_anthropic_claude3_transformation.py`, a file this PR does not touch and which is red the same way on the base tip
- grype v0.100.0 (checksum verified) on the worktree vs main: 98 rows vs 97. The only line-only finding is GHSA-w8v5-vhqr-4h9v in diskcache 5.6.3 (optional `caching` extra, state not-fixed, no fixed release exists, main no longer locks diskcache). Nothing to bump, and it predates this PR on the base branch
- gauntlet-mini: SURVIVED | degraded mode, no Agent tool, 5 lenses run by hand (conflict resolution vs main, identifiers and imports, picked tests plus mutation, line-only callers, live wire and proxy) | BASE 185dc2dca6 HEAD ff68ba4c2f | 0 verified refutations | rejected candidates: `file_search` answering 404 after the pick (the request now reaches OpenAI, which rejects the placeholder vector store id), and the `make check` lint red (pre-existing on the base)

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Two proxies, each with its own empty Postgres database and its own Redis, started with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config <config> --port <port> --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver --detailed_debug`. Before runs the base tip 185dc2dca6 on port 4100, After runs this branch at ff68ba4c2f on port 4200. Config has `gpt-5.6` as `openai/gpt-5.6` and `claude-sonnet-5-5` as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5` (newest Sonnet in the cost map), master key in `general_settings`, `router_settings.redis_host` and `redis_port` pointing at that leg's Redis. Real provider calls, real spend, no mocks

Each case is one `client.chat.completions.with_raw_response.create(model=..., messages=..., tools=..., tool_choice=...)` through the OpenAI python SDK with `base_url=http://localhost:<port>/v1`. Hosted cases use `tools=[{"type": "<hosted>"}, get_time function tool]` and the question "What is the top headline on the BBC News front page right now?". Function, required, allowed_tools and invalid cases use `tools=[get_time]` and "What time is it in Paris?". The `allowed_tools` choice is `{"type": "allowed_tools", "mode": "auto", "tools": [{"type": "function", "name": "get_time"}]}` from the #50726 proof. The `file_search` case sends `{"type": "file_search", "vector_store_ids": ["vs_does_not_exist"]}` and runs last, since its provider error puts the deployment in cooldown. Status, first line of the body and `x-litellm-response-cost` per case

| Case | Before (base tip 185dc2dca6) | After (pick) | cost before / after |
|---|---|---|---|
| web_search on gpt-5.6 | 400, litellm.BadRequestError: Invalid tool choice, tool_choice={'type': 'web_search'}. Please ensure tool_choice follows the OpenAI spec | 200, text answer with url annotations | 0 / 0.0733172 |
| web_search_preview on gpt-5.6 | 400, litellm.BadRequestError: Invalid tool choice, tool_choice={'type': 'web_search_preview'}. Please ensure tool_choice follows the OpenAI spec | 200, text answer with url annotations | 0 / 0.0415212 |
| web_search on claude-sonnet-5-5 | 400, litellm.BadRequestError: Invalid tool choice, tool_choice={'type': 'web_search'}. Please ensure tool_choice follows the OpenAI spec | 400, litellm.BadRequestError: tool_choice type 'web_search' forces an OpenAI hosted tool and is only supported for azure, litellm_proxy, openai, got custom | 0 / 0 |
| function choice on gpt-5.6 | 200, tool call get_time({"city":"Paris"}) | 200, tool call get_time({"city":"Paris"}) | 0.0005560000000000001 / 0.0005560000000000001 |
| function choice on claude-sonnet-5-5 | 400, litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: claude-sonnet-5-5 does not support forced tool use (tool_choice='required' or a named tool). issue.title: feat(rate-limit): enforce per-customer per-model tpm and rpm limits in the v3 limiter
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

enforce customer model_rpm_limit and model_tpm_limit

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer `model_tpm_limit` and `model_rpm_limit` maps (#50797) are stored but never enforced
- A customer could burn one model's allowance through many keys and replicas unchecked

How it solves it:

- New v3 limiter scope `model_per_end_user` keyed `<customer>:<model group>`
- Reads the maps already loaded on the request's customer budget
- Same Redis sliding window as every other scope, shared across keys, teams and workers
- Actual tokens settle against the same counter after the call
- Models without an entry and other customers are untouched

## User Flow

Before: a customer with a per-model TPM cap keeps getting served past it, whatever key sends the traffic

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `{"user_id": "acme", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 60}}` and gets 200 with the map on the budget
2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 again, now 60 tokens in the window
4. A third call still gets 200, the cap is never applied

After: the second key is refused once the customer's allowance for that model is spent

1. Admin sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new and gets 200
2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and gets 429 `Rate limit exceeded for model_per_end_user: acme:opus. Limit type: tokens. Current limit: 60, Remaining: 30`
4. Customer `globex` on `opus`, and `acme` on `luna` (no entry), still get 200

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10553

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [x] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, two uvicorn workers sharing one Redis (`127.0.0.1:6379`) for router state and rate-limit counters, Postgres on `127.0.0.1:5432`, mock responses so no provider spend. Env vars: `DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /home/ubuntu/qa/config2.yaml --port 4013 --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>config2.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from opus"
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"

router_settings:
  redis_host: 127.0.0.1
  redis_port: 6379

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
  coordination_redis:
    host: 127.0.0.1
    port: 6379
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>leg2.sh, the client script run against each build (`./leg2.sh 4013 <suffix>`)</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: leg2.sh <port> <suffix>
P=${1:-4013}; S=${2:-main}; H="Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"; C="Content-Type: application/json"
echo "## customer acme-$S with model_tpm_limit opus=60, customer globex-$S with none; two keys"
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:$P/customer/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d "{\"user_id\":\"acme-$S\",\"model_tpm_limit\":{\"opus\":60}}"; echo
```

## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

enforce customer model_rpm_limit and model_tpm_limit

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Customer `model_tpm_limit` and `model_rpm_limit` maps (#50797) are stored but never enforced
- A customer could burn one model's allowance through many keys and replicas unchecked

How it solves it:

- New v3 limiter scope `model_per_end_user` keyed `<customer>:<model group>`
- Reads the maps already loaded on the request's customer budget
- Same Redis sliding window as every other scope, shared across keys, teams and workers
- Actual tokens settle against the same counter after the call
- Models without an entry and other customers are untouched

Before: a customer with a per-model TPM cap keeps getting served past it, whatever key sends the traffic

1. Admin sends POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `{"user_id": "acme", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 60}}` and gets 200 with the map on the budget
2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 again, now 60 tokens in the window
4. A third call still gets 200, the cap is never applied

After: the second key is refused once the customer's allowance for that model is spent

2. Service A sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions for `opus` with `"user": "acme"` and gets 200 using 30 tokens
3. Service B sends the same request with its own key and gets 429 `Rate limit exceeded for model_per_end_user: acme:opus. Limit type: tokens. Current limit: 60, Remaining: 30`

Resolves LIT-10553

issue.title: chore(cost-map): add together_ai/elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 from the Together models API
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

[insert handwritten description here]

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Together serves elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 but the cost map has no row, so spend tracks at zero

How it solves it:

- Adds together_ai/elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 priced from GET https://api.together.ai/v1/models

## Rows

together_ai/elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 (kind api, new row)

Prices come from GET https://api.together.ai/v1/models, id `elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0`: `pricing.input = 0.6`, `pricing.output = 3`, `pricing.cached_input = 0.06` per 1M tokens, so input_cost_per_token 6e-07, output_cost_per_token 3e-06, cache_read_input_token_cost 6e-08. The same response gives `context_length: 262144`, written as max_input_tokens and max_output_tokens the way the sibling together_ai rows carry the Together context length. `type: chat` gives mode chat. Elorian's launch post https://elorian.ai/blog/introducing-glimpse states the same rates, "Input tokens cost $0.60 per million and output tokens $3.00 per million".

supports_prompt_caching true follows from the `pricing.cached_input` meter. supports_vision true and supports_reasoning true come from the Together model page https://www.together.ai/models/elorian-glimpse, which tags the model Chat, Reasoning, Vision and Video and states "Native image and video input with text output" and "Reasons in visual space, zooming into regions and returning to the visual evidence to check its interpretation before answering".

The function calling and structured output flags are left off the row. Together's function calling and structured outputs docs point at the serverless catalog table on https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless/models for the supported model list, and that table does not list glimpse-1.0 yet, so neither flag has a source. The Together model page still says "Available on dedicated endpoints; contact for pricing" while /v1/models already prices it per token, so the API is the price source and the page has not caught up.

## Changed pages checked

https://docs.together.ai/docs/changelog: the November 5 entry for moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro ($2.00 input / $10.00 output / $0.20 cached input) matches the catalog row. No other serverless price or deprecation announcement differs from the catalog. The launch entry for Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B still shows $2.50 / $6.25 / $0.50 while the catalog row carries the later /v1/models values ($2.00 / $6.00 / $0.25); that model was removed from serverless on 2026-11-04 and is no longer priced by the API, so the row is left as is.

https://docs.together.ai/docs/deprecations: every together_ai row named in the scheduled table and the Inference deprecation history table already carries the matching deprecation_date, deprecation_source and successor_model (ruling together-ai-deprecation-history-backfill, together-ai-conflicting-deprecation-dates-history-table-wins), so no backfill is needed.

## Delisted by the provider

together-ai-21.1b-41b, together-ai-4.1b-8b, together-ai-41.1b-80b, together-ai-8.1b-21b, together-ai-81.1b-110b, together-ai-embedding-151m-to-350m, together-ai-embedding-up-to-150m and together-ai-up-to-4b are generic size tier keys that /v1/models never lists by design, so they are a coverage gap and not delistings. No key is deleted.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Low

- Function calling and structured output flags omitted until Together documents them for this model

</details>

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Catalog-only JSON updates with no runtime logic; only adds pricing metadata for a new Together model.

> **Overview**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt-image-2` | `deprecation_date` | `2027-02-10` | https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations |

| `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21` | `successor_model` | `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` | first named replacement, as the `gpt-image-1` row does |

Quote from the deprecations page, section "2026-11-10: GPT Image 2": "The `gpt-image-2` model and `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21` snapshot are deprecated and will be removed from the API on February 10, 2027." Table row: "| February 10, 2027 | `gpt-image-2` \| `gpt-image-2-2026-04-21` | `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` or `gpt-image-2.6-flare` |". The page names two replacements, the row takes the first one the same way `gpt-image-1` carries `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`.

## Pages checked, no pricing difference

https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing.md (Standard, Batch, Flex, Fast, Ultrafast token tables, image, realtime and audio, transcription, specialized and fine-tuning tables) matches the catalog row for row. Every other dated row on the deprecations page already carries the same date in the catalog.

## Delisted by the provider

Not in `/v1/models` for this key, left for a human: `daybreak-blue-latest`, `daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-blue-latest`, `gpt-daybreak-red-latest`, `gpt-5.5-cyber`, `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-cyber`, `gpt-6-cyber`, `gpt-6-rosalind`, `gpt-rosalind-discovery`, `gpt-rosalind-research`, `gpt-6-astra-law`, `openai/container`, `text-embedding-ada-002-v2`, `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview`, `gpt-4o-search-preview` (the deprecations page dates only the `-2025-03-11` snapshots of the last two). issue.title: feat(budgets): add per-model tpm and rpm limit maps to budgets and customers
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add model_tpm_limit and model_rpm_limit to customers (end users)

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A customer's budget can cap tokens per minute overall, but not per model
- A per-model map sent to `/budget/new` or `/customer/new` was silently dropped
- Negative values were accepted and dropped too

How it solves it:

- `model_tpm_limit` and `model_rpm_limit` columns on `LiteLLM_BudgetTable` (schema-only migration)
- Same fields on `BudgetNewRequest` as `dict[str, NonNegativeInt]`, so a negative or fractional value is a 422
- `/budget/new`, `/budget/update`, `/budget/info`, `/budget/settings`, `/customer/new` and `/customer/info` carry them
- Auth loads a customer's maps onto `UserAPIKeyAuth.end_user_model_tpm_limit` / `end_user_model_rpm_limit`
- `CUSTOMER_ONLY_BUDGET_FIELDS` keeps the two maps out of the shared budget allowlist, so organizations, teams and projects still store them in metadata
- Enforcement in the rate limiter is a follow-up; this PR is storage and the management surface only

## User Flow

Before: an admin tries to give one customer a 400K TPM allowance on one model and the proxy accepts the request but keeps nothing

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new with `{"budget_id": "acme-tier", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 400000}}`
2. 200 comes back, but the body has no `model_tpm_limit` key at all
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `{"user_id": "acme", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 400000}}` and get 200 with `"budget_id": null`
4. They send `{"opus": -1}` by mistake and still get 200

After: the same requests store the map and hand it back, and a bad value is refused

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new and the 200 body carries `"model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 400000}`
2. POST https://litellm-domain/budget/info returns the same map for `acme-tier`
3. POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new now returns a `budget_id`, and GET https://litellm-domain/customer/info?end_user_id=acme shows the map under `litellm_budget_table`
4. `{"opus": -1}` returns 422 naming `model_tpm_limit`

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10551

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, both legs. Proxy from the repo checkout, local Postgres (`DATABASE_URL` env var), no Redis because nothing here touches shared counters. Before ran with one worker, After with two (`Started server process` twice in the log):

```
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <port> --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from opus"
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

</details>

Commands (same on both legs, `H` is the master key header, `C` is `Content-Type: application/json`):

```
curl -X POST $PROXY/budget/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"budget_id":"acme-tier","model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000},"model_rpm_limit":{"opus":200}}'
curl -X POST $PROXY/budget/info -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"budgets":["acme-tier"]}'
curl -X POST $PROXY/customer/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"user_id":"acme","model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000}}'
curl "$PROXY/customer/info?end_user_id=acme" -H "$H"
curl -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST $PROXY/budget/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"budget_id":"neg","model_tpm_limit":{"opus":-1}}'
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -At -c "select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name='LiteLLM_BudgetTable' and column_name like 'model_%'"
```

### Before (cd9f98d095)

1. `/budget/new` returns 200 with no `model_tpm_limit` or `model_rpm_limit` key in the body
2. `/budget/info` returns the budget with neither key
3. `/customer/new` returns 200 with `"budget_id": null, "litellm_budget_table": null`; `/customer/info` shows the same
4. Negative value returns `HTTP 200`
5. Columns: `model_max_budget` only

### After (94d7aa127b, unchanged in behavior by be36cedb25, which only keeps the basedpyright and ruff strict gate counts flat)

1. `/budget/new` returns 200 with `"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000},"model_rpm_limit":{"opus":200}`
2. `/budget/info` returns the same two maps
3. `/customer/new` returns a `budget_id` and `litellm_budget_table` carrying `"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000}`; `/customer/info` shows the same map
4. Negative value returns `HTTP 422`
5. Columns: `model_max_budget`, `model_rpm_limit`, `model_tpm_limit`

For the e2e-changed check: `/organization/update` with a nested `litellm_budget_table` and a top-level `budget_id` behaves as on main, since the tip restores the full budget field list on both the flatten and the strip loop.

Tests: `tests/integration/management/test_budget_model_limits.py` (4 passed against the live proxy above), `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_budget_endpoints.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_custom_auth_end_user_budget.py` and `test_new_organization_keeps_per_model_limits_in_org_metadata_not_the_budget_row` in `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_organization_endpoints.py` (org maps stay in metadata, off the budget row). Mutation: dropping the `end_user_model_tpm_limit` assignment in `_apply_budget_limits_to_end_user_params` fails `test_apply_budget_limits_copies_per_model_limits_onto_end_user_params`, and the org test fails at the first commit of this PR, where the maps leaked into the org budget row. Both green at the tip. The after leg was rerun at the tip with two workers. The new integration file first runs on main after merge, since CircleCI integration groups do not run on pull requests.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Nothing enforces the maps yet; the limiter descriptor lands in the next PR
- `/customer/update` still only accepts its own field set, so the maps change through `/budget/update`

### Low

- Organization, team and project requests keep writing `model_tpm_limit` / `model_rpm_limit` to their metadata as before; only `/budget/new`, `/budget/update` and the customer routes write the budget columns
- `/customer/new` now JSON-encodes the inline budget for the database write, which also makes inline `model_max_budget` land instead of erroring

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches budget schema migration, customer/budget APIs, and auth token fields; mis-wiring could drop or mis-apply limits, though enforcement is deferred to a follow-up.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`model_tpm_limit`** and **`model_rpm_limit`** as per-model JSON maps on budgets (new DB columns + Prisma/Pydantic/OpenAPI), with **non-negative integer validation** on create/update.
> 
> **Budget** and **customer** management APIs now **persist and return** these maps; inline customer creation stores them on the linked budget row (with JSON encoding for Prisma). **Auth** propagates them to `UserAPIKeyAuth` (`end_user_model_*`) from customer budgets and defaults, matching existing end-user limit wiring.
> 
> **`CUSTOMER_ONLY_BUDGET_FIELDS`** keeps the new maps off organization budget writes so org **metadata** behavior stays unchanged. Tests cover persistence, customer flows, validation, and auth propagation. **Rate-limit enforcement is not in this PR**—storage and management surface only.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d26174678782332e2912081ec3d03750b89b02ab. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

issue.title: fix(transcription): stop billing a FLAC with no sample count as 576 trillion seconds
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description A FLAC encoded to a pipe has no length in its header, the audio library reports that as 9223372036854775807 frames, and LiteLLM billed it as 576 trillion seconds ($43B per request, key locked out). This PR handles that edge case
Details ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A FLAC encoded to a pipe has no sample count in its header - libsndfile reports `INT64_MAX` frames for it, so the measured duration is 576,460,752,303,423.5 s at 16 kHz - One `gpt-transcribe` request then bills $43,234,556,422.76 and locks the key out of its budget - On `main` this hits responses with no `usage` (`response_format=text`), on v1.106.6 it also hits `json` How it solves it: - `calculate_request_duration` returns `None` when the frame count is `INT64_MAX` - The Amazon Transcribe passthrough's `media_file_seconds` does the same ## User Flow Before: a developer who transcribes a FLAC that was encoded to a pipe is billed about $43 billion for one request, and the key stops working 1. They run `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`, which writes a FLAC with no sample count in its header 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `response_format=text` and `piped.flac`, and get 200 with the transcript 3. The response carries `x-litellm-response-cost: 43234556422.75676` and the key's spend jumps to the same amount against its $500 budget 4. Their next POST on that key, with any file, returns 422 `Budget has been exceeded! ... Current cost: 43234556422.75676, Max budget: 500.0` After: the same request is not billed for a length nobody measured, and the key keeps working 1. They run `ffmpeg -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac`, which writes a FLAC with no sample count in its header 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/transcriptions with `model=gpt-transcribe`, `response_format=text` and `piped.flac`, and get 200 with the transcript 3. The response carries no `x-litellm-response-cost` header and the key's spend stays at $0 for that request 4. Their next POST on that key with `normal.flac` returns 200 and bills $0.00089 for 11.85 s of audio ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-10595 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more - [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both legs ran against a live proxy with real `openai/gpt-transcribe` calls, Postgres, one dedicated Redis and two workers. Each leg had its own empty database and both shared the Redis on port 6390. The proxy logged two `Started server process` lines on each leg. Proxy start command, run from a checkout of each commit, on port 4111 for Before and 4112 for After. Env vars set were `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL` and `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`. ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa_config.yaml --port 4111 --num_workers 2 --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver ``` `qa_config.yaml` ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-transcribe litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-transcribe api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY router_settings: redis_host: 127.0.0.1 redis_port: 6390 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY coordination_redis: host: 127.0.0.1 port: 6390 ```
repro.sh, run as ./repro.sh <port> <database_url> ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # usage: OPENAI_API_KEY=... LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=... ./repro.sh PORT=$1; DB=$2; B=http://localhost:$PORT; ALIAS=flac-$PORT-$(date +%s) q() { psql "$DB" -Atc "$1"; } transcribe() { curl -s -D /tmp/h.txt -o /tmp/b.txt -w "$1 http=%{http_code}" $B/v1/audio/transcriptions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -F model=gpt-transcribe -F response_format=text -F file=@$2 echo " x-litellm-response-cost=$(grep -i '^x-litellm-response-cost:' /tmp/h.txt | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}')" head -c 170 /tmp/b.txt; echo } [ -f normal.flac ] || { curl -s https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts", "voice": "alloy", "response_format": "wav", "input": "Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal."}' -o tts.wav ffmpeg -v error -y -i tts.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 normal.flac; } ffmpeg -v error -y -i normal.flac -f flac - > piped.flac echo "normal.flac $(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 normal.flac)s, piped.flac $(ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 piped.flac)" KEY=$(curl -s $B/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"max_budget\": 500, \"models\": [\"gpt-transcribe\"], \"key_alias\": \"$ALIAS\"}" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])') echo "litellm $(curl -s -D - -o /dev/null $B/health/liveliness | grep -i '^x-litellm-version' | tr -d '\r' | awk '{print $2}'), key max_budget=500" transcribe "1. piped.flac" piped.flac for i in $(seq 1 30); do [ "$(q "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" s join \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" k on k.token = s.api_key where k.key_alias = '$ALIAS'")" -ge 1 ] && break; sleep 3; done sleep 8 transcribe "2. normal.flac, same key" normal.flac sleep 25 echo "LiteLLM_SpendLogs (status|spend):" q "select s.status, s.spend from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" s join \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" k on k.token = s.api_key where k.key_alias = '$ALIAS' order by s.\"startTime\"" echo "LiteLLM_VerificationToken spend|max_budget: $(q "select spend, max_budget from \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" where key_alias = '$ALIAS'")" ```
### Before (fe6cf07cc8) 1. `./repro.sh 4111 $DATABASE_URL` ```text normal.flac 11.850000s, piped.flac N/A litellm , key max_budget=500 1. piped.flac http=200 x-litellm-response-cost=43234556422.75676 {"text":"Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are 2. normal.flac, same key http=422 x-litellm-response-cost= {"error":{"message":"Budget has been exceeded! Key=flac-4111-1794289251 (sk-...lh1g) Current cost: 43234556422.75676, Max budget: 500.0","type":"budget_exceeded","param": LiteLLM_SpendLogs (status|spend): success|43234556422.75676 failure|0 LiteLLM_VerificationToken spend|max_budget: 43234556422.75676|500 ``` ### After (eb0f251b47) 1. `./repro.sh 4112 $DATABASE_URL` ```text normal.flac 11.850000s, piped.flac N/A litellm , key max_budget=500 1. piped.flac http=200 x-litellm-response-cost= {"text":"Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are 2. normal.flac, same key http=200 x-litellm-response-cost=0.0008887499999999999 {"text":"Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are LiteLLM_SpendLogs (status|spend): success|0 success|0.0008887499999999999 LiteLLM_VerificationToken spend|max_budget: 0.0008887499999999999|500 ``` The same piped FLAC on a v1.106.6 proxy billed `43234556422.75676` for both `response_format=json` and `response_format=text`. On `main` the `json` response already bills from the provider's `usage.seconds`, so only responses with no `usage` were still wrong. echo } [ -f normal.flac ] || { curl -s https://api.openai.com/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model": "gpt-4o-mini-tts", "voice": "alloy", "response_format": "wav", "input": "Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal."}' -o tts.wav ffmpeg -v error -y -i tts.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 normal.flac; do [ "$(q "select count(*) from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" s join \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" k on k.token = s.api_key where k.key_alias = '$ALIAS'")" -ge 1 ] && break; sleep 3; done sleep 8 transcribe "2. normal.flac, same key" normal.flac sleep 25 echo "LiteLLM_SpendLogs (status|spend):" q "select s.status, s.spend from \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" s join \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" k on k.token = s.api_key where k.key_alias = '$ALIAS' order by s.\"startTime\"" echo "LiteLLM_VerificationToken spend|max_budget: $(q "select spend, max_budget from \"LiteLLM_VerificationToken\" where key_alias = '$ALIAS'")" ```

Key=flac-4111-1794289251 (sk-...lh1g) Current cost: 43234556422.75676, Max budget: 500.0","type":"budget_exceeded","param": LiteLLM_SpendLogs (status|spend): success|43234556422.75676 failure|0 LiteLLM_VerificationToken spend|max_budget: 43234556422.75676|500 ``` ### After (eb0f251b47) 1. `./repro.sh 4112 $DATABASE_URL` ```text normal.flac 11.850000s, piped.flac N/A litellm , key max_budget=500 1. piped.flac http=200 x-litellm-response-cost= {"text":"Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are 2. normal.flac, same key http=200 x-litellm-response-cost=0.0008887499999999999 {"text":"Four score and seven years ago, our fathers brought forth on this continent a new nation, conceived in liberty and dedicated to the proposition that all men are LiteLLM_SpendLogs (status|spend): success|0 success|0.0008887499999999999 LiteLLM_VerificationToken spend|max_budget: 0.0008887499999999999|500 ``` The same piped FLAC on a v1.106.6 proxy billed `43234556422.75676` for both `response_format=json` and `response_format=text`. issue.title: feat(changelog): filter /changelog.xml by kind and providers and point the page's RSS link at the current view
issue.body:
## Summary

A subscriber to `/changelog.xml` today gets every update for every provider (about 1,900 items over 30 days). A customer who keeps their own cost map asked to be told only about price changes for the providers they use, so the feed now takes a query string and the page's RSS link carries whatever is selected.

`/changelog.xml?kind=price&providers=bedrock,openai,databricks` is rebuilt per request in `middleware.ts` from the same `/changelog.json` the page reads, through `feedFilter(searchParams)` and `filterChangelogItems(items, filter)` in `src/changelogPresentation.ts`. Both params are comma lists matched against `item.kind` and `item.provider` (the `litellm_provider` id), unknown values match nothing, and an empty providers list means no filter. An empty `kind` keeps the page's default view, every kind except `metadata`, so the static feed is built through the same `filterChangelogItems` and `?kind=metadata` returns what the "Other changes" tab shows. The `atom:link rel="self"` points at the filtered URL. A request with no `kind` or `providers`, or one where `/changelog.json` cannot be read, falls through to the static file as before, so the unfiltered feed is unchanged.

Against today's live data, `?kind=price` is 481 items, `?providers=bedrock,openai,databricks` 350 and the two together 136.

On the Changelog page the "RSS feed" link becomes `` href={`/changelog.xml${feedQuery(category, provider)}`} ``, so the Prices tab plus a provider gives `?kind=price&providers=<id>`, and the label reads "RSS feed for this view" when a filter is on. Search is page only and is not carried into the feed.

Tracking: filtered fetches are still reported from the middleware as "Feed Fetched" with `kind` and `providers` arrays as properties, and the link click sends "Changelog Feed Link Clicked" with the same two values.

Tests cover the query parsing and filtering (including the metadata default), the self link, and the middleware path end to end (filtered response, headers, Mixpanel properties, fall through for no filter and for unrelated params such as `utm_source`).

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f62bb16ea5c544bc85abb338dd9988f4
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/f62bb16ea5c544bc85abb338dd9988f4?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Adds optional query-param behavior on an existing feed with static fallback; no auth or data-mutation paths touched.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Filtered changelog RSS** lets subscribers narrow `/changelog.xml` with `?kind=` and `?providers=` (comma-separated). **Middleware** rebuilds the feed per request from `/changelog.json` when those filters are present; unfiltered URLs and failed JSON loads still serve the static file. Filtered RSS uses the request URL for `atom:link rel="self"`.
> 
> Shared helpers in `changelogPresentation.ts` (`feedFilter`, `filterChangelogItems`, `feedQuery`) power the build script’s default feed (all kinds except `metadata`), the dynamic middleware path, and the Changelog UI RSS link, which now reflects the selected category/provider and tracks clicks. **Mixpanel** “Feed Fetched” events include `kind` and `providers` when filters apply.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b3fbda7cccd644b5480de88be912c57fcdf23879. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Together serves elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 but the cost map has no row, so spend tracks at zero

How it solves it:

together_ai/elorian-labs/glimpse-1.0 (kind api, new row)

The same response gives `context_length: 262144`, written as max_input_tokens and max_output_tokens the way the sibling together_ai rows carry the Together context length. `type: chat` gives mode chat. Elorian's launch post https://elorian.ai/blog/introducing-glimpse states the same rates, "Input tokens cost $0.60 per million and output tokens $3.00 per million".

supports_prompt_caching true follows from the `pricing.cached_input` meter. supports_vision true and supports_reasoning true come from the Together model page https://www.together.ai/models/elorian-glimpse, which tags the model Chat, Reasoning, Vision and Video and states "Native image and video input with text output" and "Reasons in visual space, zooming into regions and returning to the visual evidence to check its interpretation before answering".

The function calling and structured output flags are left off the row. Together's function calling and structured outputs docs point at the serverless catalog table on https://docs.together.ai/docs/serverless/models for the supported model list, and that table does not list glimpse-1.0 yet, so neither flag has a source. The Together model page still says "Available on dedicated endpoints; contact for pricing" while /v1/models already prices it per token, so the API is the price source and the page has not caught up.

issue.title: fix(prometheus): record litellm_overhead_latency_metric for streams, stamp plus the proxy's first-chunk work
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

On a streamed request the gateway's overhead number was measured once, when the provider handed back the stream object, and it never made it into `litellm_overhead_latency_metric` at all because the response assembled from the chunks does not carry it. This PR keeps that number on the logging object so the metric is recorded for streams on `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`, and adds the time the gateway itself spends on the first chunk (the per-chunk hook, `usage.cost` injection, serialization) on top of it, since that is the delay every chunk the client sees inherits. Work on later chunks is deliberately not summed, a 1 ms hook on 500 chunks delays the client by 1 ms, not 500 ms. The `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms` header is unchanged because it is sent before any chunk goes out.

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Streamed requests emitted no `litellm_overhead_latency_metric` sample at all
- The stamped overhead ends when the stream object comes back, before any chunk work
- So `include_cost_in_streaming_usage` on vs off looked identical in Prometheus
- `/v1/responses` streams wiped the stamp again at stream end

How it solves it:

- `update_response_metadata` also keeps a stream wrapper's timing on the logging object
- `async_streaming_data_generator` (/v1/messages) and `async_data_generator` (chat and /v1/responses) time the proxy's work between receiving the first chunk and yielding it, kept as `Logging.first_chunk_overhead_ms`
- `get_standard_logging_object_payload` adds that one chunk's work to the stamped `litellm_overhead_time_ms`, later chunks are not summed
- A keepalive ping sent before provider output does not count as the first chunk
- The `/v1/responses` stream-end metadata update keeps the handoff stamp instead of dropping it
- `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms` keeps its meaning, the header goes out before the chunks

## User Flow

Before: an operator turns on `include_cost_in_streaming_usage` and cannot see what it costs in latency

1. They set `litellm_settings.include_cost_in_streaming_usage: true` and `callbacks: ["prometheus"]` and restart the proxy
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true` and get the stream back with `usage.cost` on the last `message_delta` (same for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`)
3. They open https://litellm-domain/metrics/ and find `litellm_request_total_latency_metric` for the call but no `litellm_overhead_latency_metric` sample at all, with the flag on or off

After: the same request shows up in the overhead metric, and the flag's work on the first chunk is in the number

1. They set the same config and restart the proxy
2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"stream": true`
3. https://litellm-domain/metrics/ now has a `litellm_overhead_latency_metric` sample for the call, equal to the `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms` header plus the time the proxy spent on the first chunk, the delay every later chunk inherits

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup: one proxy per leg, no database, `callbacks: ["prometheus"]`, one Anthropic deployment `claude-haiku-4-5`, `--num_workers 1`. Each leg sends three streamed POST /v1/messages and three streamed POST /v1/chat/completions (`stream_options.include_usage: true`) asking for 40 numbers (23 to 26 SSE chunks each), records the `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms` header per request, then reads GET /metrics/ four seconds later. The first request of every leg is a cold start, which is why its header is ~150 to 350 ms.

### Before (f52e5057f9)

#### include_cost_in_streaming_usage: true

1. Headers, messages #1 to #3: `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms: 146.0149`, `5.9521`, `5.6479`. Chat #1 to #3: `8.2681`, `6.3262`, `5.764`. Last `message_delta` carries `"cost": 0.000436`
2. GET /metrics/:
   ```
   litellm_request_total_latency_metric_count 6.0
   litellm_request_total_latency_metric_sum 5.517748193908692
   ```
   No `litellm_overhead_latency_metric_count` or `_sum` series exists, only the `# HELP` and `# TYPE` lines

1. Headers. /v1/messages #1 to #3: `x-litellm-overhead-duration-ms: 161.9601`, `38.707`, `131.408` (total 332.08 ms, 26 to 27 frames each). /v1/chat/completions: `39.6891`, `16.463`, `15.7068` (total 71.86 ms, 23 frames). /v1/responses: `20.2689`, `14.7431`, `32.932` (total 67.94 ms, 38 frames)

   ```
   litellm_overhead_latency_metric_count{model_group="haiku-chat"} 3.0

   litellm_overhead_latency_metric_sum{model_group="gpt-5.4-mini"} 0.0719862
   ```
   /v1/messages: 334.83 ms in the metric against 332.08 ms in the headers, so 2.75 ms of first-chunk work across three streams (about 0.9 ms each). /v1/chat/completions: 72.96 against 71.86, 1.10 ms (about 0.4 ms each). /v1/responses: 71.99 against 67.94, 4.04 ms (about 1.3 ms each). With the earlier sum-over-chunks design the same three /v1/responses streams added 13.29 ms, so the metric no longer grows with the chunk count

Unit tests at 3bba741b3c: `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/llm_response_utils/test_response_metadata.py`, `tests/unit/responses/test_streaming_iterator.py`, `tests/unit/litellm_core_utils/test_litellm_logging.py -k overhead`, `tests/unit/proxy/test_common_request_processing.py -k "first_chunk or FastPath"`, `tests/unit/proxy/test_proxy_server_endpoints_and_startup.py -k "first_chunk or async_data_generator"`, 60 passed. - On a raw SSE passthrough chat stream the chat loop yields frames mid-iteration, so the send time of the first frame lands in the first-chunk number
- Datadog and OTel read the same `litellm_overhead_time_ms`, so their stream overhead grows by the same first-chunk amount

issue.title: feat(budgets): add per-model tpm and rpm limit maps to budgets and customers
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

add model_tpm_limit and model_rpm_limit to customers (end users)

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- A customer's budget can cap tokens per minute overall, but not per model
- A per-model map sent to `/budget/new` or `/customer/new` was silently dropped
- Negative values were accepted and dropped too

How it solves it:

- `model_tpm_limit` and `model_rpm_limit` columns on `LiteLLM_BudgetTable` (schema-only migration)
- Same fields on `BudgetNewRequest` as `dict[str, NonNegativeInt]`, so a negative or fractional value is a 422
- `/budget/new`, `/budget/update`, `/budget/info`, `/budget/settings`, `/customer/new` and `/customer/info` carry them
- Auth loads a customer's maps onto `UserAPIKeyAuth.end_user_model_tpm_limit` / `end_user_model_rpm_limit`
- `CUSTOMER_ONLY_BUDGET_FIELDS` keeps the two maps out of the shared budget allowlist, so organizations, teams and projects still store them in metadata
- Enforcement in the rate limiter is a follow-up; this PR is storage and the management surface only

## User Flow

Before: an admin tries to give one customer a 400K TPM allowance on one model and the proxy accepts the request but keeps nothing

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new with `{"budget_id": "acme-tier", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 400000}}`
2. 200 comes back, but the body has no `model_tpm_limit` key at all
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new with `{"user_id": "acme", "model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 400000}}` and get 200 with `"budget_id": null`
4. They send `{"opus": -1}` by mistake and still get 200

After: the same requests store the map and hand it back, and a bad value is refused

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/budget/new and the 200 body carries `"model_tpm_limit": {"opus": 400000}`
2. POST https://litellm-domain/budget/info returns the same map for `acme-tier`
3. POST https://litellm-domain/customer/new now returns a `budget_id`, and GET https://litellm-domain/customer/info?end_user_id=acme shows the map under `litellm_budget_table`
4. `{"opus": -1}` returns 422 naming `model_tpm_limit`

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-10551

## Pre-Submission checklist

**Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR**

- [x] I have added meaningful tests
- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more
- [ ] My PR passes all required CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, schema.d.ts sync check, etc.)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] Every automated review on my PR's latest commit has finished, and I have addressed or replied to each of its findings before requesting a maintainer review

## Delays in PR merge?

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA).

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Shared setup, both legs. Proxy from the repo checkout, local Postgres (`DATABASE_URL` env var), no Redis because nothing here touches shared counters. Before ran with one worker, After with two (`Started server process` twice in the log):

```
.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port <port> --num_workers 2 --use_v2_migration_resolver
```

<details>
<summary>config.yaml</summary>

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: opus
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from opus"
  - model_name: luna
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_key: fake-key
      mock_response: "hello from luna"

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

</details>

Commands (same on both legs, `H` is the master key header, `C` is `Content-Type: application/json`):

```
curl -X POST $PROXY/budget/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"budget_id":"acme-tier","model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000},"model_rpm_limit":{"opus":200}}'
curl -X POST $PROXY/budget/info -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"budgets":["acme-tier"]}'
curl -X POST $PROXY/customer/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"user_id":"acme","model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000}}'
curl "$PROXY/customer/info?end_user_id=acme" -H "$H"
curl -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST $PROXY/budget/new -H "$H" -H "$C" -d '{"budget_id":"neg","model_tpm_limit":{"opus":-1}}'
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -At -c "select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name='LiteLLM_BudgetTable' and column_name like 'model_%'"
```

### Before (cd9f98d095)

1. `/budget/new` returns 200 with no `model_tpm_limit` or `model_rpm_limit` key in the body
2. `/budget/info` returns the budget with neither key
3. `/customer/new` returns 200 with `"budget_id": null, "litellm_budget_table": null`; `/customer/info` shows the same
4. Negative value returns `HTTP 200`
5. Columns: `model_max_budget` only

### After (94d7aa127b, unchanged in behavior by be36cedb25, which only keeps the basedpyright and ruff strict gate counts flat)

1. `/budget/new` returns 200 with `"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000},"model_rpm_limit":{"opus":200}`
2. `/budget/info` returns the same two maps
3. `/customer/new` returns a `budget_id` and `litellm_budget_table` carrying `"model_tpm_limit":{"opus":400000}`; `/customer/info` shows the same map
4. Negative value returns `HTTP 422`
5. Columns: `model_max_budget`, `model_rpm_limit`, `model_tpm_limit`

For the e2e-changed check: `/organization/update` with a nested `litellm_budget_table` and a top-level `budget_id` behaves as on main, since the tip restores the full budget field list on both the flatten and the strip loop.

Tests: `tests/integration/management/test_budget_model_limits.py` (4 passed against the live proxy above), `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_budget_endpoints.py`, `tests/unit/proxy/auth/test_custom_auth_end_user_budget.py` and `test_new_organization_keeps_per_model_limits_in_org_metadata_not_the_budget_row` in `tests/unit/proxy/management_endpoints/test_organization_endpoints.py` (org maps stay in metadata, off the budget row). Mutation: dropping the `end_user_model_tpm_limit` assignment in `_apply_budget_limits_to_end_user_params` fails `test_apply_budget_limits_copies_per_model_limits_onto_end_user_params`, and the org test fails at the first commit of this PR, where the maps leaked into the org budget row. Both green at the tip. The after leg was rerun at the tip with two workers. The new integration file first runs on main after merge, since CircleCI integration groups do not run on pull requests.

## Type

🆕 New Feature

## Caveats (if any)

### Medium

- Nothing enforces the maps yet; the limiter descriptor lands in the next PR
- `/customer/update` still only accepts its own field set, so the maps change through `/budget/update`

### Low

- Organization, team and project requests keep writing `model_tpm_limit` / `model_rpm_limit` to their metadata as before; only `/budget/new`, `/budget/update` and the customer routes write the budget columns
- `/customer/new` now JSON-encodes the inline budget for the database write, which also makes inline `model_max_budget` land instead of erroring

## Final Attestation

- [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

</details>

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8
Open in Devin Desktop: https://app.devin.ai/desktop/session/d8fcbc92d0ee46eaa2eee7274baed9d8?variant=devin
Requested by: @kerry-berri


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches budget schema migration, customer/budget APIs, and auth token fields; mis-wiring could drop or mis-apply limits, though enforcement is deferred to a follow-up.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`model_tpm_limit`** and **`model_rpm_limit`** as per-model JSON maps on budgets (new DB columns + Prisma/Pydantic/OpenAPI), with **non-negative integer validation** on create/update.
> 
> **Budget** and **customer** management APIs now **persist and return** these maps; inline customer creation stores them on the linked budget row (with JSON encoding for Prisma). **Auth** propagates them to `UserAPIKeyAuth` (`end_user_model_*`) from customer budgets and defaults, matching existing end-user limit wiring.
> 
> **`CUSTOMER_ONLY_BUDGET_FIELDS`** keeps the new maps off organization budget writes so org **metadata** behavior stays unchanged. Tests cover persistence, customer flows, validation, and auth propagation. **Rate-limit enforcement is not in this PR**—storage and management surface only.
>

## Summary

Adds the `github_copilot/claude-fable-5.2` row. GitHub announced Claude Fable 5.2 in Copilot on 2026-11-09 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-09-claude-fable-5-2-in-github-copilot) and the models-and-pricing table now carries its prices. The other 29 priced Copilot rows in that table match the catalog to the digit, and model-release-status.yml lists every catalog row as GA, so no deprecation changes.

## github_copilot/claude-fable-5.2 (kind api)

Prices come from `prices github-copilot`, which reads https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/data/tables/copilot/models-and-pricing.yml. The table entry is

```
- model: Claude Fable 5.2
  provider: anthropic
  release_status: GA
  category: Powerful
  input: $8.00
  cached_input: $0.20
  output: $40.00
  cache_write: $10.00
```

so `input_cost_per_token` 0.000008, `cache_read_input_token_cost` 0.0000002, `output_cost_per_token` 0.00004 and `cache_creation_input_token_cost` 0.00001. The changelog post says "This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing", and these match the first-party `claude-fable-5-2` row.

Release status: model-release-status.yml has `name: 'Claude Fable 5.2' ... release_status: 'GA'`, so no `deprecation_date`.

`max_input_tokens` 200000, `max_output_tokens` 64000, `supported_endpoints` and every `supports_*` flag are `inherited_from: github_copilot/claude-fable-5.1`. Copilot publishes no token limits for the model. Its supported-models page lists Claude Fable 5.2 under "1 million token context window" as an opt-in extended context in VS Code and Copilot CLI only, so the row keeps the sibling default like the Fable 5 and 5.1 rows do.

## Rulings applied

github-copilot-claude-sonnet-4-leave-out: `github_copilot/claude-sonnet-4` is still priced in the table and stays out of the catalog.

## Pages checked without a pricing difference

https://github.blog/changelog/label/copilot/feed/ (only the Fable 5.2 launch touches models or prices), model-release-status.yml (all GA), models-and-pricing.yml (29 other rows match), model-deprecation-history.yml (every dated retirement already in the catalog or covered by a ruling).

issue.title: feat(usage): split customer spend by the key's current team
issue.body:
## Handwritten 1-3 sentence description

added the functionality of being able to view cost spent on a customer by individual teams

<details>
<summary>Details</summary>

## TLDR

Problem this solves:

- Same customer ID sent from two teams shows one combined spend
- Admins cannot see or filter customer spend per team

How it solves it:

- Customer usage responses add a `teams` breakdown per day
- New `team_ids` filter on customer usage routes
- Usage page customer view adds a Spend by team table
- Team comes from each key's current team, no schema change

Intentional product change: the customer view on the Usage page gets a new Spend by team table under Provider Usage.

## User Flow

Before: an admin whose two teams both send `user@example.com` as the customer ID sees one combined total and cannot split it by team

1. Team A and team B each send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with header `x-litellm-end-user: user@example.com`
2. The admin calls GET http://localhost:4000/customer/daily/activity?end_user_ids=user@example.com and gets one total with no per-team split
3. Adding `&team_ids=<team A id>` is ignored and still returns both teams' spend
4. http://localhost:3000/ui/usage?view=customer&customer=user%40example.com shows customer totals, keys, models and providers, nothing per team

After: the same admin sees each team's share of that customer's spend and can filter to one team

1. Team A and team B each send the same request with `x-litellm-end-user: user@example.com`
2. GET /customer/daily/activity?end_user_ids=user@example.com returns `breakdown.teams` with one entry per team, alias included, summing to the total
3. Adding `&team_ids=<team A id>` returns only team A's spend, requests and tokens
4. The Usage page customer view shows a Spend by team table with team A and team B rows

Before and after screenshots of this page are attached in the Devin session linked below. Before has no Spend by team table, after shows team-a and team-b rows with 1 request and 25 tokens each.

## Linear ticket

Resolves LIT-9055

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] The handful of test files covering my change pass locally, e.g. `uv run pytest tests/unit/<your_test_file>.py -v`. Leave the suites (`make test-unit-*`, `make test-unit`) to CI: it finishes in ~15 minutes where a laptop takes an hour or more

## Screenshots / Proof of Fix

Live proxy on each revision with 2 workers sharing one Redis, Postgres, and real Anthropic calls to `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`. Each run made two teams (`team-a`, `team-b`) with one key each, and sent one chat request per key with the same `x-litellm-end-user`. Each run used its own customer ID so the runs do not mix. Env vars are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`.

```python
import datetime

import time

import httpx

root = Path('/home/ubuntu/stupid-scratch/proof')
phase = sys.argv[1]
master = (root / '.master').read_text()
customer = 'lit9055-' + phase + '@example.com'
date = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).date().isoformat()
log = []
with httpx.Client(base_url='http://127.0.0.1:4000', timeout=120) as client:
    for _ in range(120):
        try:
            if client.get('/health/liveliness').status_code == 200:
                break
        except httpx.TransportError:
            pass
        time.sleep(1)

    def call(path, body=None, key=None, headers=None, params=None):
        method = 'GET' if body is None else 'POST'
        response = client.request(method, path, json=body, params=params,
            headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + (key or master), **(headers or {})})
        response.raise_for_status()
        value = response.json()
        if path == '/key/generate':
```
